children.translated_text: First I bow to <s>Harihara</s>, whose auspicious face is adorned with a digit of the moon, a treasury of blessedness and worshiped by seers,
whose nature consists in generation, preservation, and dissolution.
I also bow day after day to <s>Śāradā</s>, wearing garments white as night-lilies and jasmine and adorned with a pure pearl necklace,

children.text: sakalasiddhagaṇair api sevitāmaharahaḥ praṇamāmi ca śāradām ||
children.translated_text: who is served even by all the hosts of perfected beings.
First I bow to <s>Gaṇapati</s>, elephant-faced, radiant like a mass of cloud, three-eyed, four-armed, and small in stature,
with a crest beautifully adorned with gold and jewels.
The abode of <s>Giriśa</s> is always great and wondrous, supreme, and destructive of every disease,
skilled in the whole host of attainments, remover of the sins of those who bow, and carrying one across worldly existence.
First I describe, just as it truly is, the origin of <s>pārada</s> (mercury);

children.text: tataḥ śodhanakaṃ tasya tathāṣṭādaśa karma ca ||
children.translated_text: then its purification and likewise its eighteen operations.
I shall describe the fourfold knowledge of binding, and the reduction of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) to ash,
as well as the purification of metals, their incineration, and the account of their qualities.

children.text: aṣṭau mahārasāḥ samyak procyante 'tra mayā khalu
children.translated_text: The eight <s>mahārasa</s> substances (chief minerals) are properly set forth here by me,
and likewise the qualities, purification, and incineration of the <s>uparasa</s> substances (secondary minerals).
I shall describe in detail the dripping of molten essence for all of them,
and the merits and faults of jewels, together with their purification and incineration.
In regard to mercury, there are <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrating activation), <s>rañjana</s> (coloring), and the combining of melts;
and I describe hundreds of <s>rasa</s> formulations in full detail.
Four divisions of medicinal plants are also stated:
divine medicines, mineral medicines, perfected medicines, and, beyond these, another class.

children.text: mahauṣadhya iti proktā yaṃtrāṇyatha puṭāni ca
children.translated_text: These are called great medicines; then come the instruments and the heating procedures,
as well as crucibles and, in brief, the marvels of metals.
Aphrodisiac formulas and those that restrain semen
have been arranged in this treatise without excessive brevity or excessive expansion.
In the western region from the <s>Himālaya</s> there is a lovely mountain named <s>Girīndra</s>;
near it, in a perfectly round well, this very lord of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) dwells visibly.
A maiden endowed with beauty and virtue, adorned and mounted on an excellent vehicle,

children.text: tatrāgatā kūpamavekṣamāṇā nivartitā sā mahatā javena ||
children.translated_text: came there, looked at the well, and turned back with great speed.

children.text: pradhāvitaḥ sūtavaraścaturṣu kakupsu bhūmau patito hi nūnam ||
children.translated_text: The excellent mercury rushed forth and surely fell upon the earth in the four quarters.
All around that mountain, the field of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) is said to extend twelve yojanas,

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ ca suvṛttaṃ hi sūtakasya samīritam ||
children.translated_text: broad and perfectly circular.

children.text: tanmṛdaḥ pātane yaṃtre pātitaḥ khalu rogahā
children.translated_text: When soil from there is distilled in a <s>pātana</s> apparatus, it becomes disease-destroying,
bright and directly manifest; it is itself called <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
The <s>sūta</s> (mercury) that emerged from the well went into the four directions;

children.text: kṣatriyo vaiśyaśūdrau ca caturṇāṃ jāyate khalu ||
children.translated_text: indeed it becomes of the four classes: brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra.

children.text: śvetā kṛṣṇā tathā pītā raktā vai jāyate chaviḥ
children.translated_text: Its hue becomes white, black, yellow, and red,

children.text: prācyāṃ yāmyāṃ pratīcyāṃ ca kauberyāṃ ca diśi kramāt ||
children.translated_text: respectively in the eastern, southern, western, and northern directions.
White mercury is suited to the white procedure, and black mercury makes the body firm;
yellow-colored mercury makes gold, and red mercury destroys disease.
When all are combined into one, they always accomplish every purpose;
when used, they destroy all diseases and bring about all attainments.

children.text: itthaṃ sūtodbhavaṃ jñātvā na rogaivārdhyate khalu
children.translated_text: Having thus learned the arising of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), disease certainly does not increase;
when it has been purified, incinerated, activated, and made to flow, it is auspicious.
<s>Svedana</s> (sweating), <s>mardana</s> (grinding), <s>mūrcchana</s> (stupefaction), and then raising,
<s>pātana</s> (distillation), <s>rodhana</s> (restraining), proper regulation, and kindling,
then the feeding and measured processing of mica in due sequence,
internal liquefaction, external liquefaction, and also what is called digestion,

children.text: sāraṇaṃ krāmaṇaṃ proktaṃ vedhakarma ca raṃjanam
children.translated_text: <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing), <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrating activation), the piercing operation, and coloring are taught;
then the use of <s>pārada</s> (mercury): these are precisely the eighteen operations
whose names I have stated here only in outline.
Five faults of mercuries have been declared by the best physicians:

children.text: malo viṣaṃ tathā vahnirmado darpaśca vai kramāt
children.translated_text: impurity, poison, fire, intoxication, and arrogance, in that order;

children.text: mūrcchāṃ mṛtyuṃ madaṃ caiva sphoṭaṃ kuryuḥ śirobhramam ||
children.translated_text: they cause fainting, death, intoxication, eruptions, and dizziness.
I shall explain accurately the seven sheaths of <s>sūta</s> (mercury);
I tell their names according to the <s>Devīśāstra</s>.
Born from earth, rock, water, copper, iron, lead, and tin,
there are seven sheaths in <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), and they are like poisons.

children.text: dvādaśaiva hi doṣāḥ syuryaiśca niṣkāsitā dvijaiḥ
children.translated_text: There are indeed twelve faults; when twice-born practitioners have expelled them,
they attain mastery of <s>rasa</s> (mercurial alchemy), while others are like <s>Yama</s>.
Therefore excellent physicians must remove the faults.

children.text: tatra svedanakaṃ kuryād yathāvacca śubhe dine
children.translated_text: There one should perform the sweating operation properly on an auspicious day;
the sweating of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should be done in a swing apparatus with boluses.

children.text: kṣārau cāmlena sahitau tathā ca paṭupaṃcakam
children.translated_text: The two alkalis together with an acid, and likewise the group of five salts,
the three pungents, the three myrobalans, and citraka as well,
flower-vitriol and <s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> alum: one should grind all these,
the medicines in equal parts, in a quantity equal to one eighth of the mercury.

children.text: kṛtvāndhamūṣāṃ teṣāṃ tu tanmadhye pāradaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: After making a closed crucible from them, one should place the mercury in its middle;
one should wrap it in a very good cloth and in birch bark, in three layers.

children.text: guṇena kāṣṭhakhaṇḍe vai baddhāṃ tu rasapoṭalīm
children.translated_text: With a cord, one should tie the mercury packet to a piece of wood,
so that it hangs down in a vessel filled with husk-water.
One should sweat it properly for three days; that is called <s>svedana</s> (sweating).

children.text: atha mardanakaṃ karma yena śuddhatamo rasaḥ
children.translated_text: Now comes the grinding operation, by which <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes most pure.
It is produced; I shall tell it at length exactly as it is.

children.text: khalve vimardayetsūtaṃ dināni trīṇi caiva hi
children.translated_text: One should thoroughly grind <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in a mortar for three full days.

children.text: atha khalvapramāṇaṃ hi vakṣye tatra mayādhunā ||
children.translated_text: Now, in this connection, I shall state the proper measure of the mortar.
Its length should be sixteen fingerbreadths, and its height nine fingerbreadths.
Likewise one should make it broad, and six fingerbreadths deep.
The breadth at the back is two fingerbreadths, and the middle is made very smooth.
The pestle here is half-moon-shaped and ten fingerbreadths long.
In that mortar one should grind five palas of <s>sūta</s> with sour gruel for three days,
certainly for removing the external impurity of <s>rasarāja</s> (the king of mercury).
Immediately after that, one should wash it with hot sour-gruel water.
After this I shall explain the <s>mūrcchana</s> (stupefying treatment) of <s>pārada</s>.
<s>Mūrcchana</s>, free from faults, destroys the seven coverings.
<s>Svarjikā</s>, <s>yāvaśūka</s>, and likewise the five salts,
together with all acidic drugs, should be ground with <s>sūta</s>.
This is done in the mortar for three days, until it reaches the state of disappearing.
Through the loss of its own form, that is here called <s>mūrcchana</s>.
It obtains purity, and the breaking of knots takes place.
Then the operation called <s>utthāpana</s> (raising) of <s>pārada</s>
should be carried out carefully by excellent physicians according to the path of <s>rasaśāstra</s>.
Then it should be sweated in a <s>dolāyantra</s> for three days, as before.
It is ground for one day on a stone slab in the heat of the sun.
This is proper <s>utthāpana</s>, destroying the fault of <s>mūrcchā</s>.
<s>Pātana</s> (distillation) is indeed a great operation; I shall describe it in full detail.
<s>Pātana</s> is said to be threefold and to remove the faults of <s>rasa</s>.
There are upward distillation, downward distillation, and sideways distillation, in order.
The characteristic form of the upward-distillation apparatus is stated here.

children.text: mṛṇmayī sthālikā kāryā cocchritā tu ṣaḍaṃgulā ||
children.translated_text: An earthen vessel should be made, six fingerbreadths high.
At the mouth it should measure seven fingerbreadths, and around it thirteen fingerbreadths.

children.text: iyanmānā dvitīyā ca kartavyā sthālikā śubhā ||
children.translated_text: A second fine vessel of this same measure should also be made.

children.text: kṣāradvayaṃ rāmaṭhaṃ ca tathā hi paṭupañcakam
children.translated_text: The two alkalis, <s>rāmaṭha</s>, and likewise the five salts,
joined with the acidic class, should be used to grind <s>sūtaka</s>.
With that paste one should smear the good lower vessel.
Having placed the upper vessel over it with its mouth downward, one should make a sealed capsule.
There one should make the seal with ash and salt.

children.text: culyāṃ sthālīṃ niveśyātha dhānyāgniṃ tatra kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having set the vessel on the hearth, one should make a grain-husk fire there.
Above it a water-holder should be arranged for four watches.
When one knows that it has cooled by itself, one should collect the upward-moving <s>rasa</s>.
Thus this is declared to be the upward-distillation apparatus.

children.text: pūrvoktāṃ sthālikāṃ samyak viparītāṃ tu paṃkile
children.translated_text: The previously described vessel, properly inverted in a muddy pit,

children.text: garte tu sthāpitāṃ bhūmau jvālayenmūrdhni pāvakam ||
children.translated_text: is set in the ground, and one should kindle fire on its top.
For three watches <s>pārada</s> falls downward.
This is called the downward-distillation apparatus by those who know <s>rasa</s>.
One should thoroughly grind <s>rasarāja</s> together with the drugs mentioned before.

children.text: tiryagghaṭe rasaṃ kṣiptvā tanmukhe hyaparo ghaṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having put the <s>rasa</s> in a sideways vessel, another vessel is placed at its mouth.
In the belly of the smaller one there is a hole, and in the hole an iron tube.
Excellent physicians should arrange the tube so that it rests in a water vessel.
The wise person should kindle an intense fire beneath the <s>rasa</s>-apparatus.
For three watches, the sideways distillation of <s>rasa</s> takes place.

children.text: yaṃtrāṇāṃ pātanānāṃ ca tritayaṃ sukaraṃ khalu ||
children.translated_text: The threefold set of apparatuses and distillations is indeed easy to perform.
I have explained it properly according to the teaching of the <s>rasāgama</s>.
Now I shall explain the operation of restraining <s>rasa</s>.
When it is done, the restlessness of <s>rasarāja</s> is calmed.
One should take ten palas of salt born from the Sindhu and also three prasthas of water,
and place faultless <s>sūtaka</s> inside a pot.

children.text: pidhānena yathā samyak mudritaṃ mṛtsnayā khalu
children.translated_text: It should certainly be sealed properly with a lid and clay.
One should keep it for three days in a windless and solitary place.
By just this method perform <s>rodhana</s> (restraining), O king of physicians.
After this I shall explain the <s>niyāmana</s> (regulating) of <s>pārada</s>.
The excellent <s>rasa</s>, placed in a pot together with water and rock salt,
and sweated for three days, becomes powerful.
Now I shall explain the <s>dīpana</s> (stimulating) of <s>rasarāja</s>.

children.text: bubhukṣā vyāpakatvaṃ ca yena kṛtvā prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: By performing it, appetite and pervasiveness arise.
Mustard together with salt, black pepper, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
with <s>kāṅkṣī</s> joined with <s>kāsīsa</s> and combined with sour gruel,

children.text: dināni trīṇi saṃsvedya paścāt kṣāreṇa mardayet
children.translated_text: should be sweated for three days; afterward one should grind it with alkali.
By this very method <s>dīpana</s> certainly arises.
Intensity, quick action, pervasiveness, and hunger,
and especially strength, arise when the procedure has been done properly.
The operation of producing a mouth is indeed a form of <s>dīpana</s>.
I shall briefly explain the proper purification of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Sūtaka</s> should be combined with gold in an eighteenth part,
and ground with lemon juice for one day after that.

children.text: kṣāraiśca lavaṇai ramyaiḥ sveditaḥ kāṃjikena hi
children.translated_text: It is then sweated with fine alkalis and salts in sour gruel.
When washed with sour gruel, a mouth for eating is produced.

children.text: tāpyasatvaṃ kalāṃśena hemnā tad dviguṇena ca
children.translated_text: One should use essence of <s>tāpya</s> in a sixteenth part, and gold in twice that amount.
After heating it in a heated iron mortar, one should then grind it thoroughly.

children.text: vyaktaṃ hi rasacukreṇa kṣāreṇa caṇakasya hi
children.translated_text: Clearly, with <s>rasacakra</s> and the alkali of chickpea,
one should grind it for twenty-one days with the juices of citron and <s>pūraka</s>.

children.text: vāsare yāmamekaṃ tu pratyekaṃ hi vimardayet
children.translated_text: For one watch in a day one should grind each of them separately.

children.text: yātudhānamukhaṃ samyak yātyeva hi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It certainly becomes properly <s>yātudhānamukha</s> (demon-mouthed); there is no doubt.
Thus I have explained the second method of <s>dīpana</s> (stimulation).
And the eight refinements of <s>sūta</s> have been described for operations on the body.

children.text: tathā ca daśa karmāṇi dehalohakarāṇi hi ||
children.translated_text: So too the ten operations that produce effects in the body and in metals have been taught.
Now I shall explain the consumption of <s>abhraka</s> (mica).
By the <s>karoṭī</s> method a proper iron capsule should be made.
Through the use of a water-apparatus, <s>rasa</s> joined with <s>viḍa</s>
certainly consumes the morsels of <s>abhra</s>; there is no doubt.

children.text: ato hi jalayaṃtrasya lakṣaṇaṃ kathyate mayā
children.translated_text: Therefore I will describe the characteristics of the water-apparatus.
There should be a well-rounded iron vessel, and in it three <s>āḍhakas</s> of water.
In its middle a very firm iron capsule should be properly made.
Inside the iron capsule purified <s>pārada</s> should be placed,
carefully joined with <s>viḍa</s> in a sixteenth part,
and likewise <s>abhrasattva</s> (mica essence) in a sixty-fourth part within the capsule.
Afterward one should seal the capsule with firm watery clay,
or with fire-clay, and make the joint sealed.

children.text: culyāṃ niveśya taṃ yaṃtraṃ jalenoṣṇena pūritam
children.translated_text: Having set that apparatus on a hearth, filled with hot water,
the fire should be applied gradually for just half a day.
When this is done, it consumes a measured morsel; there is no doubt here.
By this same method it should certainly consume six morsels.
When the <s>abhrasattva</s> has been consumed, it grants success in all operations.

children.text: mānaṃ mānavihīnena kartuṃ kena na śakyate ||
children.translated_text: How can a measure be made by anyone who lacks measure?
Therefore the operation of measurement must be explained by me as taught.
A <s>bīja</s> (seed), in a sixty-fourth part, makes a mouth in <s>pārada</s>.
Afterward the excellent <s>bīja</s> should be given in a thirty-second part.
Then one should place a morsel of the <s>bīja</s> in a sixteenth part.
It should be given by the best physicians in an eighth part of the <s>rasa</s>.
Then the morsel is given in a fourth part in this way.

children.text: tathā ca samabhāgena grāsenaiva ca sādhayet
children.translated_text: Likewise one should accomplish it with a morsel in an equal part.
With <s>viḍa</s> in a sixteenth part, the <s>rasa</s> becomes hungry.

children.text: yadā jīrṇo bhaved grāsaḥ pātitaśca viḍena hi ||
children.translated_text: When the morsel has become digested and has been brought down with <s>viḍa</s>,
<s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>sindhu</s> salt, <s>sauvarcala</s>, and <s>surāṣṭrikā</s>,

children.text: gaṃdhakena samaṃ kṛtvā viḍo 'yaṃ vahnikṛd bhavet ||
children.translated_text: made equal with sulphur, form this <s>viḍa</s>, which produces fire.
Now, as for the operation of internal liquefaction, the <s>cāraṇa</s> (assimilation) that increases qualities,
I shall explain it exactly, as it brings accomplishment for <s>rasarāja</s>.
Essence of <s>tāpya</s>, essence of <s>abhra</s>, and copper extracted from <s>ghoṣa</s>-metal,
all in equal portions, should be smelted with a fire of <s>khadira</s> wood.
With a pair of bellows, until only the mica remains,
one should make that <s>abhrasattva</s>, in an equal portion, assimilate with <s>sūta</s>.
By this very method the digestion in <s>rasa</s> is threefold.
The digestion belonging to internal liquefaction has been taught by the best physicians.
Now the procedure for external liquefaction is described according to the path of the guru.
<s>Abhrasattva</s> in a crucible, with the juice of <s>vajravallī</s>,
when smelted with <s>sauvarcala</s>, becomes <s>rasa</s>-like.
The fusion of <s>abhradruti</s> (mica liquefaction) and <s>sūta</s> is made in equal parts.

children.text: tena bandhatvamāyāti bāhyā sā kathyate drutiḥ
children.translated_text: By that it attains the state of being bound; that is called external liquefaction.
The operation of external liquefaction succeeds through devotion to <s>Śiva</s>.
Through the guru's grace and constant worship of <s>Mahābhairava</s>,
and through worship of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śivā</s>, the external liquefaction succeeds.
Now I shall explain the operation of <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion/calcination) in full detail.

children.text: abhrakaṃ tāpyasatvaṃ ca samaṃ kṛtvā tu saṃdhamet ||
children.translated_text: One should make <s>abhraka</s> and essence of <s>tāpya</s> equal and smelt them.
The essence that is made with the mica remaining should be digested in <s>rasa</s>.
Thus, by just the <s>pūtidvana</s> procedure, one should prepare the dense essence.
According to the metallurgical procedure, it makes metal; it does not make the body.
<s>Gaja</s> and <s>vaṅga</s>, being very dangerous, should always be avoided.
That prepared dense essence, rubbed down and resembling dust,
should be placed, in the measure of one <s>valla</s>, in the mouth of the hungry <s>rasa</s>.
The <s>rasa</s> is stated to be one quarter of a <s>gadyāṇaka</s>.
An acidic liquid kept in a copper vessel, combined with rock salt,
or else together with milk, should be left for a period of two days.

children.text: jātaṃ tutthasamaṃ nīlaṃ kalkaṃ tatprocyate budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The blue paste that becomes like <s>tuttha</s> is called <s>kalka</s> by the wise.
Together with this paste one should grind <s>sūtaka</s>
for three days in a heated mortar; afterward it is washed with sour gruel.
One should place it in a bronze vessel, and put <s>viḍa</s> above and below it.
Then one should make a capsule with an eighth part of the <s>rasa</s>.
Having closed the mouth with birch-bark, one should wrap it with thread.
After wrapping the capsule in cloth, one should then sweat it in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus.
Day by day, with cow urine, the class of acids, and sour gruel,
in a stone vessel, or in an iron vessel, or else in one made of glass,
one should then wash the <s>rasa</s> with hot sour-gruel water.
After placing it in a firm cloth folded four times, the <s>rasa</s>, when pressed downward,
falls into another vessel, if all the <s>pārada</s> does so.
Then the mica has been properly digested, and the <s>rasa</s> becomes <s>daṇḍadhārī</s> (staff-bearing).
Again, at the measure of a morsel, the unsurpassed <s>abhrabīja</s> should be given.
By eight morsels it should digest everything according to the guru's path.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte samaṃ cābhraṃ sūtake jīryati dhruvam
children.translated_text: When this is done, an equal quantity of <s>abhra</s> is certainly digested in <s>sūtaka</s>.

children.text: svahastena kṛtaṃ samyak jāraṇaṃ na śrutaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: This proper <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) was done by my own hand; it was not merely heard of by me.
When an equal amount of <s>abhraka</s> (mica) has been properly digested, the <s>rasa</s> becomes staff-bearing.
It is then called a child, and even that can accomplish some work.

children.text: dviguṇe triguṇe caiva kathyate 'tra mayā khalu
children.translated_text: At double and triple [digestion] it is indeed described here by me.
When fourfold <s>abhraka</s> has been digested, I call it an adolescent.

children.text: jīrṇe pañcaguṇe cābhre yuvā caiva rasottamaḥ
children.translated_text: When fivefold <s>abhraka</s> has been digested, the excellent <s>rasa</s> is a young man.
But when sixfold <s>abhraka</s> has been caused to digest, the excellent <s>rasa</s> is an old man.
When sevenfold or eightfold mica-essence has been digested, it is extremely aged.
This <s>pārada</s> itself then produces every accomplishment.
By this same method one should cause all metals to be digested.
Now I shall explain the cause of the increase of <s>vedha</s> (transmuting penetration).
It is <s>sāraṇa</s>, the great accomplisher among all operations.
A crucible, shaped like a <s>dhūrta</s> flower, should be eight finger-breadths long.
It should be made very wide at the mouth, measuring four finger-breadths.
It should be made of clay, dry, and very smooth inside.
Another crucible serving as a cover should be well hollowed and furnished with a hole.
Pure, well-digested <s>sūta</s> should be placed in the middle of the crucible.
There should be fish, turtle, frog, leech, sheep, and boar;

children.text: ekīkṛtya vasāmeṣām evaṃ tailaṃ tu sāraṇam
children.translated_text: after combining their fat, the oil is thus the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil.
Earthworm dung, honey, and crow excrement,
as well as that of locusts and the dirt from the ears of buffaloes,
one should prescribe these as a paste in a sixteenth part of the <s>rasa</s>.
After filtering it through cloth, one should place it in the oil.

children.text: sāraṇārthe kṛtaṃ tailaṃ tasmin taile supācayet ||
children.translated_text: In that oil, made for the purpose of <s>sāraṇa</s>, one should cook it well.

children.text: bījaṃ ca kalkamiśraṃ hi kṛtvā mūṣopari nyaset
children.translated_text: Having made the <s>bīja</s> (metal seed) mixed with the paste, one should place it above the crucible.
With the second cover one should close the mouth of the crucible.
One should seal the pair of crucibles with ash and salt.
Having dug out [a pit] for three parts of the small crucible, one should set it in the earth.
Above that one should smelt it properly with firm charcoal and a fierce fire.
Thus the well-digested <s>bīja</s> falls fully into the <s>rasa</s>.
The lordly <s>sūta</s> comes into fixation; when subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s>, it becomes endowed with qualities.
First digested and then subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s>, it grants every accomplishment.

children.text: no jāritaḥ sāritaśca kathaṃ bandhakaro bhavet
children.translated_text: If it is not digested and subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s>, how could it produce fixation?
Known through a teacher's instruction, the operation of <s>sāraṇa</s> is excellent.
It was done properly by the method of direct experience; it was not merely heard.
Now the <s>krāmaṇaka</s> (penetrating) operation of <s>pārada</s> is stated.

children.text: śāstrātkṛtaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ hi yathāvat krāmayedrasam ||
children.translated_text: A procedure done only from a treatise has not in fact been seen; [here is] how one should make the <s>rasa</s> penetrate properly.
Ear dirt of buffalo cows and woman's milk, mixed with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax),

children.text: etānyeva samāni ca kṛtvā dravyāṇi mardayecca dinam ||
children.translated_text: having made these substances equal, one should grind them for a day.
Poison, <s>darada</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, and red <s>kāntaka</s>,
<s>indragopa</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and also crow excrement:

children.text: kalkametad adhordhvaṃ hi madhye sūtaṃ nidhāpayet
children.translated_text: placing this paste below and above, one should set the <s>sūta</s> in the middle.
Then, after adding powdered glass, one should heat it in a closed crucible.
By this very <s>krāmaṇa</s>, <s>pārada</s> penetrates in an instant.
This excellent <s>krāmaṇaka</s> was taught by <s>Nandirāja</s>.

children.text: tāpyasattvaṃ tathā nāgaṃ śuddhaṃ krāmaṇakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The essence of <s>tāpya</s>, purified <s>nāga</s> (lead), and the purified <s>krāmaṇaka</s>

children.text: bījāni pāradasyāpi kramate ca na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are also <s>bīja</s>s for <s>pārada</s>; it penetrates, without doubt.
Now I shall explain in full detail the procedure of <s>vedha</s>.
By merely knowing it, a man becomes one who understands <s>vedha</s>.
Oil of <s>dhūrta</s> (datura), <s>ahiphena</s> (opium), and likewise <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil,
<s>bhṛṅgī</s> oil, poison, and oil produced from nutmeg,
oil from the root of <s>hayamāra</s>, and the oil called <s>abdhiśoṣaka</s>,
know these and other oils to be agents of <s>vedha</s>.

children.text: siddhasūtena ca samaṃ marditaṃ vedhakṛd bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Ground with accomplished <s>sūta</s> in equal quantity, it becomes productive of <s>vedha</s>.
There is <s>lepavedha</s> (penetration by coating), <s>kṣepavedha</s> (penetration by casting in), and <s>kuntavedha</s> as well.
There is the one called smoke and <s>śabdavedha</s> (penetration by sound); thus it is remembered as fivefold.
Thin copper sheets, and also sheets made of purified silver,
smeared with the paste, should be heated by means of a closed crucible.
When they have cooled, one should take them out; this is called <s>lepavedha</s>.

children.text: drute tāmre 'thavā raupye rasaṃ tatra vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Into molten copper or silver one should cast the <s>rasa</s> there.

children.text: vidhyate tena sahasā kṣepavedhaḥ sa kathyate
children.translated_text: It is penetrated by that at once; this is called <s>kṣepavedha</s>.
One should melt lead, silver, copper, and likewise the other lower metals.
When <s>pārada</s> is placed here in any vessel while [the metal] is molten,
it penetrates; this is <s>kuntavedha</s>, so those who know the śāstra have said.
Through contact with the smoke, metals become gold and silver.
That should certainly be known as the <s>dhūmavedha</s> of <s>rasarāja</s>.
When the excellent bound <s>rasa</s> is present, a sound arises directly from contact;

children.text: tathaiva jāyate vedhaḥ śabdavedhaḥ sa kathyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>vedha</s> likewise occurs; that is called <s>śabdavedha</s>.
Now I shall explain the coloring of <s>pārada</s>.
When colored and made to penetrate, it is directly the god <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Coloring is prescribed with iron and copper by means of <s>rasaka</s>;
it should likewise be carried out according to the path of the śāstra with the red group.
Then the coloring of <s>pārada</s> should be done with the <s>gandharāga</s> (sulfur coloring).
with copper, red glass, and red rock salt.
The <s>sūta</s> placed in a closed crucible should be colored with copper and the other substances.
One should color it with the <s>gandharāga</s> by means of the brick-apparatus.
And with the coloring of <s>rasaka</s>, through the use of the balance-apparatus, [it should be colored].
By continual grinding with the powder of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (sharp iron), one should color <s>sūtaka</s>.
One should keep it for seven days with copper made into a paste.
There is no doubt that the coloring of <s>sūtarāja</s> comes about.
An earthen crucible should be made, smeared with substances of the red group.

children.text: tanmadhye pāradaṃ kṣiptvā dhmānād rañjanakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having put <s>pārada</s> in its middle, by heating with bellows it becomes a coloring preparation.

children.text: mayā saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ raṃjanaṃ pāradasya hi
children.translated_text: Thus I have briefly stated the coloring of <s>pārada</s>.
In the method of the <s>śāstra</s>, coloring has indeed been shown in many ways.
Now the operation of ingestion, the eighteenth for <s>pārada</s>,
is carefully explained here by me at length.
When carefully used according to the method of the <s>śāstra</s>, <s>sūta</s> grants accomplishments.
But when eaten otherwise, it kills a man like poison.
First one should perform emesis; afterward one should undertake purgation.
Then one should eat incinerated <s>abhra</s> (mica); after that comes the use of <s>sūta</s>.
The excellent <s>sūta</s>, properly purified, always acts upon the body and metals.
When used, it destroys all diseases and brings all accomplishments.
In whatever measure it becomes capable of penetrating a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of metal,
when eaten in that same measure for the body, it removes disease.
A <s>rājikā</s>, then a <s>priyaṅgu</s>, a mustard seed, a green gram, and a black gram,
a <s>raktikā</s>, a chickpea, or else a <s>valla</s>: the <s>rasa</s> should be of such a measure.
These doses for <s>rasa</s> have been stated by those skilled in all operations.
One should consume it with an accompanying drink and with a small piece of leaf.
When <s>sūta</s> is used in this way, one is freed from every disease.
Freed from every sin, one attains the highest state.
Now I shall explain the binding of <s>rasarāja</s>.

children.text: anubhūtaṃ mayā kiṃcit gurūṇāṃ hi prasādataḥ ||
children.translated_text: What I have experienced, through the grace of the teachers, is set forth in some measure.
Binding is said to be fourfold: <s>jalaukā</s>, <s>khoṭa</s>, and <s>pāṭa</s>,
and also that called <s>bhasma</s>; so it is directly taught in the <s>rasāgama</s>.
Cooked binding is <s>jalaukā</s>; the fixing of <s>piṣṭī</s> is <s>khoṭaka</s>.
<s>Pāṭa</s> is the binding as <s>parpaṭikā</s>, while <s>bhasma</s> is like ash.
Here they are: a herbal agent, a gem, gold, and the pair lead and tin;
these four are the causes of the binding of <s>sūta</s>.
The herbal binding is the best; the gem binding is middling.
The metal binding is inferior, and <s>pūti-bandha</s> is the lowest of the low.
The fifth is <s>druti-bandha</s> (binding through liquefaction), always effective for the body and metals.
By the special liquefaction of <s>abhra</s>, it should be recognized by the best physicians.
In due order I shall now explain the herbal binding of <s>rasa</s>.
The <s>rasa</s> should be purified, possessed of <s>rākṣasavaktra</s>, and digested with <s>abhraka</s>.
<s>Pārada</s> is ground for three days in the extract of the root of <s>iṅgudī</s>.

children.text: tata uddhṛtya vastreṇa baṃdhanaṃ kārayed bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: Then, having removed it, the physician should bind it with a cloth.
He should sweat it steadily in sour gruel for seven days.
And it should be cooked in the midst of grain for the span of a year.
Then, placed in a fruit of <s>dhūrta</s>, it should be sweated a hundred times.
It is cooked in <s>mahātaila</s>, in <s>dhūrta</s> oil, and in a heap of grain.
Bound by that method, it becomes hard.

children.text: vaṃgasya stambhanaṃ samyak karotyeva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: It properly fixes tin, without any doubt.
When held directly in the mouth, it always causes retention of semen.
Thus one herbal binding of <s>pārada</s> has been described.
Now there is another method of binding with regard to <s>pārada</s>.
One should grind it for seven days with juices from the roots of <s>nāgārjunī</s>.
Ground with neem wood and with substances produced by chewing in the mouth,
<s>pārada</s> then becomes like fresh butter through that treatment.

children.text: vastreṇa baṃdhanaṃ kṛtvā phale dhaurte niveśayet
children.translated_text: Having made a binding with cloth, one should insert it into a <s>dhūrta</s> fruit.
That, wrapped with cow-dung cakes, should be cooked in a dung-cake fire.

children.text: lāvakākhye puṭe samyak kramavṛddhyā śataṃ puṭet
children.translated_text: In the heating cycle called <s>lāvaka</s>, one should heat it properly a hundred times, increasing in sequence.
It should be cooked for a period of three months in the midst of grain.
Afterward one should give a hundred heating cycles with goat dung as before.
By just this method <s>sūtaka</s> is always bound.
This is a proven and observed procedure, taught for the practitioner.
When it is held properly in the mouth, it is supreme at producing retention of semen.
Thus the excellent bound <s>sūta</s> is fully capable of fixing tin as well.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sujāritābhraṃ vai sūtakaṃ ca vimardayet
children.translated_text: One should carefully grind purified <s>sūtaka</s>, well digested with <s>abhra</s>,
with the juice of <s>arka</s> root for one day, with care.
Then an adamantine crucible should be made, very firm and smoothed.
It should be smeared with a paste made from <s>arka</s> root.
After placing the <s>rasa</s> inside the crucible, one should seal it with another crucible.
When it has been properly heated with bellows for half a watch, a <s>rasakhoṭa</s> is produced.
Knowing that it has cooled by itself, one should take out the <s>rasakhoṭa</s>.
Kept in the mouth for the measure of a year, it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.
This <s>pārada</s> bound by herbs also grants all accomplishments.
Herbal binding is true; it was performed by <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and others.
It is excellent, producing all accomplishments and always accomplishing every task.
The excellent <s>rasa</s>, purified properly and likewise fed on <s>ambara</s> (mica),
should then be ground for seven days with juices of <s>jalakūmbhī</s>.
One should prepare a crucible from that; the <s>sūtaka</s> should be placed there.
In another blind crucible one should confine the crucible containing <s>sūta</s>.
A heating cycle should be applied there with one <s>araṇyaka</s>.
Heating cycles should then be given, increasing by one <s>utpala</s> each time.
By this very procedure one should administer three <s>puṭa</s> heating cycles.
The lord of mercury, <s>sūtendra</s>, attains binding; this is true, as is the guru's word.
One should carefully pulverize <s>dhūrta</s> seeds thoroughly.
In the same amount as <s>sūtarāja</s>, one should distill them by an upward apparatus.
Twenty-one times; then one should place it in a mortar.
One should grind it for seven days in the extract of <s>iṅgudī</s> leaves.
Then with the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> and with <s>viṣakharparaka</s>,
grinding with juice of <s>pāṭhā</s> and also the fresh juice of <s>lajjālu</s>,

children.text: tryahaṃ tryahaṃ ca saṃmardya bandhamāyāti niścitam
children.translated_text: grinding for three days with each, it certainly comes to binding.
It should be sweated in a <s>dolāyantra</s> for a week in the juice of <s>dhūrta</s>.
Having placed it in the belly of a <s>viṣa</s>-crucible, together with flesh produced from a pig,
one should fry it with <s>dhūrta</s> oil; in a week a mouth arises.
It becomes hard, like diamond; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: kṣīraṃ śoṣayate nityaṃ kautukārthe na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It continually dries up milk, as a demonstration; there is no doubt.

children.text: vīryaṃ vaṃgaṃ stambhayati satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: It arrests semen and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin); true, true, there is no doubt.
Five procedures have been told for the binding of <s>sūtarāja</s>.
Now, in sequence, comes the second, <s>vajrabandha</s>, just as it is.
Having examined the <s>rasaśāstra</s>s in many ways, I speak.

children.text: vajrasatvaṃ tathā sūtaṃ samāṃśaṃ kārayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: A wise person should take essence of diamond and <s>sūta</s> in equal portions.
Gold equal to a quarter of the <s>rasa</s> should be added; one should grind the three together.
Then one should process it with the root juice of <s>vandhyākarkoṭikā</s>.
Likewise, also with juice of <s>dhūrta</s> and with juice of <s>citraka</s>.
Also with <s>kāmbojī</s> juice and likewise with <s>nāḍī</s> juice.

children.text: āsāṃ niyāmikānāṃ ca rasaṃ vastreṇa gālayet ||
children.translated_text: The juices of these regulating substances should be strained through cloth.
In this order, one should grind it for one day each in the heat of the sun.
The ball, placed in a closed crucible, should be sealed with a firm seal.
Afterward, it is placed in an iron capsule and sealed firmly.
It should then be heated with bellows for a measure of two <s>ghaṭikā</s>s.
When one knows that it has cooled by itself, one should take up the crucible.
Digging it out carefully, one should collect the ash of <s>sūta</s>.
That ball, heated with a combination of glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
as <s>sūtaka</s>, effects a hundredfold transmutation; there is no doubt.
Kept in the mouth, it destroys death and becomes capable of perfecting body and metals.

children.text: vajrabhasma tathā sūtaṃ samaṃ kṛtvā tu mardayet
children.translated_text: Taking diamond ash and <s>sūta</s> in equal measure, one should grind them.
with the juices of <s>trinemikā</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, and <s>sahadevī</s>.
For a week, with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, in very intense solar heat,

children.text: rasagolaṃ suvṛttaṃ tu śuṣkaṃ caivātha lepayet ||
children.translated_text: then one should coat the well-rounded <s>rasa</s> ball after it has dried.
With juice of <s>kākamācī</s> and with the fresh juice of <s>lāṅgalī</s>,
and with juice of <s>gojihvikā</s>, one should coat it seven times.
The ball placed in a diamond crucible should be sealed with a firm seal.
It should be enclosed in an iron capsule-crucible and set in the middle.
Coat it properly with seven clay-smeared cloth layers and make it very firm.
Heated there with strong charcoal, it is then cooled in place.
After breaking it open, the <s>sūta</s> in the crucible is a lump like a star,
bright, capable of every operation; when tinctured, it becomes capable of transmutation.
One should also grind <s>sūtaka</s> together with liquefied <s>abhraka</s>.
In equal portions, on a stone slab, for three watches without interruption.
It should be combined with <s>kastūrī</s> and <s>dhanasāra</s>, and mixed with black <s>agaru</s>.
Joined also with sugar, garlic, and <s>rāmaṭha</s>.
And with <s>palāśa</s> seed, as well as with the juice of its flowers,
then <s>sūtaka</s>, ground in the fierce sun together with the liquefactions,
surely combines; there is no doubt. What need is there for much speech?
Then with the juice of <s>guñjā</s> and of white <s>vṛścīvaka</s>,
and with the juices of <s>lāṅgalī</s>, until binding takes place.
Then, in an open crucible, one should blow it briefly with five coals.
It comes swiftly to binding, like a lotus at sunrise.
When combined with liquefied <s>abhraka</s>, <s>rasendra</s> is indeed fixed.
One should be a direct devotee of <s>Śiva</s>, truthful and with restrained senses.
The proper union of the two <s>Śiva</s>s will take place in his hand.
The binding of <s>pārada</s> that has been taught in the <s>rasāgama</s>s,

children.text: kathitaṃ tanmayā spaṣṭaṃ nānubhūtaṃ na ceṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: that has been clearly stated by me; it is not unexperienced or unpracticed.
For diamonds of the <s>brahma</s> class, the liquefaction should be the measure of a <s>valla</s>.
One should grind it with a <s>tolaka</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> in the juice of <s>kanyakā</s>.
One should grind it thoroughly until a paste is produced.
Having made a clean, even crucible fashioned from fire-stone,

children.text: tanmadhye piṣṭikāṃ muktvā piṣṭīmānaṃ viṣaṃ tvaheḥ
children.translated_text: put the little paste inside it, and add snake poison equal to the paste.
One should make a matching lid and then close the mouth with it.
One should place the good crucible in the middle of a bronze vessel.

children.text: bhājanāni ca catvāri caturdikṣu gatāni ca ||
children.translated_text: And four vessels should be placed in the four directions.
Wonderful: through the contact of heat, <s>pārada</s> comes to binding.
In one watch under fierce sunlight, constantly; this was spoken very clearly by <s>Śiva</s>.
Through combination with diamond liquefaction, <s>sūta</s> goes to binding.
Of all bindings of <s>sūta</s>, this has truly been declared the best.
Now I shall explain the binding of <s>sūtarāja</s>.
One should grind liquefied gold with <s>rasendra</s> for seven days.
It is washed with the juice of <s>jvālāmukhī</s> and afterward with sour gruel.
Each day one should wash it at night, and by day with the juice just mentioned.
Afterward, when it has been put in a closed crucible, with clay and cloth...
One should coat it seven times and place the ball in a pit in the ground.
It should be twelve aṅgulas broad and twelve aṅgulas deep.
The measure of the pit has been clearly stated according to the teacher's method.

children.text: tatropari puṭaṃ deyaṃ gajāhvaṃ chagaṇena ca
children.translated_text: Over it one should give the heating called <s>gaja</s>, with dung-cakes as fuel.
In just twelve watches <s>pārada</s> (mercury) becomes bound by itself.
The <s>rasa</s> bound in molten gold perfects the body and metals.
It is splendid, produces all accomplishments, and destroys old age and poverty.
This is the third binding with metals, performed by me with my own hand.
I shall explain it exactly as it is, for the sake of the practitioner.
One should have very fine sheets of gold made, like birch bark.
They should be only the size of a <s>kola</s>; the <s>sūtaka</s> should measure one <s>pala</s>.
One should grind it with lemon juice for one day without interruption.
Then, after making it into a ball, one should set it on a potsherd.
It should be placed on the hearth, and one should sprinkle it with sour grain-liquid.
The fixing of the paste should be done regularly for a period of three days.
Then one should steam it with the juice of <s>dhūrta</s> for seven days.

children.text: śvetā punarnavā ciṃcā sahadevī ca nīlikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śvetā punarnavā</s>, <s>ciñcā</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and <s>nīlikā</s>,
and likewise <s>dhūrtavadhū</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>suradālikā</s>,
have been declared by <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and others to be the best agents for binding <s>sūta</s>.
With the fresh juices and pastes of these, one should coat the ball of <s>sūta</s>.
After that, one should wrap it in three layers of birch-bark leaves.
After tying it into a cloth packet, one should steam it with lemon juice.

children.text: yāmatrayaṃ prayatnena dhautaḥ paścād gavāṃ jalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is done carefully for three watches; afterward it is washed with cow-water.
Then one should cook it, placed inside fruits of <s>dhūrta</s>, with many heatings.
With heatings called <s>lāvaka</s>, the wise man makes it beautiful, like a sun-stone.

children.text: jāyate nātra saṃdeho baddhaḥ śivasamo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: It comes into being; there is no doubt. Once bound, it becomes equal to <s>Śiva</s>.
One should thoroughly grind <s>sūtaka</s> with silver in a one-eighth portion.
The wise man should make a paste with the fresh juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s>.

children.text: khoṭaṃ baddhvā tu vipacet dhūrtataile trivāsarān
children.translated_text: After binding it as a <s>khoṭa</s> (lump), he should cook it in <s>dhūrta</s> oil for three days.
Likewise in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil, and in oil produced from the root of <s>karavīra</s>,
also in oil produced from <s>jātīphala</s>, and in that produced from <s>vatsanāga</s>,
and likewise in that produced from <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, and indeed from <s>samudraśoṣaka</s>,
and also in that produced from <s>devadāru</s>; the intelligent physician should cook it.
Afterward very strong liquor is to be applied by means of a husk-fire.
For a full seven days; a mouth certainly arises.
It properly causes retention of semen; it drinks milk, and not otherwise.
In a very broad iron vessel one should make a basin of <s>tuttha</s>.
Having placed in it a measured amount of <s>sūta</s> that has undergone the eight purifications,
one should cover it with powdered <s>tuttha</s> and fill it with lemon juice.
The mouth of the iron vessel should be carefully closed with a lid.
Then it should be kept for three days in a windless, solitary place.
The physician should wash it repeatedly with warm sour gruel.
The color of the <s>sūtaka</s> is seen to be like fresh butter.
Then, after binding the <s>rasa</s> into a <s>khoṭa</s>, one should steam it with sour gruels for three days.
After placing the <s>khoṭa</s> in the middle of a small heap of stone-powder,
water-sprinkling should be done; when it has cooled, one should take it up.
By this very method one should certainly cook it three times.
It surely attains hardness, just as the guru's word is true.
Then one should cook it also with a thousand fruits of <s>dhūrta</s>.
Its mouth arises properly, and this too causes retention of potency.
Having made <s>vaṅga</s> and <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s> equal, one should smelt them in a diamond crucible.
With intense charcoal, one should carefully bring the <s>vaṅga</s> through properly.
By this same method one should make the <s>trapu</s> carry three times over.

children.text: bījaṃ śāṇapramāṇaṃ hi sūtaṃ palamitaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The seed should be the measure of a <s>śāṇa</s>, while the <s>sūta</s> should measure one <s>pala</s>.
One should grind it with the juice of <s>kanyakā</s> for one day and dry it out.
The steaming of the ball should likewise be done for seven days.
The wise man should steam it for three watches in a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.
With the fresh juice of <s>kumārī</s> and also with the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>,

children.text: bhṛṃgīrasena ca tathā tridinaṃ svedyameva hi
children.translated_text: and likewise with the juice of <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, it should indeed be steamed for three days.
In this way, with each herb separately, one should place it in a glass bottle.
After grinding <s>khaṭī</s>, <s>paṭu</s>, and <s>śivābhakta</s>, one should seal the mouth.
The pit should be three cubits in measure, and one should have it filled with <s>laddī</s> fuel.
In the middle one should place a small glass vessel filled with liquor.
After it has remained in the ground for two months, one should take it out.
The excellent bound <s>sūta</s> should be collected, white and resembling moonlight.
Kept in the mouth, it properly makes the body firm like a strong diamond.
A man may go to a hundred women, free from wrinkles and grey hair.
According to the teaching of the <s>Devīśāstra</s>, this too is <s>rasa</s> bound by metals.

children.text: prakāśito mayā samyak nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: It has been fully revealed by me; no deliberation should be made about it.

children.text: raseṃdraḥ kāntalohaṃ ca tīkṣṇalohaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rasendra</s>, <s>kāntaloha</s>, and likewise <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s>,
as well as the essence of <s>abhraka</s> and the essence of <s>tāpya</s>, combined with gold,
all in equal parts, should be ground with lemon juice.
One should saturate them for one day and afterward make a ball.
A baked crucible should be prepared, and the ball should be placed in its womb.

children.text: gojihvā kākamācī ca nirguṃḍī dugdhikā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gojihvā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and likewise <s>dugdhikā</s>,
<s>kumārī</s> and <s>meghanādā</s>, combined with honey and rock salt,
with the fresh juice of these the physician should steam it repeatedly.
The ball should be steamed until it becomes firm.

children.text: vaktre dhṛtaṃ jarāmṛtyuṃ nihanti ca na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Held in the mouth, it destroys old age and death; there is no doubt.
Having quickly destroyed all diseases, it certainly arrests age.

children.text: karṇe kaṇṭhe tathā haste dhāritā mastake'pi vā
children.translated_text: When it is worn on the ear, on the neck, likewise on the hand, or even on the head,
defects such as hostile magic never occur.
The four kinds of binding of the venerable king <s>sūta</s> (mercury) have thus been taught by me.

children.text: kurvanti ye tattvavido bhiṣagvarā rājñāṃ gṛhe te'pi bhavanti pūjyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those excellent physicians, knowers of the truth, who perform them become honored even in the houses of kings.

children.text: iti paramarahasyaṃ sūtarājasya coktaṃ rasanigamamahābdher labdham etat suratnam
children.translated_text: Thus the supreme secret of the king <s>sūta</s> has been stated: this fine jewel obtained from the great ocean of the <s>rasa</s> scriptures.

children.text: sakalaguṇavariṣṭhā vādinaḥ kautukajñā nijahṛdi ca sukaṇṭhe dhārayiṣyanti tajjñāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who know it, eminent in every virtue, skilled in disputation and aware of marvels, will hold it in their own heart and in their fine throat.
Now <s>rasabhasma</s> (mercurial ash) is described by me according to the injunctions of the whole science of <s>pārada</s>.
It is adorned with a set of four colors: white, black, bright yellow, and red.
Fine <s>darada</s> prepared by the <s>haṃsapāka</s> method is ground with all the juice of neem.
For a fixed four watches it is stirred in equal proportion in the thick sour juice of <s>āmalaka</s>.
It is placed in an apparatus called <s>ḍamaruka</s>; after that, iron powder equal to chalk is added.

children.text: supayasā lavaṇena vimarditaṃ kuru bhiṣagvara yantrasurodhanam ||
children.translated_text: Ground with good milk and salt, O best physician, make a thorough sealing of the apparatus.
Here one should cook the <s>rasa</s> evenly with a mild fire for a fixed four watches.

children.text: upari tatra jalena niṣiñcayediti bhaveddaradād varasūtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should sprinkle water over it there; thus excellent <s>sūtaka</s> comes from <s>darada</s>.
Just as, by the best full purification, it is freed from all defects of its coverings,
so too it becomes a remover of many faults; that which arises from <s>darada</s> becomes supremely purified.
There should be eight <s>palas</s> of pure, excellent <s>sūta</s>; then the substances <s>dhātu</s>, <s>khaṭī</s>, <s>paṭu</s>, and <s>kāṅkṣikā</s>
are each in separate four-<s>pala</s> portions, while pure <s>sphaṭika</s> is measured at eight <s>palas</s>.

children.text: saha jalena vimṛdya ca yāmakaṃ lavaṇakāmlajalena vimiśritāḥ
children.translated_text: After grinding them with water for one watch, they are mixed with salt and sour water.

children.text: uditadhātugaṇasya ca mūṣikāṃ kuru viṣaṃ viniveśaya tatra vai ||
children.translated_text: Make a crucible from the stated group of substances, and place the poison there.
Cook this for twelve watches with fire in the excellent apparatus called <s>ḍamaruka</s>.
It always removes disorders of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and wasting, and is supreme in removing all diseases.
It gives men strength like that of the lord of elephants, and grants eyesight like that of the lord of birds.
This excellent <s>sūta</s> always gives pleasure and brings about amorous play with young women.
Endowed with dense essence, it gives luster and is said by me to remove every kind of skin disease.
Purified <s>rasa</s> and <s>gandhaka</s>, made free from faults, are then drenched with citrus juice.

children.text: praharayugmamitaṃ ca śilātale ravikareṇa vimardya vicūrṇitau ||
children.translated_text: They are rubbed on a stone slab in the sun's rays for two <s>praharas</s> and reduced to powder.
Placed in a beautiful glass flask and set in the excellent sand apparatus for three days,

children.text: kuru bhiṣagvara vahnim adhastataḥ sa ca bhavedaruṇaḥ kamalacchaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: O best physician, apply fire beneath it; it becomes red, with the hue of a lotus.
This <s>rasa</s>, named <s>Udayabhāskara</s>, itself becomes a destroyer of disease.
It should always be consumed in a dose of three <s>guñjās</s>, together with <s>magadhajā</s> (long pepper) and honey.
Even an old man who desires graceful acts of love becomes youthful in intercourse.

children.text: gadaharo balado'pi hi varṇado bhavati karmavipākajarogahā
children.translated_text: It removes illness, gives strength and complexion, and removes diseases born from the ripening of karma.
It has been revealed by me, a foremost twice-born, after consideration of the whole science of <s>sūtaka</s>.

children.text: rasavidāpi rasaḥ pariśodhito vigatadoṣakṛto'pi hi gaṃdhakaḥ
children.translated_text: Even when the <s>rasa</s> has been purified by a knower of <s>rasa</s> and the <s>gandhaka</s> has been made free from faults,
the pure sulfur powder should be poured into a clean iron pan.

children.text: atikuśāgniyute dravati svayaṃ tadanu tatra rasaḥ parimucyatām
children.translated_text: When, over a very sharp fire, it melts by itself, then <s>rasa</s> should be added there.
One should stir it with a clean iron spoon for the measure of three <s>praharas</s>.

children.text: tadanu kācaghaṭīṃ viniveśya vai sikatayantravareṇa hi pācitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after placing it in a glass flask, it is cooked in the excellent sand apparatus.
With fire applied beneath for twelve watches, the red <s>rasa</s> becomes reduced to ash at the bottom.

children.text: gatabalena nareṇa susevito bhavati vājikaraḥ sukhadaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: When properly used by a man whose strength has gone, it becomes aphrodisiac and always gives pleasure.
It destroys wrinkles and gray hair, and produces supreme freedom from disease for a hundred autumns.
One part of excellent purified <s>nāga</s> is mixed with four parts of <s>haraja</s>.

children.text: satatameva vimardya śilātale balivasāṃ ca samāṃ kuru tadbhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: After grinding it constantly on a stone slab, the physician should make it equal with <s>balivasā</s>.

children.text: dinamitaṃ suvimardya ca kanyakāsvarasa ainakareṇa viśoṣayet
children.translated_text: After grinding it well for a day, he should dry it with the fresh juice of <s>kanyā</s> in the sun.

children.text: tadanu sūtavarasya tu kajjalīṃ rucirakācaghaṭe viniveśaya ||
children.translated_text: After that, he should place the <s>kajjalī</s> of excellent <s>sūta</s> in a beautiful glass vessel.

children.text: divasayugmamadhaḥ kṛtavahninā sa ca bhavedaruṇaḥ kamalacchaviḥ
children.translated_text: With fire applied below for two days, it becomes red, with the hue of a lotus.
It destroys all diseases, kindles the digestive fire, gives strength, and is supremely luster-giving.
It destroys eye disease and produces the charms of all lovers.

children.text: sa khalu karmavipākajarogahā viśadanāgayutaḥ khalu pāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>pārada</s>, joined with purified <s>nāga</s>, indeed removes diseases born from the ripening of karma.

children.text: mṛdumṛdā racitā masṛṇeṣṭikā upari gartavareṇa ca saṃyutā
children.translated_text: On a smooth brick made of soft clay and furnished above with a fine hollow,
one should place ten <s>śāṇas</s> of excellent <s>rasa</s> together with fine <s>śukapiccha</s>.
When the good hollow has been completely filled with liquid produced from lime fruit,

children.text: sthagaya taṃ ca pidhānavareṇa vai mṛditayā sumṛdā parimudritam ||
children.translated_text: cover it with an excellent lid, well sealed with thoroughly kneaded fine clay.

children.text: tadanu kukkuṭānāṃ puṭe śṛto hupalakena vanodbhavakena vai
children.translated_text: Then it is heated in a <s>kukkuṭapuṭa</s> with forest-produced fuel-cakes.

children.text: vidhividā bhiṣajā hyamunā kṛto vimalaṣaḍguṇagandhakam aśnute ||
children.translated_text: A physician who knows the procedure should prepare it by this method and take pure <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) in a sixfold measure.

children.text: sa ca śarīrakaro'pyatha lohakṛt sakalasiddhikaraḥ paramo bhavet
children.translated_text: It becomes supreme, effecting the body, effecting metals, and accomplishing every <s>siddhi</s> (perfection).

children.text: śataguṇaṃ hi yadā parijīryate rasavaraḥ khalu hemakaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For when the excellent <s>rasa</s> is digested a hundredfold, it indeed becomes able to make gold.

children.text: saśukapicchasamo'pi hi pārado bhavati khalvatalena ca kuṭṭitaḥ
children.translated_text: Even <s>pārada</s> (mercury), when pounded on the surface of a mortar, becomes like a parrot's feather.
Prepare a very firm <s>parpaṭī</s> (thin flake preparation), and also a <s>poṭalī</s> (packet) made bound in cloth.

children.text: upari nāgarasena vilepitā ravikareṇa sadā pariśoṣitām
children.translated_text: It should be smeared above with <s>nāga-rasa</s> and always dried by the rays of the sun.
After coating it seven times with the juice of gold leaf, place it at the bottom of a pit in the ground.
The pit in the ground should be one cubit long and exactly twelve finger-breadths deep.

children.text: sikatayā paripūrya tadardhakaṃ tadanu tatra niveśaya poṭṭalīm ||
children.translated_text: Fill half of it with sand, and then place the <s>poṭalī</s> there.

children.text: upari vālukayā paripūrya tacchagaṇakaiśca puṭaṃ paridīyatām
children.translated_text: Fill it above with sand, and give it a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating) with cow-dung cakes.

children.text: dvidaśayāmam athāgnimaho kuru bhavati tena mahārasapoṭalī
children.translated_text: Then apply fire for twelve watches; by this it becomes the <s>mahārasa-poṭalī</s>.

children.text: iti mayā kathitā rasapoṭalī balakarā sukarā sukhasiddhidā ||
children.translated_text: Thus I have taught the <s>rasa-poṭalī</s>, strength-giving, easy to make, and giving easy success.
Then <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), likewise equal to purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury), is well triturated on the mortar slab.

children.text: tridinameva hi haṃsapadīrase dinakarasya kareṇa suśoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For three days, with the juice of <s>haṃsapadī</s>, it is thoroughly dried by the rays of the sun.

children.text: vimalalohamaye dṛḍhakharpare tadanu kajjalikāṃ pratimucya vai
children.translated_text: Then, in a firm saucer made of pure iron, one should put the <s>kajjalī</s> (black mercury-sulfur compound).

children.text: karamitā sukṛtāpi hi cuhlikā hyupari tatra niveśaya ca bhājanaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Having made a good hand-measured little stove, place a vessel there above it.

children.text: amalalohamayena ca darviṇā rasavaraṃ niyataṃ parimardayet
children.translated_text: With a clean iron ladle one should constantly stir the excellent <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: tadanu vahnimadhaḥ kuru vai dṛḍhaṃ satatameva hi yāmacatuṣṭayam ||
children.translated_text: Then make a strong fire beneath it, continuously for four watches.

children.text: supaca eṣa raso jaladopamo bhavati vallamito madhunā yutaḥ
children.translated_text: When well cooked, this cloud-colored <s>rasa</s>, in a <s>valla</s> measure and joined with honey,
when swallowed, removes the group of wasting diseases and is supreme for increasing men's sexual vigor.

children.text: sa ca valīpalitāni vināśayet sakalakuṣṭhavināśakaraḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: It destroys wrinkles and gray hair, and is excellent for destroying every skin disease.
One should place on the ground a small crucible fashioned from soft clay, measured in finger-breadths according to the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: rasavaraṃ vimalaṃ ca suśobhitaṃ saśukapicchasamaṃ parimarditam ||
children.translated_text: The excellent purified <s>rasa</s>, splendid and ground until it resembles a parrot's feather,
should be measured equal to the <s>rasa</s>, held in a crucible, paired with another, and carefully sealed.

children.text: kanakamūlarasena ca pācitaṃ tadanu saptadinaṃ kṛśavahninā ||
children.translated_text: It is cooked with the juice of <s>kanakamūla</s> for seven days over a low fire.

children.text: rasavarasya śubhaṃ hi vipācanaṃ yavamito rasarājavaras tadā
children.translated_text: This indeed is the good cooking of excellent <s>rasa</s>; then the best king of <s>rasa</s>, in a barley-sized dose,

children.text: dinamukhe pratihanti subhakṣitaḥ sakaladoṣakṛtāṃ vikṛtiṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: when eaten properly at daybreak, destroys and overcomes disorders produced by all the <s>doṣa</s>s.
Take two <s>pala</s>s of excellent <s>rasa</s> and an equal portion of attractive copper.

children.text: balivasāṃ ca ghṛtena vimardayed atikṛśāgnikṛte dravati svayam ||
children.translated_text: Grind them with <s>bali-vasā</s> (animal fat) and ghee; when put over a very low fire, it melts by itself.

children.text: tadanu tāmrarasau viniveśyatāṃ trayamidaṃ sarasaṃ ca vimarditam
children.translated_text: Then the copper and <s>rasa</s> should be placed in; these three, moist, are ground together.

children.text: drutamayaṃ ca sadāyasabhājane tadanu sūtakṛtāṃ varakajjalīm ||
children.translated_text: When the molten mass is in an iron vessel, then the fine <s>kajjalī</s> made from <s>sūta</s>
should be stirred with an iron ladle, and then poured upon a plantain leaf.

children.text: bhavati sāratamā rasaparpaṭī sakalarogavighātakarī hi sā ||
children.translated_text: That becomes the most essential <s>rasa-parpaṭī</s>; it destroys all diseases.
Make it joined with an equal amount of <s>trikaṭu</s> and measured with two <s>marica</s> seeds; it is always comfort-giving.
As an <s>anupāna</s> (adjuvant), it should be used combined with <s>triphalā</s> and honey.
One should eat the <s>parpaṭī</s> in the morning, likewise combined with <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>.
Combined with <s>pañcakola</s>, it removes <s>sannipāta</s>.
Eaten together with honey, it destroys every fever.
Together with <s>kaṇā</s> and honey, it cuts off every swelling.
With <s>śyāmā</s> and <s>trikaṭu</s>, it conquers <s>grahaṇī</s> arising from <s>vāta</s>.
Together with <s>guggulu</s> and <s>triphalā</s>, it destroys <s>vātarakta</s>.
Properly combined with <s>hiṅgu</s> and <s>puṣkara</s>, it removes colic from <s>vāta</s>.
With <s>vyoṣa</s> or with juices of <s>kanyā</s>, it destroys disorders of <s>kapha</s>.
With a decoction of <s>daśamūla</s>, too, it eliminates fever caused by <s>vāta</s>.
With a paste of <s>vākucī</s> seeds, it destroys itching and <s>pāmā</s>.
Combined with <s>āruṣkara</s>, it destroys <s>sidhma</s>.
With cow urine as the <s>anupāna</s>, it also destroys hemorrhoidal disease.
<s>Navamālikā</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>,
<s>śālmalī</s>, the five parts of <s>nimba</s>, <s>kalhāra</s>, and <s>guḍūcikā</s>,
and <s>nirguṇḍī</s>: the best physician should prepare these in equal parts.
Having powdered all that, he should make it the <s>anupāna</s> for <s>parpaṭī</s>.

children.text: aṣṭādaśa ca kuṣṭhāni nihantyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It destroys the eighteen kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease); there is no doubt.
<s>Parpaṭī</s> and the king of <s>rasa</s> destroy diseases according to the <s>anupāna</s>.
One should not eat unsuitable food, with attention to the <s>doṣa</s>, the affected tissue, and the rest.

children.text: śuddhaṃ rasaṃ gaṃdhakameva śuddhaṃ pṛthak samāṃśaṃ kuru yatnatastataḥ
children.translated_text: Carefully make purified <s>rasa</s> and purified <s>gandhaka</s> separately in equal portions.

children.text: eraṃḍamūlasya rasena sūtaṃ tathādrikarṇyā svarasena mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Grind the <s>sūta</s> with the juice of castor root and with the fresh juice of <s>adrikarṇī</s>.

children.text: taṃ kākamācyāḥ svarasena piṣṭvā tathā ca taṃ dāḍimabījatoyaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having ground it with the fresh juice of <s>kākamācī</s>, and likewise with the water of pomegranate seeds,

children.text: krameṇa sūtaṃ hi dinaiścaturbhiḥ śuddhatvamāyāti hi niścayena ||
children.translated_text: in sequence, over four days, the <s>sūta</s> certainly attains purification.

children.text: tatastu gaṃdhaṃ khalu mārkavadravair vibhāvyamānaṃ kuru lohapātre
children.translated_text: Then place the <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), repeatedly impregnated with the liquids of <s>mārkava</s>, in an iron vessel.

children.text: pradrāvayettaṃ badarasya cāgninā praḍhālayed bhṛṃgarase trivāram ||
children.translated_text: Melt it with a fire of <s>badara</s> wood and pour it into <s>bhṛṅga</s> juice three times.

children.text: kāryā tataḥ kajjalikā vimardya tāṃ drāvayellohamaye supātre
children.translated_text: Then <s>kajjalī</s> should be made by grinding; melt it in an excellent iron vessel.

children.text: praḍhālayettāṃ kadalīdale hi saṃchādya cānyena dalena paścāt ||
children.translated_text: Pour it onto a plantain leaf, and afterward cover it with another leaf.

children.text: tasyās tv adhordhvaṃ pradadīta gomayaṃ śītīkṛtā gavyaghṛtena bharjitā
children.translated_text: Cow dung should be placed below and above it; when cooled, it is fried with cow ghee.
This <s>rasa-parpaṭī</s> indeed destroys all diseases that arise from impurities and disturbed humors.

children.text: sā jīrakeṇaiva tu rāmaṭhena vātāmaśūlaṃ gṛhaṇīṃ sakāmalām
children.translated_text: With cumin and with <s>rāmaṭha</s>, it treats colic from wind and undigested matter, and <s>grahaṇī</s> accompanied by jaundice;

children.text: gulmāni cāṣṭāvudarāṇi hanyāt saṃsevitā śuddharasasya parpaṭī ||
children.translated_text: when regularly taken, this <s>parpaṭī</s> of purified <s>rasa</s> destroys abdominal tumors and the eight abdominal diseases.

children.text: mayāpi sadvaidyahitāya nūnaṃ pradarśiteyaṃ khalu roganāśinī ||
children.translated_text: Indeed this disease-destroying preparation has been set forth by me also for the benefit of good physicians.
One should grind very pure <s>sūta</s> with the four salts and also with the three alkalis,
dry it, and afterward grind it equally with these: <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>rājikā</s>, and dry ginger.

children.text: rasena sārdhaṃ hi kumārikāyā mūṣāṃ vidadhyādravigharmaśoṣitām
children.translated_text: With the juice of <s>kumārikā</s>, one should make a crucible and dry it in the heat of the sun.

children.text: tasyāṃ nidhāyātha rasasya golakaṃ taṃ sveditaṃ cāmlarasena samyak ||
children.translated_text: Then, placing in it the ball of <s>rasa</s>, one should properly steam that ball with sour liquid.
After eight watches in a fire-heated <s>dolā</s> apparatus, it is next triturated with juices,
namely with the juices of <s>bhekaparṇī</s>, <s>uruvu</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, ginger, and <s>girikarṇikā</s>,
with the liquids of <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>javibhaktikā</s>, <s>dhūrtaja</s>, and <s>jayantikā</s>,
and ground for three days on a smooth mortar-stone with the juice of <s>sindhuvāra</s>.

children.text: pratirasaṃ ca viśoṣya hi bhakṣayedraktikādvayamitaṃ rujāpaham
children.translated_text: After drying it after each juice, one should consume a two-<s>raktikā</s> measure; it removes pain and disease.
When ground with the biles of peacock, buffalo, and boar, and with the fluid of tortoise,
it becomes still greater in virtue and overcomes fainting produced by the combined humors.

children.text: yaḥ śrīsūtavarasya sevanamidaṃ nityaṃ karotīha vai dīrghāyurdhanadhānyadharmasahitaḥ prāpnoti saukhyaṃ param
children.translated_text: Whoever here regularly undertakes this use of excellent, auspicious <s>sūta</s> obtains long life, wealth, grain, righteousness, and supreme happiness.

children.text: loke kīrtiparaṃparāṃ vitanute dharme matirjāyate prānte tasya parā gatirhi niyataṃ satyaṃ śivenoditam ||
children.translated_text: He spreads a lineage of fame in the world, his mind inclines toward <s>dharma</s>, and at the end his highest destiny is assured; this truth was spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.
Now, therefore, I shall explain the purification and calcination of metals,
partly as experienced by me and partly in accordance with the śāstras.
Gold and silver are declared to be pure metals.
Copper, <s>aśmasāra</s>, lead, and tin likewise
are described by knowers of <s>rasa</s> as the second class, the base metals.
The mixed metals are the triad called <s>saurāṣṭra</s>, <s>rīti</s>, and <s>vartaka</s>.

children.text: ete'ṣṭau dhātavo jñeyā lohānyevaṃ bhavanti hi ||
children.translated_text: These are to be known as the eight <s>dhātus</s>; thus they are the metals.
Gold is to be known as twofold: produced from <s>rasa</s> and arising from mines.

children.text: anye trayaḥ suvarṇasya prakārāḥ santi noditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: No other three varieties of gold have been stated.
Beautiful gold produced from <s>rasa</s> arises through transmutation by <s>rasa</s>.
It possesses fourteenfold quality and is supremely capable of every operation.
In some mountains and tracts of earth, when mining is done,
mine-born gold is seen by the wise; that too has fourteenfold quality.

children.text: rūpyādiyogena yadā miśraṃ svarṇaṃ hi jāyate
children.translated_text: When gold becomes mixed through combination with silver and the like,

children.text: hemakāryaṃ na cettena tadā śodhyaṃ bhiṣagvaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: if gold-work cannot be done with it, then it should be purified by excellent physicians.
One should have sheets made from gold of deficient quality,
and grind powdered chalk and salt thoroughly with sour gruel.
Then one should carefully coat the sheets with that paste.
A furnace-pit, not too broad, should be made with <s>āraṇyotpala</s> fuel-cakes.
After placing that sealed capsule in the middle, one should then kindle the fire.

children.text: evaṃ puṭatrayaṃ dattvā śuddhaṃ hema samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: After giving three <s>puṭas</s> in this way, one should take out the purified gold.

children.text: na tu śuddhasya hemnaśca śodhanaṃ kārayedbhiṣak
children.translated_text: But a physician should not perform purification on gold that is already pure.
A physician should perform purification only on the other metals.

children.text: tataḥ svarṇabhavaṃ patraṃ tāpitaṃ hi vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: Next, a sheet made of gold should be heated and placed
in the juice of <s>jvālāmukhī</s>; by six <s>puṭas</s> it becomes fully reduced to ash.

children.text: guruṇā kathitaṃ samyak nirutthaṃ jāyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: As properly taught by the guru, it certainly becomes <s>niruttha</s>, incapable of revival,
and it destroys all diseases; no doubt should be entertained here.
One should have fine sheets of gold made, thin enough to be pierced by a needle.
After coating them with <s>sūta</s>-ash mixed in aged water, one should dry them.

children.text: saṃpuṭe ca tato rundhyāt puṭayeddaśabhiḥ puṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then one should seal them in a closed capsule and heat them with ten <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: mriyate nātra saṃdeho nirutthaṃ bhasma jāyate ||
children.translated_text: The metal is calcined, there is no doubt; a <s>niruttha</s> ash is produced.
Taking fine leaves of gold resembling birch bark, one should coat them
with equal parts of <s>vajrī</s> latex, <s>hiṅgu</s>, and <s>hiṅgula</s>, ground together in one place.

children.text: satyaṃ saṃpuṭake nidhāya daśabhiścaivaṃ puṭaiḥ kukkuṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: Truly, after placing it in a sealed capsule, it should be cooked in this way with ten <s>kukkuṭa-puṭas</s>.

children.text: pācyaṃ hema ca raktagairikasamaṃ saṃjāyate niścitam ||
children.translated_text: The gold certainly becomes like red ocher.
Dead <s>sūta</s>, bound as an iron <s>parpaṭikā</s> and taken in an equal portion,
when cast into melted gold, becomes radiant like gold ash.
That ash, combined with <s>darada</s>, should be ground with <s>puratoya</s>

children.text: mardayed dinam ekaṃ tu saṃpuṭe dhārayettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for one day; then it should be kept in a sealed capsule.
When heated ten times, the gold becomes like vermilion.

children.text: jāyate nātra saṃdeho raṃjanaṃ kurute dhruvam
children.translated_text: There is no doubt here; it certainly produces tincturing.

children.text: dehaṃ lohaṃ ca matimān sudhanī sādhayedidam ||
children.translated_text: A wise man with sufficient wealth should accomplish this for the perfection of the body and of metals.

children.text: etatsvarṇabhavaṃ karoti ca rajaḥ saundaryatāṃ vai sadā
children.translated_text: This powder produced from gold always brings about beauty,
and it destroys all diseases caused by divine forces, as well as those arising from the three humors.

children.text: yaḥ seveta naraḥ samān dvidaśakān vṛddhaśca no jāyate
children.translated_text: A man who uses it for twenty years does not become old,

children.text: doṣāścaiva garodbhavā viṣakṛtā āgantujā naiva hi ||
children.translated_text: and disorders born of slow poison, caused by poison, or arising adventitiously do not occur.

children.text: rūpyaṃ ca trividhaṃ proktaṃ khanijaṃ sahajaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Silver is said to be threefold: mine-born, natural,

children.text: kṛtrimaṃ ca trayo bhedāḥ kathitāḥ pūrvasūribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and artificial; these three divisions have been taught by the earlier sages.

children.text: bhūdhare kutra cetprāptaṃ khanyamāne ca khanijam
children.translated_text: That which is found somewhere in a mountain when mining is done is mine-born.
That which arises from the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s> is declared natural.
That which is produced from tin through transmutation by <s>rasa</s> is considered artificial.

children.text: yadrūpyaṃ vahninā taptam ujjvalaṃ hi viniḥsaret
children.translated_text: Whatever silver, when heated by fire, comes out bright,
that is pure, refined silver and supremely effective for every operation.

children.text: tāmrādisaṃsargabhavaṃ tvaśuddhaṃ rūpyaṃ hi miśraṃ khalu doṣalaṃ ca
children.translated_text: But silver made impure by contact with copper and the like is certainly mixed and faulty.

children.text: tacchodhayedvai bhasitasya mūṣyāṃ sīsena sārdhaṃ rajataṃ tu dhmāpayet ||
children.translated_text: One should purify it: the silver should be smelted with lead in an ash-lined crucible.
A wise man should carefully smelt <s>nāga</s> (lead), six times the amount of the <s>tāra</s> (silver).
When it is blown on slowly, it becomes free from defects.
By this same procedure one should always purify silver.
It is to be used in every operation and brings about every success.
One part silver and four parts <s>sūta</s> (mercury)
should be ground continuously for one day with <s>nimbu</s> juice.
From the grinding a <s>piṣṭi</s> (amalgam paste) certainly forms in one day.

children.text: mūṣāmadhye tu tāṃ muktvā adhordhvaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: After placing that in the middle of a crucible, one should set sulfur below and above it.
It should stand inside a sand apparatus and be cooked for one day
with strong fire and care, then allowed to become cool by itself.
Having ground it on a stone slab together with <s>tālaka</s> and sour liquid,
one should then give it twelve <s>puṭas</s> (heating cycles).

children.text: anena vidhinā samyak rajataṃ mriyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: By this method silver is certainly killed, that is, fully calcined.
One should grind powder of <s>tāra</s> (silver) and <s>mākṣika</s> with sour liquid.
With twenty <s>puṭas</s>, that silver surely becomes ash.

children.text: puṭādhikyaṃ hi lohānāṃ samyak syād guṇakāri ca
children.translated_text: An increase in <s>puṭas</s> for metals is indeed proper and productive of good qualities.
It brings about very strong coloring; a red product is said to tend toward whiteness.
Purified silver made into ash, combined with <s>sāraghājya</s>,
always destroys eye diseases, and also disorders born of sneezing and disorders of the rectum;
those born of <s>pitta</s>, those produced by cough, <s>pāṇḍu</s>, and abdominal diseases,
and all those born of the <s>doṣas</s>; it always destroys loss of appetite.

children.text: tāmraṃ cāpi dvidhā proktaṃ nepālaṃ mlecchadeśajam
children.translated_text: Copper too is said to be twofold: from <s>Nepāla</s> and from <s>mleccha</s> lands.
The learned call copper other than that from the land of <s>Nepāla</s> '<s>mleccha</s>'.
One should purify copper with an equal amount of lead, just as silver is purified.
Afterwards proper killing, or calcination, should be performed by the knower of <s>rasa</s>.
Having made sheets of copper, one should put them in leaves of <s>kanyā</s>.
Immediately after that one should heat them properly in the <s>puṭa</s> called <s>kukkuṭa</s>.
A very pleasing <s>piṣṭi</s> of <s>sūta</s> and sulfur should be prepared.
After grinding it with <s>nimbu</s> water, one should coat those sheets.
Then one should seal them inside a pot and cook them for four <s>yāmas</s>.
By that very process the copper becomes free from the five defects.
With potent <s>sūta</s> equal in amount to the copper,
with <s>tālaka</s> half as much and <s>śilā</s> half as much,
the discerning physician should make a powder black like collyrium.
After carefully placing the sheets inside a closed pair of earthen saucers,
one should lay the sheets and the <s>kajjalī</s> one above another.
One should cook them in the fire for one <s>yāma</s>, inside the chamber of a <s>garbha-yantra</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out and pulverize it finely in a mortar.
It should be licked with honey and with suitable accompanying vehicles.
Sheets of purified copper should be carefully made.
Sulfur equal in amount to that and mercury equal in amount to it should be taken,
along with <s>tālaka</s> half that amount and <s>śilā</s> half that amount.
Also <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>tālamūlī</s>, and <s>karañja</s>,
with equal parts of <s>viṣa</s>, <s>śamyāka</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, and rock salt,
and then the powder should be made very liquid with the juice of <s>jambīra</s>.
All of that should be carefully placed in a stone vessel.
The sheets, thin enough to be pierced by a needle and coated with the <s>rasa</s>,
should be inserted into the middle of the paste for exactly seven days.
Then, when powdered and combined with honey, ghee, and two <s>kaṇās</s>,
