and licked in a dose of one <s>valla</s>, it destroys old age and death.
This auspicious preparation, named <s>Somanātha</s>, was taught by <s>Somadeva</s>.

children.text: śuddhaṃ śulvaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ vai samāṃśaṃ pūrvaṃ sthālyāṃ sthāpayedgaṃdhakārdham
children.translated_text: Pure copper and sulfur should be equal in quantity; first one should place half the sulfur in a pot.

children.text: madhye śulbaṃ sthāpanīyaṃ prayatnāttasyordhvaṃ vai gaṃdhacūrṇasya cārdham ||
children.translated_text: The copper is to be carefully placed in the middle, and above it the other half of the sulfur powder.

children.text: sthālīmukhe cūrṇaghaṭīṃ niveśya lepaṃ tathā saindhavamṛtsnayāpi
children.translated_text: Having set a small vessel for the powder at the mouth of the pot, one should seal it with a paste of rock salt and clay.

children.text: cullyāṃ ca kuryādatha vahnimeva yāmatrayeṇaiva supācitaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should put it on a hearth and apply fire; in three <s>yāmas</s> it becomes well cooked.

children.text: śītībhūtaṃ doṣahīnaṃ tadeva kṛtvā cūrṇaṃ gālitaṃ vastrakhaṇḍe
children.translated_text: Once cooled and free from defects, that same substance should be powdered and strained through a piece of cloth.

children.text: sevyaṃ samyak caikavallapramāṇaṃ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ hanti gulmapramehān ||
children.translated_text: Taken properly in a dose of one <s>valla</s>, it destroys cough, dyspnea, <s>gulma</s>, and <s>prameha</s>.
One <s>valla</s> of copper ash should be taken in the forenoon by order of a physician.

children.text: pariṇāmabhavaṃ śūlaṃ tathā cāṣṭavidhaṃ ca ruk
children.translated_text: It conquers colic arising during digestion, and also the eight kinds of pain,
abdominal disease, <s>pāṇḍu</s>, swelling, <s>gulma</s>, diseases of the spleen and liver, and wasting,
disorders caused by weak digestive fire and wasting, urinary disorders and the like, and diseases of the <s>grahaṇī</s>.
According to the different accompanying vehicles, it conquers many kinds of diseases.
Together with long pepper and honey, it is the supreme remover of all <s>doṣas</s>.
It also destroys hemorrhoids, indigestion, fever, and the like; it is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It destroys enlargement, dyspnea, and cough, and it removes old age and death.

children.text: yathottaraṃ syād guṇavarṇahīnaṃ prakāśitaṃ vaidyavareṇa samyak
children.translated_text: In the order that follows, each is deficient in quality and color; this has been properly explained by the best of physicians.

children.text: kāṃtaṃ tathā tīkṣṇavaraṃ hi muṇḍaṃ lohaṃ bhavedvai trividhaṃ krameṇa ||
children.translated_text: Iron is indeed threefold in sequence: <s>kānta</s>, excellent <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s>.

children.text: kāṃtaṃ caturdhā kila kathyate'tra tadromakaṃ bhrāmakacumbake ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> is said here to be fourfold: <s>romaka</s>, <s>bhrāmaka</s>, and <s>cumbaka</s>.

children.text: saṃdrāvakaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ tathā hi saṃkathyate śāstravidai rasajñaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, indeed, it is described by knowers of the śāstra and experts in <s>rasa</s> as the very best liquefying agent.
When a mine is being dug, the stones that come out
and the metal smelted from them are called <s>romaka</s> iron.

children.text: yatra kvāpi girau śreṣṭhe labhyate bhrāmakopalaḥ
children.translated_text: Wherever, on some excellent mountain, a <s>bhrāmaka</s> stone is found,
the iron produced from that is called <s>bhrāmaka</s> here.
On the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain there is a stone, wondrous, which attracts iron
and never releases it, just as a devotee does not abandon devotion to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: himādrau labhyate duḥkhād yaḥ spṛṣṭo drāvayedayaḥ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Himādri</s> a stone is found with difficulty which, when touched, liquefies iron
and likewise gold and the other metals; that <s>kānta</s> is a liquefying agent.

children.text: śuddhe kāṃtabhave pātre śṛtaṃ dugdhaṃ hi nodgiret
children.translated_text: Milk boiled in a vessel made from pure <s>kānta</s> does not boil over.
Water boiled in it becomes like the smell of <s>hiṅgu</s>.
A drop of oil cast into water does not spread out very much,
nor does a coating form; this is the sign of pure <s>kānta</s>.
<s>Tīkṣṇa</s> iron is a hundred times superior to <s>muṇḍa</s>, and <s>kānta</s> has great virtues beyond <s>tīkṣṇa</s>.
<s>Cumbaka</s> and <s>drāvaka</s> are likewise said to have virtues counted by crores.
When coated with hare's blood and heated seven times,
all metals beginning with <s>kānta</s> are certainly purified; there is no doubt.
Similarly, when coated with sea salt and quenched in <s>triphalā</s> water,
it becomes pure, as surely as the word of the guru is true.

children.text: lohacūrṇaṃ ghṛtāktaṃ hi kṣiptvā lohasya kharpare
children.translated_text: Iron powder, anointed with ghee, should be placed in an iron pan,
and it should be stirred with a ladle until it has the glow and color of fire.

children.text: khalve ca vipacettadvat pañcavāram ataḥ param
children.translated_text: Then it should be cooked in the mortar in the same way five times; after that,
the iron should be given four <s>puṭas</s> with excellent liquids.
When well ground, it becomes able to float on water; there is no doubt here.
By this method the preparation of all kinds of iron should be carried out.
When administered, it cures all diseases and removes grey hair.
Take two <s>palas</s> of iron powder, with jaggery and sulfur in equal parts,
grind them very thoroughly in a mortar, and give twenty <s>puṭas</s>.
The grinding must be done first, and the <s>puṭa</s> is given afterward.
By this method it certainly becomes ash properly,
and it surely destroys all diseases; no doubt should be entertained here.
Ten <s>puṭas</s> should then be given with the water of white <s>punarnavā</s> leaves,
and it becomes like vermilion in color.
Now another method for the calcination of iron is taught here.
Sulfur equal to the iron powder should be ground with the juices of <s>kanyakā</s>.
Made into a lump, it should be placed in an iron vessel and kept in the shade for a long time.

children.text: mriyate nātra saṃdeho hyanubhūtaṃ mayaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: It is calcined; there is no doubt here, for this has been experienced by me myself.
A wise man should use the <s>niruttha</s> ash produced from iron here,
mixed with <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>vellā</s>, ghee, and honey in the measure of a <s>ṭaṅka</s>.
It destroys old age, death, and disease, and it grants sons.
It destroys the diseases of embodied beings that arise from the faults of old age.

children.text: baṃgaṃ tu dvividhaṃ proktaṃ khuraṃ miśraṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Tin is said to be twofold: <s>khura</s> and <s>miśra</s>.
That which is pure, straight, and white is called <s>khura</s>.
<s>Khura</s> tin is purified when melted down in oil made from <s>bhallātaka</s>.
<s>Miśra</s> tin, poured out with <s>punarnavā</s>, rock-salt powder, and <s>viṣa</s>,

children.text: takramadhye trivāraṃ hi miśraṃ baṃgaṃ viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: is purified when poured three times into buttermilk.
After making a hollow on top of a dung cake, one should put in powdered tamarind bark.
A tin disk weighing one <s>karṣa</s> should be placed on top of it.
Then the disk, wrapped with four times as much material, should be held there,
and afterward a <s>puṭa</s>-fire should be given with dried goat dung.
When it has cooled of itself, one should take it out and employ it in all operations.
By this method one should certainly calcine the remaining, uncooked portion.

children.text: athāparaḥ prakāro hi vakṣyate cādhunā mayā
children.translated_text: Now another method will be explained by me at this point.
One should make even sheets of purified tin.

children.text: ajāśakṛt varā tulyā cūrṇitā ca niśā tathā
children.translated_text: Goat dung, <s>varā</s>, and likewise turmeric should be powdered in equal measure.
Then one should make a square, sunken pit measuring one cubit.
The physician should constantly fill half of it with goat-dung cakes.
Then the pit should be covered with cloth made of hemp,

children.text: pūrvaṃ prakalpitaṃ cūrṇaṃ tatropari ca vinyaset
children.translated_text: and the powder prepared earlier should be spread upon it.

children.text: tasyopari ca patrāṇi samāni parito nyaset ||
children.translated_text: On top of that, the even sheets should be placed all around.
After carefully covering them with the powder, one should then fill it with goat dung.
It should be heated properly with fire and taken out when it has cooled of itself.
Afterward the dead tin should be ground with <s>pūra</s> water.
An equal portion of <s>rasasindūra</s> should be mixed with it.
After grinding it very firmly in a mortar, one should place it in a glass bottle.
It should be cooked by the application of fire for a measure of sixteen <s>yāmas</s>.
Dead tin with the luster of gold is produced; it is <s>rasavaṅgaka</s>.
Tin is vāta-producing, dry, bitter, and destructive of <s>meha</s> disorders.
It destroys diseases of fat and worms, and removes kapha-doṣa and poison.
It quickly removes all diseases, gives strength, and is rich in virtues.
After considering the disease and the patient's strength, it should be given in a dose of one <s>valla</s>.
It destroys the eighty diseases born of vāta and also the twenty <s>mehas</s>,
merely by being eaten in a single seven-day course, and not otherwise.
Tin is vāta-producing and dry, and is said to destroy <s>meha</s> disorders.
It destroys worm and fat disorders, and removes kapha-doṣa and poison.

children.text: chede kṛṣṇaṃ guru snigdhaṃ drutadrāvam athojjvalam
children.translated_text: When cut, it is black, heavy, unctuous, quickly melting, and bright.
A <s>nāga</s> (lead) that is black in color outside and pure is wholesome; otherwise it is the opposite.
One should break down the lead in the juices of <s>sinduvāra</s> and <s>haridrā</s>.
Thus the lead becomes completely purified and does not cause fainting, eruptions, and the like.
One should then have thin sheets made from purified lead, with their layers intact.
One should grind <s>śilā</s> with the juice of <s>vāsā</s> for one <s>yāma</s> (three-hour period).
With that paste one should coat the sheets; then one should place them in a sealed <s>saṃpuṭa</s>.
The wise man should cook them with a <s>vārāha-puṭa</s>, using an intense fire.
When this has been done three times, ash of lead is produced.
Now, by another method, the killing of lead is accomplished.

children.text: lohapātre drute nāge gharṣaṇaṃ tu prakārayet ||
children.translated_text: When the lead has melted in an iron vessel, one should perform rubbing.
It should be done carefully for four <s>yāmas</s> with roots produced from <s>palāśa</s>.
One should properly kindle a forced, intense fire underneath; it certainly dies.
A red-colored powder is produced; one should employ it in all operations.
In all operations it always becomes an eradicator of disease.
The killing of lead has been taught in many ways by many wise men.
In every respect there is no killing of <s>sūta</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>Śambhu</s>.
It destroys <s>prameha</s>, diseases born of <s>vāta</s>, and disorders such as <s>dhanurvāta</s>,
as well as the twenty diseases born of <s>śleṣman</s>; there is no doubt.
<s>Pittala</s> (brass) is said to be twofold: <s>rītikā</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍikā</s>.

children.text: taptā tuṣajale kṣiptā śuklavarṇā tu rītikā ||
children.translated_text: When heated and thrown into husk-water, the white-colored variety is <s>rītikā</s>.

children.text: nikṣiptā kāṃjike kṛṣṇā sā smṛtā kākatuṇḍikā ||
children.translated_text: When placed in sour gruel and black, it is remembered as <s>kākatuṇḍikā</s>.
If it is yellowish, soft, heavy, sound-bodied, and golden in color,

children.text: masṛṇāṅgī tu susnigdhā śubhā rītīti kathyate ||
children.translated_text: smooth-limbed and very glossy, it is called excellent <s>rīti</s>.

children.text: durgandhā pūtigandhā vā kharasparśā ca pāṇḍurā
children.translated_text: If it has a bad or putrid smell, is rough to the touch and pale,
unable to withstand heavy hammering and dry, <s>rīti</s> is not desired in <s>rasāyana</s>.
It is to be heated and carefully cast into the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>;
after five times, <s>rīti</s> attains purification immediately.
With the very well-ground essences of <s>śilā</s>, <s>gandhaka</s>, and <s>sindhūttha</s>,
the sheets of <s>rīti</s> should be coated and then subjected to <s>puṭa</s> eight times.
They at once become ash; afterward they are to be used in <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Rītikā</s> is considered to check <s>raktapitta</s>, to be dry, and to kill worms.
<s>Kākatuṇḍā</s> is considered to remove skin disease, to have hot potency, and to be moving or laxative.
With four parts of <s>ravi</s> (copper) and one part of excellent tin,
superior <s>kāṃsya</s> (bronze) is produced; that born in <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is good.

children.text: taptaṃ kāṃsyaṃ gavāṃ mūtre saptavāreṇa śudhyati
children.translated_text: Heated <s>kāṃsya</s> is purified by seven immersions in cow's urine.
It is killed with <s>haritāla</s> and <s>gandhaka</s> by five <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: mṛtaṃ kāṃsyaṃ vātaharaṃ pramehāṇāṃ ca nāśanam
children.translated_text: Dead <s>kāṃsya</s> removes <s>vāta</s> and destroys <s>prameha</s>.

children.text: śuddhe kāṃsyabhave pātre sarvameva hi bhojanam
children.translated_text: In a purified vessel made of <s>kāṃsya</s>, indeed all food
becomes wholesome, provided it is not sour and excludes ghee, greens, and the like.
What is produced from iron, <s>kāṃsya</s>, copper, and <s>rīti</s> is <s>vartaloha</s>.
That same thing is called <s>viḍaloha</s> by the learned.
When thoroughly melted and cast into horse urine, it attains purification.
Subjected to <s>puṭa</s> with <s>gandhatāla</s>, <s>vartaloha</s> is killed.
It removes <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is sour and appetizing, and also kills worms.
It pacifies eye disease and removes diseases of the throat.

children.text: pathyaṃ sarvaṃ hi tadbhāṇḍe sarvadoṣaharaṃ param
children.translated_text: All food in that vessel is wholesome and an excellent remover of all <s>doṣas</s>.
Except for alkali and sour substances, it produces appetite and is an excellent digestive.
The purifications and the killings, and the merits and faults, have been stated by me.

children.text: anyāni śāstrāṇi suvistarāṇi nirīkṣya yatnātkṛtameva samyak ||
children.translated_text: Having carefully examined other very extensive treatises, I have indeed done this correctly.
Now I shall describe the <s>mahārasas</s>, because of the superiority of their qualities;
their names, classes, <s>sattvas</s> (extractable essences), and their qualities.

children.text: krameṇa gaganaṃ tāpyaṃ vaikrāṃtaṃ vimalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: In order, there are <s>gagana</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, and likewise <s>vimala</s>,
<s>rasaka</s>, <s>śailasaṃbhūta</s>, <s>rājāvartaka</s>, and <s>sasyaka</s>;
these eight <s>mahārasas</s> have been stated by the experts in <s>rasa</s>.
Having reached it in sequence, I shall describe <s>gagana</s>; <s>gagana</s> is fourfold:

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ paramasuṃdaram ||
children.translated_text: white, red, yellow, and black, each supremely beautiful.

children.text: śvetaṃ śvetakriyāyogyaṃ raktaṃ pītaṃ hi pītakṛt
children.translated_text: The white is suitable for white operations; the red and yellow indeed produce yellow effects.
Black mica is always the supreme destroyer of all diseases.
The varieties are called <s>vajra</s>, <s>pināka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>maṇḍūka</s>.

children.text: anena vidhinā proktā bhedāḥ santīha ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: By this method the divisions here are said to be sixteen.
Of all micas, the <s>vajra</s> variety alone is always best.

children.text: śeṣāṇi trīṇi cābhrāṇi ghorān vyādhīn sṛjanti hi
children.translated_text: The remaining three micas indeed give rise to terrible diseases;
therefore good physicians should always carefully avoid them.

children.text: vajrābhraṃ dhamyamāne'gnau vikṛtiṃ na kvacid bhajet
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrābhra</s>, when blown in fire, nowhere undergoes alteration.

children.text: sevitaṃ tanmṛtiṃ hanti vajrābhaṃ kurute vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: When used, it destroys death and makes the body diamond-like.
<s>Pinākābhra</s>, heated by fire, releases a mass of layers.
When used for one month, it readily causes worms and skin disease.

children.text: nāgābhraṃ dhmāpitaṃ samyak nāgavat sphūrjate dhruvam
children.translated_text: <s>Nāgābhra</s>, when properly blown in fire, certainly crackles like lead.
When used, it brings about the arising of wasting disease.
Poison, the <s>hālāhala</s>, when drunk, certainly kills;
likewise this one called <s>nāgābhra</s>, a good physician declares sufficiently.
<s>Maṇḍūkābhra</s>, when constantly heated, behaves in this way:

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ cāgnau na tiṣṭheta maṃḍūkasadṛśāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: it does not remain in the fire even for a moment, moving like a frog.

children.text: maṃḍūkābhraṃ na sevyaṃ hi kathitaṃ rasavedibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇḍūkābhra</s> is not to be used; this has been stated by knowers of <s>rasa</s>.
One should sweat <s>abhraka</s> (mica) for one day with <s>kāñjika</s>,
then with a decoction of <s>kulattha</s>, with buttermilk, with urine, and then by fire.
When it has been cooked and is free from defects, it certainly attains purification.
Likewise, after heating it thoroughly in the fire, one should quench it seven times.

children.text: kāṃjike cāpi nirdoṣam abhrake jāyate dhruvam
children.translated_text: In sour gruel too, <s>abhraka</s> certainly becomes faultless.

children.text: varākvāthe tathā dugdhe gavāṃ mūtre tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Likewise in a decoction of <s>varā</s>, in milk, and also in cow's urine,
and also with the juice of <s>mārkava</s>, it becomes free from defects.
Then, after making it into a fine powder and grinding it with juices of <s>haṃsapadī</s>,
one should form it into round cakes, dry them, and place them in the <s>ardhagaja</s>-type <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: ṣaṭ puṭāni tato dattvā punarevaṃ punarnavā
children.translated_text: After then giving six <s>puṭas</s>, again in the same way with <s>punarnavā</s>,
one should grind it hard with its juice, adding <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) in a fraction of the <s>abhraka</s>.
Again making it into little cakes, one should indeed heat it with <s>puṭas</s> seven times,
with juice of <s>taṇḍulīya</s>, and likewise with juice of <s>vāsā</s>.
One should heat it seven times, giving a half-<s>gaja</s> <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: anena vidhinā cābhraṃ mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: By this method <s>abhraka</s> is calcined; there is no doubt here.
Properly bereft of its glitter, it becomes like vermilion.
Excellent <s>dhānyābhra</s>, cooked in the juice of <s>kāsamarda</s>,
is calcined in a hundred repetitions; no deliberation should be made about this.
In the same way, also with juice of <s>mustā</s> and with juices of <s>taṇḍulīya</s> root,
after grinding the <s>abhraka</s> with an equal amount of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, one makes it into round cakes.
Cooked with sixty <s>puṭas</s>, it becomes like vermilion.
The <s>abhraka</s> certainly becomes destructive of diseases such as skin disease and consumption.
With juices of <s>nāgavallī</s> leaves and with bark of the banyan root,
with <s>vṛṣā</s> and <s>matsyādanī</s>, with <s>matsyākṣī</s> and <s>punarbhū</s>,
and ground with the root of the banyan tree, dense <s>abhraka</s>, when heated,
becomes vermilion-like in color at the twentieth <s>puṭa</s>.
Very fine, floating on water, and shining with a red color,
it becomes a remover of all diseases after many <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: mṛtaṃ vajrābhrakaṃ samyak sevanīyaṃ sadā budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Properly calcined <s>vajrābhraka</s> should always be used by the wise,
for the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and for firmness of the body.
It removes every disease, pacifies the three humors, and kindles the digestive fire;
this supreme substance increases retention of virility and removes diseases such as dysuria.
It wards off possession and madness, produces memory, and destroys swelling disorders;

children.text: sadyaḥ prāṇavivardhanaṃ jvaraharaṃ sevyaṃ sadā cābhrakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>abhraka</s> should always be used, for it at once increases life-force and removes fever.

children.text: yathā viṣaṃ yathā vajraṃ śastro 'gniḥ prāṇahṛdyathā
children.translated_text: As poison, as a diamond, as a weapon, and as fire take life,
so, in its qualities, is <s>abhraka</s> that still has glitter when eaten.
After adding one quarter part <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and grinding it with <s>musalī</s> juice,
when it is blown in the <s>koṣṭhikā</s> apparatus it becomes <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence).

children.text: khalve piṣṭvā tu matimān sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: A wise man should grind it in a mortar and make it into a fine powder.
After filtering it through a piece of cloth and saturating it with ghee,
it should be fried ten times in an iron pan.
He should grind and fry it until it becomes the color of fire.
After grinding it to the color of a parrot's feather in a decoction made from banyan root,
one should then heat it twenty times with <s>puṭas</s> called <s>śūkara</s>.
The wise physician should do likewise with decoctions of <s>varā</s>.
He should thoroughly impregnate it with roots of <s>nīlī</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, <s>varā</s>, and <s>pathyā</s>.
When it is well dried, the learned man may consume it; it is the supreme remover of all diseases.
There is no unsurpassed <s>rasāyana</s> beyond <s>abhrasattva</s>.
If one cooks <s>abhraka</s> a hundred times with intense fire,
then it becomes like nectar, supreme in bringing about transformation of the body and metals.
Then, having prepared <s>dhānyābhraka</s> in the measure of thirty-two <s>palas</s>,
one should make lac, <s>guñjā</s>, small fish, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and sheep's milk,
mustard seeds, oilcake of <s>śigru</s>, rock salt, deer horn,

children.text: mākṣikaṃ ca samāṃśāni sarvāṇyeva tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>mākṣika</s> all in equal portions.
The wise physician should grind them with an equal amount of <s>dhānyābhraka</s>,
with the separate juices of <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>kāsamarda</s>, and rice,
with those of <s>matsyākṣī</s>, <s>haṃsapadī</s>, and <s>kāravellī</s>, each separately;
with powders of oilcake and wheat he should make good pellets.
Afterwards he should heat those dried pellets in a furnace with a pair of bellows.

children.text: khadirasya tu cāṃgāraiḥ satvaṃ niḥsarati dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: With charcoal of khadira, the <s>sattva</s> certainly comes out.

children.text: pṛthak kṛtvā tu ravakān kāṃsyavarṇān viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Having separated the grains, especially those bronze-colored ones,
he should then mix the slag with cow dung and again make pellets.

children.text: dhmāpayet pūrvavidhinā punaḥ satvaṃ hi niḥsaret
children.translated_text: He should blow them in the previous manner; the <s>sattva</s> will again come out.
This method should be performed with it mixed with <s>pañcagavya</s>.
Then do the same with the five goat-products and with the five buffalo-products.
In this way it falls out without doubt, as true as the guru's word.
Next, the grains of <s>abhrasattva</s> should be cooked with the acidic group.
They should be purified in a crucible with the purifying group itself.
One should indeed purify them with glass, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>guñjā</s>, ghee, and <s>sāragha</s>.
One should quench them ten times in honey, oil, muscle-fat, and ghee.
This procedure always truly produces softness in the <s>sattva</s>.
Thus the balls of <s>sattva</s> should be heated and then, in this way, in sour gruel,
quenched; immediately one should pound them with an iron pestle.
By this very method one should make them into a fine powder.

children.text: bharjayed ghṛtamadhye tu trīṇi vārāṇi yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: One should carefully fry it in ghee three times,
and the grinding should be carefully done on a stone slab.
Also with the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> leaves, or with the juice of its fruit,
with <s>punarbhū</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, sour gruel, and then sulfurs,
one should heat it ten times with <s>puṭas</s>; the <s>abhrasattva</s> is calcined.
The calcined <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) wards off death and destroys all diseases,

children.text: kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ grahaṇikāṃ śvāsaṃ śūlaṃ sakāmalam ||
children.translated_text: including consumption, <s>pāṇḍu</s>, <s>grahaṇikā</s>, dyspnea, and colic together with jaundice;
also fevers, urinary disorders, and coughs, and even the five kinds of <s>gulma</s> (abdominal masses),
weak digestion, abdominal diseases, and various sorts of piles.
Through the use of an appropriate <s>anupāna</s> (vehicle), it destroys all diseases.
The qualities of <s>abhrasattva</s> (mica essence) cannot be stated in brief.
Somewhat red, or blue, and always shining with a mixed color,

children.text: taulye guruśca masṛṇo rājāvartto varaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: heavy when weighed and smooth: this is remembered as excellent <s>rājāvarta</s>.
Steamed with cow urine, with alkalis, and likewise with sour liquids,
<s>rājāvarta</s> and the other <s>rasas</s> (minerals) are purified by three repetitions.
Powdered with <s>śukapiccha</s> and with the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>,
<s>rājāvarta</s>, heated in seven <s>puṭas</s> (calcining heats), will be calcined.
It removes phlegm, <s>prameha</s>, bad piles, <s>pāṇḍu</s>, and consumption;
it digests and kindles appetite, is aphrodisiac, and removes wind and poison.
<s>Kośātakī</s>, <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, and likewise barren <s>karkoṭakī</s>,
<s>kākamācī</s>, royal <s>śamī</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and household soot:
<s>rājāvarta</s>, triturated with the juices of these, releases its <s>sattva</s> (essence)
when smelted with <s>khadira</s> charcoal and with a pair of bellows.
Having eight edges and lip-like plates, six-cornered, smooth, and heavy,
and endowed with pure and mixed colors, it is called <s>vaikrānta</s>.
White, yellow, black, blue, pigeon-hued,
mottled, and dark-colored: <s>vaikrānta</s> is remembered as eightfold.

children.text: kvāthe kulatthaje svinno vaikrāṃtaḥ śudhyati dhruvam
children.translated_text: Steamed in a decoction of <s>kulattha</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s> is certainly purified;
ground with sulfur and lemon juice and calcined, it is surely reduced to ash.
It grants long life, pacifies the three doṣas, is aphrodisiac, and always gives vital breath;
it gives vigor, produces potency, and indeed brings intelligence and complexion.
Among all <s>rasāyanas</s> it is foremost and removes disease;
acting like diamond in its qualities, <s>vaikrānta</s> binds <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
When it is rubbed in the sun with the herbs of the <s>sattvapātana</s> group,
dried, made into pills, placed in a crucible, and then smelted,

children.text: satvaṃ muñcati vaikrāṃtaḥ satyaṃ guruvaco yathā
children.translated_text: <s>vaikrānta</s> releases its <s>sattva</s>; this is true, just as the guru's word.
The <s>sattva</s> arising from <s>vaikrānta</s>, in an equal part with calcined <s>sūta</s> (mercury),
combined with calcined <s>abhrasattva</s> and triturated in equal measure,
mixed with long pepper, honey, and ghee, and taken in a <s>valla</s>-measure,
quickly destroys all diseases; one lives happily for a hundred years.
Certainly, by use for three years, it destroys wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: sadyo hālāhalaṃ pītam amṛtaṃ garuḍena ca
children.translated_text: The <s>hālāhala</s> poison was at once drunk as nectar by <s>Garuḍa</s>;
when that poison, joined with nectar, was vomited on the mountain called <s>Marut</s>,

children.text: ghanībhūtaṃ ca saṃjātaṃ sasyakaṃ khalu kathyate
children.translated_text: it solidified and came into being; that indeed is called <s>sasyaka</s>.
The blue kind, with the hue of emerald and endowed with brilliance, is praised.
Steamed with buffalo ghee and with cow urine or human urine,

children.text: dolāyantreṇa yāmau dvau śudhyatyeva hi sasyakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>sasyaka</s> is purified in a <s>dolāyantra</s> for two <s>yāmas</s>.
Ground with sulfur and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> in the liquid of <s>lakuca</s>,
it is calcined in a closed crucible with seven <s>kukkuṭa</s>-named <s>puṭas</s>.
Rubbed down with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and lemon liquid in a crucible,

children.text: dhmātaṃ ca tāmrarūpaṃ hi sattvaṃ muñcati sasyakam ||
children.translated_text: and smelted, <s>sasyaka</s> releases a <s>sattva</s> having the form of copper.
Because it is joined with poison, it therefore has qualities stronger than poison;
because that poison is joined with nectar, likewise it has qualities stronger than nectar.
It pacifies the three doṣas, removes poison, and takes away pain in the rectum;
it destroys acid dyspepsia and constipation, and is always an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: vāntiṃ karoti rekaṃ ca śvitrakuṣṭhāpahaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: It causes vomiting and purgation, and removes leucoderma and skin disease;
by the name <s>mayūratuttha</s>, it prevents every illness.
This <s>sattva</s>, combined with <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s>, should be made equal;

children.text: anayormudraikā kāryā śūlaghnī sā bhavet khalu ||
children.translated_text: one seal-ring should be made from the two, and it indeed becomes pain-relieving.
It conquers <s>ḍākinī</s>, spirit-possession, and poison from moving and unmoving beings;
a fine ring should always be prepared for the protection of kings.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is to be known as twofold, distinguished as <s>rukma</s> and <s>tāpya</s>;
the first <s>mākṣika</s>, the golden one, is produced in <s>Kānyakubja</s>.
It resembles the color of gold and is furnished with nine colors;

children.text: taṭe tapatyāḥ saṃjātaṃ tāpyākhyaṃ mākṣikaṃ vadet ||
children.translated_text: that born on the bank of the <s>Tapatī</s> is called <s>tāpya-mākṣika</s>.
Mixed with flakes of stone, pale, and as if five-colored,
this has few virtues and releases only a little <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: mūtre takre ca kaulatthe marditaṃ śuṣkameva ca
children.translated_text: Rubbed in urine, buttermilk, and a <s>kulattha</s> preparation, and then dried,
ground with sulfur and citron, and enclosed in a saucer-capsule,
it obtains calcination when burned with five <s>vārāha-puṭas</s>.
Well burned in an iron vessel and rubbed with an iron rod,
when, through lemon liquids, it becomes red and like metal,

children.text: gharṣayet triguṇaṃ sūtaṃ muktvā saṃgharṣaṇaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: one should add three times as much <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and carry out thorough rubbing.
After rubbing it for one day, one should strain it through a strong cloth.

children.text: vastrasthā piṣṭikā lagnā tvadhaḥ patati pāradaḥ
children.translated_text: The paste remains stuck in the cloth, while <s>pārada</s> (mercury) falls below.
By this very method one should strain it two or three times.
That ball of paste should be taken and placed in a <s>ḍamaruka-yantra</s>;
then one should kindle the fire below for the measure of two <s>praharas</s>.
The wise person should collect the <s>sattva</s> below, resembling an <s>indragopa</s> insect;
by this very procedure one should obtain the <s>sattva</s> of <s>tāpya</s>.
When, combined with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, it is melted in a crucible,

children.text: tadā tāmraprabhaṃ satvaṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then a copper-colored <s>sattva</s> arises; there is no doubt about this.
It is said in the <s>Devīśāstra</s> to accomplish the body and metals properly.
The supreme nectar of <s>pārada</s> (mercury) always destroys every disease.

children.text: melanaṃ kurute lohe paramaṃ ca rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: It produces combination in metal and is also an excellent <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating elixir).
The first <s>vimala</s> is golden <s>vimala</s>, endowed with a gold-like color.
The second is silver <s>vimala</s>; indeed it appears like silver.
The third is bronze <s>vimala</s>, and it has a color equal to bronze.
It is unctuous and round, six-angled, and furnished with plates.
When ground in the juice of <s>vāsā</s>, it becomes purified and exceedingly clear.
Ground with liquids of <s>gandhāśman</s> and <s>nimbuka</s> and heated in a <s>puṭa</s>, it undergoes calcination.

children.text: śṛṅgasya bhasmanā cāpi puṭaiśca daśadhā puṭet ||
children.translated_text: And with ash of horn too, one should heat it ten times by <s>puṭas</s>.
After grinding it with lemon juice and confining it inside a crucible,
<s>Vimala</s>, when blown upon, releases a <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence) resembling lead.
That <s>sattva</s>, made into a paste and combined with <s>pārada</s> (mercury),

children.text: drute gaṃdhe hi nikṣiptaṃ tālakaṃ triguṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: should be placed in molten sulfur, along with three times as much <s>tālaka</s>.
There should also be five times as much <s>manaḥśilā</s>, in a sand-bath apparatus.
One should heat it gradually, and afterward add ash of silver.
With an equal measure of <s>vaikrānta</s>, all of it should indeed be powdered.
After carefully straining it through cloth, one should place it inside a bottle.
One should apply fire for eight <s>yāmas</s>, and take it out when it has cooled by itself.
A dose the size of a <s>valla</s> should be licked with honey, mixed with <s>vyoṣa</s>.
It removes diseases of children and dispels fever, anemia, and <s>prameha</s>.
It removes <s>grahaṇī</s>, jaundice, colic, weak digestion, wasting, and pitta disorders.
With specific accompanying drinks it destroys all diseases.
It is aphrodisiac, removes pitta and wind, and is indeed the best <s>rasāyana</s>.
Among these, the first is of two kinds: possessing good <s>sattva</s> and lacking <s>sattva</s>.
Of the two, the former, richer in qualities, removes every fault.
In summer, because of intense heat, from mountains bordering the snowy region,
<s>śilājatu</s> flows forth from gold-, silver-, and copper-bearing mountains.
That born in a gold-bearing mountain is like a <s>bandhūka</s> flower, heavy, unctuous, and very cooling.
It is the supreme <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Śilāja</s> is somewhat bitter and sweet, and removes every <s>doṣa</s>.
That born from a silver-bearing mountain is pale, sweet, and cooling.
Pale <s>śilājatu</s> destroys pitta disorders, anemia, and wasting.
That born from a copper-bearing mountain is black in color, dense, and heavy.
This mountain-born substance destroys kapha and vāta and, especially, conquers every disease.
When thrown into fire, if it becomes <s>liṅga</s>-shaped and smokeless,

children.text: udake ca vilīyeta tacchuddhaṃ ca vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and if it dissolves in water, that is prescribed as pure.
With sour substances together with <s>guggulu</s>, and with alkalis and the like, inside a vessel,
<s>śilājatu</s>, steamed for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>, is purified.
With <s>manaḥśilā</s> and citron juice, or with stone and sulfur,
or else with <s>tālaka</s>, when heated in a <s>puṭa</s>, <s>śilāja</s> is certainly calcined.
When treated with eight <s>chagaṇas</s> (dung-cake fuel units), <s>śilājatu</s> becomes ash.

children.text: śilājatu tu saṃśuddhaṃ seveta yaḥ pumān sadā
children.translated_text: A man who constantly consumes well-purified <s>śilājatu</s>
lives more than a hundred years and is indeed not afflicted by diseases.
Dysuria and stone diseases surely depart; there is no doubt.
The qualities that the learned have described in the great minerals, secondary minerals, metals, gems, and <s>pārada</s>,

children.text: ye guṇāḥ kathitāḥ sadbhiḥ śilādhātau vadanti te ||
children.translated_text: they say are also present in <s>śilādhātu</s> (mineral pitch).
Combined with <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and <s>trikaṭu</s>,
one should take a <s>valla</s>-measure of it, for it removes the whole multitude of diseases.

children.text: palitaṃ valibhiḥ sārdhaṃ hanyādeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It certainly destroys gray hair together with wrinkles; there is no doubt.
The white <s>śilājatu</s>, like camphor, is called camphor-like.
It destroys stones, <s>meha</s>, and urinary difficulty, and removes jaundice and anemia.
Steamed in sour water and dried, it attains purification.
The learned do not prescribe calcination or extraction of <s>sattva</s> for it.
<s>Rasaka</s> is said to be of two kinds: <s>kāravellaka</s> and <s>dardura</s>.
The latter is said to be best for extracting <s>sattva</s>, and the former for medicines and the like.
It removes all <s>meha</s> disorders and destroys pitta and phlegm.
The two excellent <s>rasas</s>, both efficacious, were taught by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
By the one who has made auspicious <s>sūta</s> and <s>kharparaka</s> able to endure fire,
a heaven-like accomplishment has been obtained; there is no doubt here.
When <s>rasaka</s> is properly heated and placed in a mercury-filled vessel,
it attains purity after being immersed seven times.

children.text: kāṃjike vātha takre vā nṛmūtre meṣamūtrake
children.translated_text: Or in sour gruel, buttermilk, human urine, or sheep urine,
<s>kharpara</s>, melted and poured properly, is purified.
Purified <s>kharpara</s>, filed down and placed in human urine,
colors copper for one month with an excellent gold-like brilliance.
<s>Śilā</s>, turmeric, <s>triphala</s>, and household soot, together with rock salt,
with <s>bhallātakas</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇas</s>, alkalis, and sour substances, should be rubbed together.
With quarter-portions added, a crucible resembling an eggplant fruit
should be sealed and dried, and then one should place a crucible upon a crucible.

children.text: pradhmāte kharpare jvālā sitā nīlā bhavedyadā
children.translated_text: When, in the blown <s>kharpara</s>, the flame becomes white and blue,
one should take it with iron tongs and hold the crucible mouth downward.

children.text: bhūmyām āḍhālayet sattvaṃ yathā nālaṃ na bhajyate
children.translated_text: One should pour the <s>sattva</s> onto the ground so that the channel is not broken.

children.text: tadā sīsopamaṃ satvaṃ patatyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a lead-like <s>sattva</s> certainly falls out; there is no doubt.

children.text: anenaiva prakāreṇa trivāraṃ hi kṛte sati
children.translated_text: When this very procedure has been done three times,
all the <s>sattva</s> comes forth; this truth was spoken by the guru.
The <s>sattva</s>, mixed with <s>tālaka</s>, should be placed in the <s>kharpara</s>...
One should rub it with an iron rod; it is calcined, without doubt.

children.text: mṛtaṃ satvaṃ mṛtaṃ kāṃtaṃ samāṃśenāpi yojitam
children.translated_text: The calcined <s>sattva</s> and calcined <s>kānta</s> are combined even in equal parts;
this powder, in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>, is mixed with a decoction of <s>varā</s>.
Kept overnight in an iron vessel, it is to be given with a sesame-oil admixture.

children.text: nihanti madhumehaṃ ca kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ tathānilam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys diabetes, consumption, anemia, and also vāta disorder.
and vaginal disorders of women, and even intermittent fevers;
it destroys all women's diseases, as well as disorders headed by dyspnea and cough.

children.text: tālakaṃ tuvarī gaṃdhaṃ kaṃkuṣṭhaṃ kunaṭī tathā
children.translated_text: The substances are <s>tālaka</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, and also <s>kunaṭī</s>;
<s>sauvīra</s>, <s>gairika</s>, and the eighth, called <s>khecara</s>.
<s>Tālaka</s> is said to be of two kinds, one called <s>dala</s> and one named <s>aśma</s>.

children.text: sūkṣmapatraṃ hemavarṇaṃ guru snigdhaṃ ca bhāsuram ||
children.translated_text: The <s>dala</s> type has fine leaves, is gold-colored, heavy, unctuous, and shining.
That <s>tālaka</s> called <s>dala</s> has abundant <s>sattva</s> and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
The other is without leaves, stone-like, with little <s>sattva</s>, and likewise heavy.
That <s>aśmatālaka</s> stops women's menstruation and is unwholesome.
Boiled in water of <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s>, or then in alkaline water,
or boiled in <s>cūrṇa</s>-water, it is purified in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus).
With horse-gram decoction, <s>saubhāgya</s>, buffalo ghee, and honey,
one should place that <s>tālaka</s> in a mortar and grind it for one day.
After removing the husks, one should then grind castor seeds,
making them one eighth of the <s>tālaka</s>, whose measure is eight <s>palas</s>.
Having added the castor seeds, one should grind them together.

children.text: yavābhā guṭikā kāryā śuṣkā kupyāṃ nidhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Pellets the size of barley grains should be made; when dry, they should be placed in a flask.
In the middle of a <s>vālukāyantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus), fire should be applied for twelve <s>yāmas</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out and collect the <s>sattva</s> that has gone upward.
There are many methods for the <s>sattvas</s> of stone-minerals;
the <s>sattvas</s> that are effective have indeed been described.
It removes vāta and kapha, drives away blood disorders and <s>bhūta</s> affliction, and stops menstruation in women.
It is very unctuous, hot, pungent, kindles digestion, and removes <s>kuṣṭha</s> disease.
<s>Tuvarī</s> is considered a mineral born in the land of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>;

children.text: yā lepitā śvetavastre raṅgabandhakarī hi sā ||
children.translated_text: when it is smeared on white cloth, it fixes the color there.
<s>Phullikā</s> and <s>khaṭikā</s> are likewise praised as the two kinds.
The slightly yellow and very unctuous one destroys <s>garadoṣa</s> (poisoning).
The other, white in color and sour, is <s>phullikā</s>, which calcines iron.
<s>Kāṅkṣī</s> is astringent, sweet, pungent, and destroys poison;
it heals wounds and removes kapha, eye diseases, and the three humors;
it removes <s>kuṣṭha</s> disease and carries <s>bīja</s> in <s>pārada</s> (mercury).

children.text: dhānyāmle tuvarī kṣiptā śudhyati tridinena vai
children.translated_text: <s>Tuvarī</s>, placed in sour grain-gruel, is purified in three days.
Rubbed with alkalis and acids and then blown in the fire, it releases <s>sattva</s>.
That <s>sattva</s> is suitable for <s>dhātuvāda</s> (metallurgical transmutation), not for medicine.

children.text: manaḥśilā triprakārā śyāmā raktā ca khaṇḍikā
children.translated_text: <s>Manaḥśilā</s> is of three kinds: dark, red, and <s>khaṇḍikā</s>;

children.text: śyāmā raktā miśravarṇā bhārāḍhyā śyāmikā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the dark kind is dark-red, mixed in color, and heavy in weight.
The <s>kaṇavīrā</s>, with a very red body and copper-like appearance, is praised.

children.text: cūrṇitā yāti raktāṅgī guruḥ snigdhā ca khaṇḍikā ||
children.translated_text: When powdered it becomes red-bodied; <s>khaṇḍikā</s> is heavy and unctuous.

children.text: sarvāḥ kunaṭyaḥ kathitāḥ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ guṇottarāḥ
children.translated_text: All are called <s>kunaṭī</s>; each earlier one is superior in qualities.
With juice of <s>munipatra</s>, or else with juice of ginger,
when infused seven times, it is purified without doubt.
Then, with ghee and jaggery, or with slag and <s>guggulu</s>,

children.text: dhmātā tu koṣṭhikāyantre muñcet sattvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when blown in a <s>koṣṭhikāyantra</s>, it releases <s>sattva</s>, without doubt.
All are excellent <s>rasāyanas</s> and destroy vāta and kapha.
Rich in <s>sattva</s> and antidotal, they remove <s>bhūta</s> affliction, itching, and wasting.
They calm weak digestion and eliminate diseases of the bowels.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ca rasāṃjanaṃ nigaditaṃ srotoṃjanaṃ caiva hi
children.translated_text: There is <s>sauvīra</s>, and <s>rasāñjana</s> is named, and also <s>srotoñjana</s>;
similarly <s>puṣpāñjana</s>, and after that <s>nīlāñjana</s> is described.
For all five, according to proper rule, their names, colors, qualities, and forms

children.text: kathyante'tra mayāpi śodhanam idaṃ satvaṃ mṛtiścocyate ||
children.translated_text: are described here by me, and their purification, <s>sattva</s>, and calcination are also stated.
The collyrium called <s>sauvīra</s> is smoke-colored; it destroys pitta and blood disorders, vomiting, hiccup, and wounds.

children.text: netravyādhau śodhane ropaṇe ca śreṣṭhaṃ proktaṃ karṇarogapraśāṃtyai ||
children.translated_text: It is declared best for eye disease, for cleansing and healing, and for calming ear disease.
Yellowish, calming poison and blood disorders, removing dyspnea and hiccup,
improving complexion, destroying vāta and worms, handsome, and produced from <s>dārvī</s>,
unctuous, sweet and astringent, removing poison, vomiting, pitta, and blood,
<s>Srotoñjana</s> is always said to be good for the eyes and to remove hiccup and pain.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is white, unctuous, cooling, and removes eye disease and poison;
it is described here as destroying fever and severe hiccup.
<s>Nīlāñjana</s> is a <s>rasāyana</s>, calcines gold, is heavy and unctuous, and removes the three humors;
and it is said to make iron soft.
All the collyria are purified here with the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> alone,
continually, as the guru's word is true.
One should extract the <s>sattva</s> of the collyria just as the <s>sattva</s> of <s>śilā</s>.
The earlier sages have identified four divisions of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur):
it is fourfold: white, yellow, red, and black.
The white is chalk-like; by smearing it, the calcination of iron

children.text: jāyate nātra saṃdeho hyanubhūtaṃ mayā khalu ||
children.translated_text: takes place, without doubt; indeed this has been experienced by me.
The one that is yellow in color is called <s>amalasāraka</s>;

children.text: rase rasāyane śreṣṭhaḥ śukapicchaḥ sa kathyate ||
children.translated_text: it is best in mercury work and <s>rasāyana</s>; it is called <s>śukapiccha</s>.
The red one, resembling lac-juice, is called <s>śukatuṇḍa</s>.
It causes the coloring of metals and is fully able to bind <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: yaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaḥ sa tu durlabho'sti nāśaṃ karotīha jarāpamṛtyoḥ
children.translated_text: That which is black in color is rare; here it destroys old age and untimely death.

children.text: saṃsevanādvajrasamaṃ śarīraṃ bhavetsukāntaṃ hi nirāmayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Through its use the body becomes diamond-like, beautiful, and free from disease.

children.text: ghaṭīmadhye payaḥ kṣiptvā mukhe vastraṃ prabandhayet
children.translated_text: After putting milk inside a pot, one should tie a cloth over its mouth.
On top of the cloth one should put the powder of <s>bali</s> and seal the mouth with a saucer.
Having placed that vessel in the ground, one should carefully give it a <s>puṭa</s> heating.
With twenty cow-dung cakes, one should then remove it when it has cooled on its own.
By this same procedure, again and again, letting it cool naturally each time,
sulfur purified in this way becomes capable of accomplishing every operation.
<s>Gandhapāṣāṇa</s> is sweet in post-digestive effect and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
It pacifies erysipelas, itching, and skin disease, and it also kindles digestion.
It calms <s>āma</s> and indigestion, removes poison, and absorbs <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Born directly from the flower of <s>Pārvatī</s>, it gives potency to <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
It properly removes worm disease and certainly renders <s>sūta</s> (mercury) <s>mūrchita</s>.
It was consumed by King <s>Bali</s> as the cause of abundant strength.
Therefore this very pleasing <s>gandhaka</s> is called <s>balivasā</s>.
But <s>śukapiccha</s> should be made into a paste with an equal part of black pepper.
Six times as much <s>triphalā</s> should be prepared, and one should grind it with <s>kṛtamālā</s>
root liquids; then, when drunk, it destroys many kinds of skin disease.
Ground in the water of that root, and then smeared over the body,
it quickly destroys those very skin diseases, giving immediate proof of its effect.
One should also grind well-purified sulfur together with oil,
with water of <s>apāmārga</s> alkali, with oil, and with black pepper.
After anointing the entire body, one should remain in the heat of the sun.
In the third watch one should have him eat rice with buttermilk.
At night one should make him sweat by fire; rising in the morning, one should massage him.
He should bathe with buffalo dung and cold water.

children.text: snānaṃ kuryāduṣasyevaṃ kaṇḍūḥ pāmā ca naśyati
children.translated_text: Taking the bath at dawn in this way, itching and scabies disappear.
This treatment of observed efficacy has indeed been taught here by me.
It destroys longstanding skin disease, scabies, and eczema.
Powder of purified sulfur should be mixed with a one-sixteenth part of <s>vyoṣa</s>.
The sulfur powder, mixed with oil, should be spread on a cloth measuring a span.

children.text: vilipya veṣṭayitvā ca vartiṃ sūtreṇa veṣṭayet
children.translated_text: After smearing it on and rolling it up, one should wrap the wick with thread.
Holding the wick with tongs, one should light it in the middle.
The melted sulfur falls drop by drop into a glass vessel.
One should place three drops of that molten substance on a <s>nāgavallī</s> leaf.
Having put there a <s>valla</s>-measure of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), one should rub it with a finger.
Afterwards one should eat all of that and then drink cow's milk.
It kindles sexual vigor and destroys consumption and pallor.
It destroys a diseased <s>grahaṇī</s>, colicky pain, dyspnea, and cough.
It calms <s>āma</s> and indigestion, and a feeling of lightness arises.

children.text: gaṃdhakasya guṇānvaktuṃ śaktaḥ kaḥ śaṃbhunā vinā ||
children.translated_text: Who but <s>Śambhu</s> is able to describe the qualities of sulfur?
On a mountain near the snow there grows the very beautiful <s>kaṅkuṣṭhaka</s>.

children.text: ekameva nalikābhidhānakaṃ reṇukaṃ tadanu cāparaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: One kind is called <s>nalikā</s>, and after that there is another, <s>reṇuka</s>.

children.text: pītavarṇamasṛṇaṃ ca vai guru snigdham uttamataraṃ pravakṣyate
children.translated_text: The yellow-colored, smooth, heavy, and oily kind is declared to be the best.
The dark-yellow one, very deficient in essence, is said to be the second, <s>reṇuka</s>.

children.text: vadanti kaṃkuṣṭhamathāpare hi sadyaḥ prasūtasya ca dantinaḥ śakṛt
children.translated_text: Others say that <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is the dung of a newly born elephant.

children.text: tat kṛṣṇapītaṃ bhavatīva recanaṃ tṛtīyamāhurvibudhā bhiṣagvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: That black-yellow kind acts as a purgative; wise and excellent physicians call it the third.

children.text: caturthakaṅkuṣṭhamihaiva vājināṃ nālaṃ hi kecitpravadanti tajjñāḥ
children.translated_text: Some experts say that the fourth <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> here is the <s>nāla</s> of horses.
That which comes from an elephant, white or very yellow, quickly produces purgation.

children.text: rasāyane śreṣṭhataraṃ rase ca satvena yuktaṃ khalu gauravānvitam
children.translated_text: It is especially excellent in <s>rasāyana</s> and in mercury work, endowed with essence and weight.

children.text: śuṃṭhyambhasā bhāvitameva śuddhiṃ kaṃkuṣṭhamāyāti hi satyamuktam ||
children.translated_text: When impregnated with ginger-water, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> becomes purified; this is truly stated.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭhaka</s> is bitter, pungent, and hot in potency, and especially produces purgation.
The ancient knowers of śāstra declare it excellent for removing rectal pain, abdominal tumors, wounds, and colic.

children.text: sattvākṛṣṭirna ca proktā yasmātsatvamayaṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: Extraction of <s>sattva</s> is not prescribed, because it is itself made of <s>sattva</s>.
One should take it in the measure of a barley grain for purgation; there is no doubt.
When purgation has occurred, it destroys <s>āma</s> fever in a moment.

children.text: tāṃbūlena samaṃ caivaṃ bhakṣitaṃ sārayed dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Eaten in this way together with betel, it certainly causes evacuation.
A decoction of <s>babbūla</s> root, combined with <s>saubhāgya</s> and <s>ajājī</s>,

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ pibeddhīmān viṣaṃ kaṃkuṣṭhajaṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: a wise person should drink again and again; he will overcome poison arising from <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>.
As for <s>kāsīsa</s>, the first is this one called <s>saikata</s>; another is called <s>puṣpa</s>.
It is alkaline-sour, heavy, smoke-colored, poison-removing, hot in potency, and color-giving.
That first <s>saikata</s> destroys leukoderma and colors the face and hair.

children.text: puṣpākhyaṃ hyaparaṃ guṇaiśca sahitaṃ sevyaṃ sadā rogahṛt ||
children.translated_text: The other, called <s>puṣpa</s>, is endowed with qualities, should always be used, and removes disease.
The <s>kāsīsa</s> called <s>puṣpa</s> is well known as removing eye diseases.
It is hot in potency, astringent and sour, poison-destroying, and phlegm-destroying.
It removes wounds, destroys wasting disease, and is excellent for dyeing cloth.
Steamed in the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, it becomes pure.
One should extract its <s>sattva</s> just like the <s>sattva</s> of <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> and the ash of <s>kānta</s> should both be taken in equal parts.
Mixed with <s>varā</s> and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, drenched with ghee and honey, and taken in the morning,
it quickly destroys <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia) and <s>yakṣmā</s> (consumption) as well.
It completely removes splenic disease, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal masses), pain in the rectum, and urinary difficulty.
When used according to the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen, it destroys all diseases.
It stimulates the digestive fire and removes wrinkles and gray hair.
It certainly destroys diseases produced by <s>āma</s> and indigestion; there is no doubt.
The salt called <s>navasāra</s>, known as <s>cullikā</s>, has been described.
It is said to melt metals and also to digest <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
It quickly kindles the digestive fire and removes <s>gulma</s> and disorders of the spleen.
It properly digests meat and the like, and brings about the cooking of food that has been eaten.
A <s>varāṭikā</s> that measures one and a half <s>niṣkas</s>

children.text: śreṣṭhā saiva budhaiḥ proktā ṭaṅkabhārā hi madhyamā ||
children.translated_text: is declared by the learned to be the best; one of a <s>ṭaṅka</s> weight is middling.
One whose weight is three quarters of a <s>ṭaṅka</s> is said to be inferior.
In preparations of <s>rasa</s> and <s>rasāyana</s>, it is said to remove colic beginning with <s>pariṇāmaśūla</s>.
It destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> disease and consumption, is hot in potency, and is considered digestive-stimulating.
It is aphrodisiac, removes the <s>doṣas</s>, benefits the eyes, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
It is praised for digesting <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) and is always useful among <s>biḍa</s> preparations.
A large <s>varāṭikā</s> is said to be heavy and to remove <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
Steamed with sour <s>āranāla</s> for one <s>yāma</s>, it obtains purification.
<s>Darada</s> is of the kind called <s>śukatuṇḍa</s>; another is <s>haṃsapāka</s>.

children.text: carmāraḥ prathamaḥ prokto hīnasatvaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The first is called <s>carmāra</s>; it is said to have poor <s>sattva</s> (extractable essence).
The excellent <s>haṃsapāka</s> kind resembles coral and is rich in streaks.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> stimulates digestion, destroys all <s>doṣas</s>, and is an eminent <s>rasāyana</s>.
It directly removes every disease and is highly praised for liquefying operations.
Just as the king of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), digested with six times as much sulfur,
so <s>sūta</s> (mercury) extracted from <s>darada</s> becomes endowed with qualities of this sort.
When it is steamed inside a piece of gourd with the juice of <s>lakuca</s>,
it becomes purified at once and should be applied in all operations.
One kind is <s>pāṣāṇagairika</s>, stone ochre; the second is <s>svarṇagairika</s>, golden ochre.
<s>Pāṣāṇagairika</s> is said to be hard and copper-colored.
<s>Svarṇagairika</s> is intensely red, unctuous, and smooth.

children.text: svādu tiktaṃ himaṃ netryaṃ kaṣāyaṃ raktapittanut ||
children.translated_text: It is sweet, bitter, cooling, good for the eyes, astringent, and removes <s>raktapitta</s>.
<s>Svarṇagairika</s> also removes hiccup, vomiting, poison, and bleeding disorders.
The other, <s>pāṣāṇagairika</s>, has fewer qualities than the preceding one.
<s>Gairika</s>, when impregnated with cow's milk, reaches purification.
<s>Gairika</s> has indeed been described by <s>Nandin</s> as being in the form of <s>sattva</s>.
The afterbirth of the <s>agninakra</s>, cast out by the ocean,
and dried by the sun's heat, is remembered as <s>agnijāra</s>.
It pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>, is absorbent, and is an excellent remover of <s>dhanurvāta</s>.
It increases the potency of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and is remembered as a supreme digestant.
The red-colored fluid lodged within rock on the great mountain,
dried by the heat of the sun, is called <s>girisindūra</s>.
<s>Girisindūra</s> binds <s>rasa</s> (mercury), is penetrating, and pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>.
It is said to act on the body and metals and to be good for the eyes.
In the land of <s>Gurjaraka</s> there is a foliated yellow substance,
on the side of Mount <s>Arbuda</s>, called <s>Vodāraśṛṅgaka</s> by name.
It has the <s>sattva</s> of <s>nāga</s>, removes defects of the <s>liṅga</s>, and destroys disorders of <s>śleṣman</s>.
It properly binds <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and is excellent for dyeing the beard.
All the ordinary <s>rasas</s>, with the juice of <s>bījapūra</s>,
when impregnated three times and dried, become free of defects.
In the same way, <s>biḍa</s> is said to be an excellent remover of all defects.

children.text: māṇikyaṃ mauktikaṃ caiva vidrumaṃ tārkṣyaṃ puṣpakam
children.translated_text: <s>Māṇikya</s> (ruby), <s>mauktika</s> (pearl), <s>vidruma</s> (coral), <s>tārkṣya</s>, and <s>puṣpaka</s>,

children.text: vajraṃ nīlaṃ ca gomedaṃ vaiḍūryaṃ ca krameṇa hi ||
children.translated_text: then <s>vajra</s> (diamond), <s>nīla</s> (sapphire), <s>gomeda</s>, and <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, in order:
a gem endowed with good birth and good qualities grants the accomplishment of every aim.
It is useful in gifts, in <s>rasāyana</s>, in wearing, and in the worship of deities.
The first, called <s>padmarāga</s>, is declared to be the best.

children.text: dvitīyaṃ nīlagandhi syād ghanaṃ raktaṃ suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: The second is <s>nīlagandhi</s>; it should be dense, red, and very beautiful.

children.text: mahacca kamalacchāyaṃ snigdhaṃ svacchaṃ guru sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Large, lotus-hued, glossy, clear, heavy, and bright,

children.text: samaṃ vṛttāyataṃ gātre māṇikyaṃ cottamaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: even, round, and elongated in body: such a ruby is considered excellent.
A ruby produced from the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with a blue interior and reddish luster,
having the same hue as described before, is called <s>nīlagandhi</s>.

children.text: māṇikyaṃ cāṣṭadhā neṣṭaṃ sacchidraṃ malinaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: A ruby is undesirable in eight ways: if it is perforated, dirty, light,

children.text: karkaśaṃ cipiṭaṃ vakraṃ sūkṣmaṃ cāviśadaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: rough, flattened, crooked, tiny, or unclear as well.

children.text: saṃdīpanaṃ vṛṣyatamaṃ hi rūkṣaṃ vātāpahaṃ karmarujāpahaṃ ca
children.translated_text: It kindles digestion, is highly aphrodisiac, dry, removes <s>vāta</s>, and removes pains arising from activity.

children.text: bhūtādidoṣatrayanāśanaṃ paraṃ rājñāṃ sadā yogyatamaṃ praśastam ||
children.translated_text: It supremely destroys the threefold disorders beginning with spirit affliction, and is always most suitable and praised for kings.

children.text: hlādi śvetaṃ raśmimannirmalaṃ ca vṛttaṃ khyātaṃ mauktikaṃ toyabhāsam
children.translated_text: A pearl is known as pleasing, white, radiant, spotless, round, and water-like in sheen.

children.text: snigdhaṃ taulye gauravaṃ cenmahattalliṃgairetair lakṣitaṃ tacca śuddham ||
children.translated_text: If it is glossy, heavy when weighed, and large, marked by these signs, it is pure.

children.text: rūkṣāṅgaṃ cenniṣprabhaṃ śyāvatāmraṃ cārdhaṃ śubhraṃ graṃthilaṃ mauktikaṃ ca
children.translated_text: But a pearl with a rough body, without luster, dusky or coppery, half white, or knotty,

children.text: kṣārābhāsaṃ vaikaṭaṃ yugmakaṃ ca doṣairyuktaṃ sarvathā tyājyamebhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: alkaline-looking, deformed, or double, is joined with these defects and should be rejected entirely.

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ vahnimāṃdyaṃ kṣayaṃ ca hanyād vṛṣyaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ pittahāri
children.translated_text: It destroys cough, dyspnea, weak digestion, and consumption; it is aphrodisiac, nourishing, and removes <s>pitta</s>.
Taken in this way at all times, it destroys burning, <s>śleṣman</s>, insanity, <s>vāta</s>, and other diseases.

children.text: snigdhaṃ sthūlaṃ pakvabimbīphalābhaṃ vṛttaṃ dīrghaṃ nirvraṇaṃ cāpyadīrgham
children.translated_text: Glossy, large, resembling a ripe <s>bimbī</s> fruit, round, elongated, unblemished, and yet not overlong,

children.text: khyātaṃ sadbhiḥ saptadhā vidrumaṃ ca doṣairmuktaṃ sarvakāryeṣu śastam ||
children.translated_text: And <s>vidruma</s> (coral), known by the good as sevenfold, is praised for all purposes when free from defects.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ śvetaṃ savraṇaṃ dhūsaraṃ ca nirbhāraṃ cecchulbavarṇaṃ pravālam
children.translated_text: Coral that is dry, white, marked by wounds, gray, without weight, or copper-colored

children.text: doṣairyuktaṃ koṭarairāvṛtaṃ ca neṣṭaṃ sadbhir bhakṣaṇe dhāraṇe ca ||
children.translated_text: and joined with defects and covered with hollows is not approved by the good for eating or wearing.

children.text: pittāsraghnaṃ śvāsakāsādirogān hanyād evaṃ durnivāraṃ viṣaṃ ca
children.translated_text: It destroys disorders of bile and blood, asthma, cough and related diseases, and also poison that is hard to check.

children.text: bhūtonmādān netrarogān nihanyāt sadyaḥ kuryāddīpanaṃ pācanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It removes spirit-possession, insanity, and eye diseases, and at once produces appetite-kindling and digestion.

children.text: tārkṣyaṃ snigdhaṃ bhāsuraṃ śaṣpavarṇaṃ gātraiḥ śuddhaṃ bhāravadraśmiyuktam
children.translated_text: <s>Tārkṣya</s> should be unctuous, shining, grass-colored, pure in body, heavy, and endowed with rays of luster.

children.text: ete proktā saptasaṃkhyā guṇā vai dāne śastaṃ bhakṣaṇe dhāraṇe ca ||
children.translated_text: These seven qualities are indeed declared; it is praised for giving, eating, and wearing.

children.text: nīlaṃ śvetaṃ karkaśaṃ śyāvarūkṣaṃ vakraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ cippaṭaṃ bhārahīnam
children.translated_text: Blue, white, rough, dark and dry, crooked, black, flat, and lacking weight,

children.text: duṣṭaṃ tārkṣyaṃ cauṣadhenopayojyaṃ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ sannipātāgnimāṃdyam ||
children.translated_text: such <s>tārkṣya</s> is defective and not fit for medicinal use; the good kind destroys cough, asthma, derangement of all three humors, and weak digestion,

children.text: śophaṃ śūlaṃ jūrtirogaṃ viṣaṃ ca durnāmānaṃ pāṇḍurogaṃ nihanyāt ||
children.translated_text: and it removes swelling, colic, the disease called <s>jūrti</s>, poison, piles, and anemia.

children.text: svacchaṃ sthūlaṃ puṣparāgaṃ guru syātsnigdhaṃ varṇe karṇikāraprasūnam
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣparāga</s> should be clear, large, heavy, unctuous, and in color like a blossom of <s>karṇikāra</s>.

children.text: taccāvakraṃ masṛṇaṃ komalaṃ ca liṃgairetaiḥ śobhanaṃ puṣparāgam ||
children.translated_text: It should also be straight, smooth, and soft; by these marks <s>puṣparāga</s> is excellent.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ pītaṃ karkaśaṃ śyāmalaṃ ca pāṇḍu syādvā kāpilaṃ toyahīnam
children.translated_text: A dry, yellow, rough, dark, pale, tawny, or lusterless stone,

children.text: doṣairyuktaṃ niṣprabhaṃ puṣparāgaṃ no sevyaṃ tannaiva deyaṃ dvijebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a defective and brilliance-less <s>puṣparāga</s>, should not be used and should not be given to the twice-born.

children.text: kuṣṭhaṃ chardiṃ śleṣmavātau nihanti maṃdāgnīnāmetadeva praśastam
children.translated_text: It destroys skin disease, vomiting, phlegm, and wind; this very stone is excellent for those with weak digestive fire.

children.text: dāhe kṛcchre dīpanaṃ pācanaṃ ca tasmātsevyaṃ sarvakālaṃ manuṣyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In burning sensation and dysuria it kindles appetite and promotes digestion; therefore people should use it at all times.

children.text: sarveṣu ratneṣu sadā variṣṭhaṃ mūlyairgariṣṭhaṃ vividhaṃ hi vajram
children.translated_text: Among all jewels, <s>vajra</s> (diamond) is always the best, highest in value, and indeed of various kinds.

children.text: naraśca nārī ca tathā tṛtīyaṃ teṣāṃ guṇānvacmi samāsato hi ||
children.translated_text: It is male, female, and likewise a third type; I shall briefly state their qualities.

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ śreṣṭhametatpradiṣṭaṃ dravyād vīryāt pākataśca prabhāvāt
children.translated_text: Each preceding type is declared superior because of substance, potency, digestion, and specific efficacy.

children.text: teṣāṃ varṇā jātayaśca prabhedāḥ kathyante'ṣṭau śāstrataścāpakarṣāt ||
children.translated_text: Their colors, classes, and eight divisions are taught from the treatise in descending order.

children.text: śvetādikaṃ varṇacatuṣṭayaṃ hi sarveṣu ratneṣu ca kathyate budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: The fourfold set of colors beginning with white is taught by the wise for all jewels.
They are, in sequence, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>śūdra</s> classes and colors.

children.text: puṃvajraṃ yatprocyate cāṣṭadhāraṃ ṣaṭkoṇaṃ ced indracāpena tulyam
children.translated_text: What is called a male diamond has eight edges and, if it has six angles, is equal to a rainbow.

children.text: aṣṭau cetsyuḥ phālakā bhāsuraṃ vai pūrvaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvadoṣāpahaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: If it has eight facets and is shining, the first type is best and removes all defects.

children.text: strīvajraṃ cettādṛśaṃ vartulaṃ hi kiṃciccaivaṃ cippaṭaṃ karkaśaṃ ca
children.translated_text: If a female diamond is like that, but round, somewhat flat, and rough,

children.text: koṇāgraṃ vai kuṇṭhitaṃ vartulaṃ ca kiṃciddhīnaṃ procyate tattṛtīyam ||
children.translated_text: with its angular tips blunted and rounded, that third type is said to be somewhat inferior.

children.text: strī pumān no strī pumān yacca vajraṃ yojyaṃ tacca strīṣu puṃsveva ṣaṇḍhe
children.translated_text: A diamond that is female, male, or neither female nor male should be applied respectively to women, men, and eunuchs.

children.text: vyatyāsādvai naiva dattaṃ phalaṃ taddadyād vajraṃ vā vinā tatpumāṃsam ||
children.translated_text: If the assignment is reversed, it certainly does not give that promised fruit; one should give a diamond while avoiding that male one.

children.text: varṇe'pyevaṃ yasya varṇasya vajraṃ tattadvarṇe śobhanīyaṃ pradiṣṭam
children.translated_text: So too with color: a diamond of whatever color is prescribed as suitable for that corresponding color-class.

children.text: nyāyaścāyaṃ bhairaveṇa pradiṣṭaḥ sarveṣveva ratnavargeṣu samyak ||
children.translated_text: This rule was properly taught by <s>Bhairava</s> for all classes of jewels.

children.text: yāmāvadhi sveditameva vajraṃ śuddhiṃ prayātīha kulatthatoye
children.translated_text: A diamond steamed for the span of a <s>yāma</s> becomes purified here in <s>kulattha</s> water.

children.text: siddhaṃ tathā kodravaje śṛte vā vajraṃ viśudhyeddhi viniścitena ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, diamond is certainly purified when cooked in a decoction made from <s>kodrava</s>.
Diamond, well impregnated with bedbug blood and dried four times,

children.text: chucchuṃdarīsthaṃ hi vipācitaṃ puṭe puṭedvarāheṇa ca triṃśadevam ||
children.translated_text: is placed in a <s>chucchuṃdarī</s>, cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>, and then heated with a <s>vārāha-puṭa</s> thirty times.

children.text: dhmātaṃ punardhmāya śataṃ hi vārān kvāthe kulatthasya hi nikṣipecca
children.translated_text: After it has been smelted, one should smelt it again a hundred times and cast it into a decoction of <s>kulattha</s>.

children.text: saṃpeṣayettaṃ hi śilātalena manaḥśilābhiḥ saha kārayedvaṭīm ||
children.translated_text: One should grind it on a stone slab together with <s>manaḥśilā</s> and make it into a pill.

children.text: kṣiptvā nirundhyāpi ca mūṣikāyāṃ puṭānyathāṣṭau ca vanopalairdadet
children.translated_text: Having put it into a small crucible and sealed it, one should then give eight <s>puṭas</s> with forest cow-dung cakes.

children.text: vārān śataṃ cāpi tato dhamettaṃ saṃmarditaṃ śodhitapāradena ||
children.translated_text: After that, one should smelt it a hundred times, once it has been thoroughly rubbed with purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury).

children.text: vajrāṇi sarvāṇi mṛtībhavanti tadbhasmakaṃ vāritaraṃ bhavecca
children.translated_text: All diamonds become calcined; that ash becomes able to float on water.

children.text: śrīsomadevena ca satyavācā vajrasya mṛtyuḥ kathito hi samyak ||
children.translated_text: The calcination of diamond was correctly taught by truth-speaking <s>Śrī Somadeva</s>.
In an iron vessel filled with the juice of <s>kāsamarda</s>, it is smeared with bedbug blood,

children.text: sveditaṃ ca bhiduraṃ hi saptabhirvāsaraiḥ pariniṣecya mūtrake ||
children.translated_text: and, after being steamed for seven days and repeatedly sprinkled with urine, it indeed becomes brittle.

children.text: dhmāpitaṃ hi khalu vajrasaṃjñakaṃ mārayediti vadanti tadvidaḥ
children.translated_text: When it is heated, the substance called diamond is thereby killed, so those who know this say.

children.text: nīlajvālāvīrudhaḥ kandakeṣu ghṛṣṭaṃ gharme śoṣitaṃ bhasmabhāvam ||
children.translated_text: Ground in the tubers of the <s>nīlajvālā</s> plant and dried in the sun, it reaches the state of ash.

children.text: vajraṃ yāti svairavahnipradānāt piṣṭaiścāpi kṣoṇināgaiḥ praliptam
children.translated_text: Diamond reaches that state through repeated applications of fire, being smeared also with ground <s>kṣoṇināga</s> (earth-worm substance).
One should carefully enclose it twenty times in a sealed capsule, with forest fuel or cow-dung cakes, in a fierce fire.

children.text: vajraṃ caivaṃ bhasmasādvīryayuktaṃ sarvasminvai yojanīyaṃ rasādau ||
children.translated_text: Thus diamond, reduced to ash and endowed with potency, is to be employed in every mercurial preparation and the like.
It is prescribed as life-giving, extremely aphrodisiac, and likewise as uprooting the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors).

children.text: rasendrakasyāpi hi baṃdhakṛtsadā sudhāsamaṃ cāpamṛtiṃ ca hanyāt ||
children.translated_text: It always causes the binding of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury); equal to nectar, it destroys untimely death.

children.text: bhūnāgasatvena samaṃ vimardya vajrasya bhūtiṃ ca samānahemnā
children.translated_text: Having triturated diamond ash with an equal amount of <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s> and with an equal amount of gold,

children.text: dhmātaṃ rasādāvapi yojanīyaṃ rasāyanaṃ tadbhavatīha samyak ||
children.translated_text: the smelted product should be used in mercury and the like; here it becomes a true <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: bhāgāstrayaścaiva hi sūtakasya bhāgaṃ vimardyātha mṛtaṃ hi vajram
children.translated_text: Three parts of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) and one part of calcined diamond should then be triturated.

children.text: vajrasya bhūtiḥ kila poṭalīkṛtā mukhe dhṛtā dārḍhyakarī dvijānām ||
children.translated_text: Diamond ash, made into a packet and held in the mouth, is said to strengthen the teeth.

children.text: vajrabhasma kila bhāgatriṃśakaṃ svarṇameva kathitaṃ kalāṃśakam
children.translated_text: <s>Vajra-bhasma</s> (diamond ash), indeed, is thirty parts; gold is stated to be a <s>kalā</s>-part.

children.text: aṣṭabhāgamiha tārakaṃ kuru sūtamatra samabhāgakaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Here make <s>tāraka</s> (silver) eight parts, and in this case <s>sūta</s> (mercury) always an equal part.
Ash of mica-<s>sattva</s> should be an equal portion, and here <s>tāpya</s> should be a fourth part.

children.text: vaikrāṃtabhasmātra tathāṣṭabhāgakaṃ ṣaḍeva bhāgā hi balervidheyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, ash of <s>vaikrānta</s> should be eight parts here, and exactly six parts of <s>bali</s> are to be used.
It always attains sixfold accomplishment; when consumed, it attains accomplishment of every aim.
Now there is <s>indranīla</s>, <s>vārinīlaka</s>, and also <s>nīlaka</s> with whiteness inside.

children.text: kathyate hi laghu vārinīlakaṃ tucchameva kathitaṃ bhiṣagvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: The light <s>vārinīlaka</s> is said by the best physicians to be worthless.

children.text: kāntyā yuktaṃ kārṣṇyagarbhaṃ ca nīlaṃ taccāpyuktaṃ śakranīlābhidhānam ||
children.translated_text: A blue gem endowed with brilliance and having blackness within is also called by the name <s>śakranīla</s>.

children.text: ekacchāyaṃ snigdhavarṇaṃ guru syātsvacchaṃ madhye collasatkāṃtiyuktam
children.translated_text: It should have a single shade, an unctuous color, be heavy and clear, and be endowed with flashing brilliance in the middle.

children.text: nīlaṃ proktaṃ piṇḍitaṃ saptasaṃjñair etair liṅgair lakṣitaṃ cottamaṃ hi ||
children.translated_text: A compact <s>nīla</s>, marked by these seven characteristics, is indeed said to be excellent.

children.text: nirbhāraṃ cetkomalaṃ cāsragandhi rūkṣaṃ varṇe sūkṣmakaṃ cippiṭaṃ ca
children.translated_text: But if it is weightless, soft, blood-scented, rough in color, tiny, and flattened,

children.text: proktaṃ vai tadvārinīlaṃ bhiṣagbhiretairliṃgaiḥ saptabhiḥ kṣepaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>vārinīla</s> by physicians, and by these seven marks it is to be rejected.

children.text: saṃdīpanaṃ śvāsaharaṃ ca vṛṣyaṃ doṣatrayonmūlanakaṃ viṣaghnam
children.translated_text: It stimulates digestion, removes dyspnea, is virilizing, uproots the three <s>doṣas</s>, and destroys poison.
This excellent <s>nīla</s> destroys <s>durnāma</s> and <s>pāṇḍu</s>, is exceedingly strengthening, and conquers wasting.

children.text: gomedakaṃ ratnavaraṃ praśastaṃ gomedavad rāgayutaṃ pracakṣate
children.translated_text: <s>Gomedaka</s>, an excellent and praised gem, is described as possessing a hue like <s>gomeda</s>.
Here pure <s>gomedaka</s> is said to be very clear and of a color like cow urine.

children.text: dīptaṃ snigdhaṃ nirdalaṃ masṛṇaṃ vai mūtracchāyaṃ svacchametatsamaṃ ca
children.translated_text: It is bright, unctuous, without fissures, smooth, urine-colored, clear, and even.

children.text: ebhir liṅgairlakṣitaṃ vai garīyaḥ sarvāsvetadyojanīyaṃ kriyāsu ||
children.translated_text: Marked by these signs, it is superior, and it should be employed in all procedures.

children.text: vicchāyaṃ vā cippiṭaṃ niṣprabhaṃ ca rūkṣaṃ cālpaṃ cāvṛtaṃ pāṭalena
children.translated_text: But if it is discolored, flattened, dull, rough, small, or covered with a reddish tint,

children.text: nirbhāraṃ vā pītakācābhayuktaṃ gomedaṃ cedīdṛśaṃ no variṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: or if the <s>gomeda</s> is weightless or has the appearance of yellow glass, such a stone is not the best.

children.text: gomedakaṃ pittaharaṃ pradiṣṭaṃ pāṇḍukṣayaghnaṃ kaphanāśanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Gomedaka</s> is prescribed as removing <s>pitta</s>, destroying <s>pāṇḍu</s> and wasting, and eliminating <s>kapha</s>.
It stimulates digestion, promotes cooking of food, is pleasing to the appetite, and very powerfully awakens the intellect.

children.text: svacchaṃ samaṃ cāpi viḍūryakaṃ hi śyāmābhaśubhraṃ ca guru sphuṭaṃ vā
children.translated_text: <s>Viḍūryaka</s> is clear and even, with a dark and bright sheen, heavy, and distinctly transparent.
It displays here three pure white lines resembling a sacred thread.

children.text: karkaśaṃ ca laghu cippaṭaṃ sadā śyāmatoyamiva dṛśyate chaviḥ
children.translated_text: If it is rough, light, and flat, and its appearance always looks like dark water,
or if it has a red interior or covering, this <s>viḍūryaka</s> is not good.
<s>Viḍūryaka</s> pacifies bleeding <s>pitta</s>, increases intellect, and kindles digestion.
It always removes the impurity of <s>pitta</s> disorders; the wise person should wear it, for it brings ease.

children.text: gharṣaśca biṃduśca tathaiva reṣā trāsaśca pānīyakṛtā sagarbhatā
children.translated_text: Abrasion, spots, lines, cracks, and inclusions produced by water

children.text: sarveṣu ratneṣu ca pañcadoṣāḥ sādhāraṇāste kathitā munīndraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: are the five faults common to all gems, as taught by the foremost sages.

children.text: ye kṣetratoyaprabhavāśca doṣāḥ sarveṣu ratneṣu galanti samyak ||
children.translated_text: The faults in all gems that arise from the mine and from water are properly removed.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca śuddhiṃ śṛṇu bhairavoktāṃ yathā hi doṣasya vināśanaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: Hear their purification, spoken by <s>Bhairava</s>, by which the destruction of the fault occurs.

children.text: amlena vai śudhyati māṇikyākhyaṃ jayantikāyāḥ svarasena mauktikam ||
children.translated_text: The gem called ruby is purified with a sour liquid, and pearl with the fresh juice of <s>jayantikā</s>.

children.text: kṣāreṇa sarveṇa hi vidrumaṃ ca godugdhatas tārkṣyamupaiti śuddhim
children.translated_text: Coral is purified with any alkali, and <s>tārkṣya</s> attains purification through cow's milk.

children.text: dhānyasyāmlaiḥ puṣparāgasya śuddhiṃ kaulatthe vai kvāthyamānaṃ hi vajram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣparāga</s> is purified with sour grain-liquids, while diamond is purified by being boiled in horse-gram decoction.

children.text: nīlaṃ nīlīpatrajātai rasaiśca gomedaṃ vai rocanāyā rasena
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s> is purified with juices made from <s>nīlī</s> leaves, and <s>gomeda</s> with the juice of <s>rocanā</s>.
If <s>vaiḍūrya</s> is combined with a decoction of <s>uttamā</s> and steamed for one <s>yāma</s> each, it attains purification.
One should rub it together with <s>tālaka</s>, sulfur, and <s>śilā</s>, using the juice of <s>lakuca</s>.

children.text: vajravarjyamapi cāṣṭabhiḥ puṭai ratnabhasma bhavatīti niścitam ||
children.translated_text: Except for diamond, it is certain that gem ash is produced by eight <s>puṭas</s> (heatings).
<s>Rāmaṭha</s>, the five salts, and also the pair of alkalis should always be finely ground,
together with <s>cūlikā</s> salt, <s>amlavetasa</s>, and the ripe fruit of <s>kumbhikā</s> as well.
<s>Citramūlaka</s>, auspicious <s>rudantikā</s>, <s>jambukī</s> mixed with water, and <s>dravantikā</s>,
with the milky sap of <s>arka</s> and an equal milky sap of <s>saudhā</s>: all of this is rubbed on a stone slab.

children.text: golamasya ca vidhāya nikṣipedratnajātiṣu varāṇi peṣayet
children.translated_text: Having made a ball of this, one should place the excellent varieties of gems in it and grind them.
After wrapping the ball in birch bark, one should wind thread over the ball.

children.text: vastreṇa saṃveṣṭya tataḥ prayatnād dolākhyayaṃtre'tha niveśya golakam
children.translated_text: Then, having carefully wrapped the ball in cloth, one should place it in the apparatus called <s>dolā</s>.
