children.text: sarvāmlayukte tuṣavāripūrite pātraṃ dṛḍhe mṛṇmayasaṃjñake hi ||
children.translated_text: It should be in a firm earthen vessel filled with husk-water combined with all sour substances.
Steaming is to be done for three days; then one should take out that excellent ball from it.
One should wash it also with sour water, and a <s>druti</s> (liquefied essence) born from the gems is produced.

children.text: varṇena sā ratnanibhā ca kāntyā laghvī bhaveddehakarī ca samyak
children.translated_text: In color and brilliance it resembles the gem; it should be light and properly capable of forming the body.

children.text: lohasya vedhaṃ prakaroti samyak sūtena samyaṅmilanaṃ prayāti ||
children.translated_text: It properly effects penetration of metal and comes into proper union with <s>sūta</s> (mercury).

children.text: tadā bhaveyuḥ khalu siddhatā yadā hiṃgvādivargeṇa milanti samyak
children.translated_text: Then accomplishment truly exists when they combine properly with the group beginning with <s>hiṅgu</s>.

children.text: yāmadvayaṃ kāṃsyavimarditā vai cātiprayatnena tu vaidyavaryaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are to be rubbed on bronze for two <s>yāmas</s> with very great care by the best physicians.

children.text: kasyāpi nuḥ sidhyati vai drutiśca yadā prasannaḥ khalu pārvatīśaḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>druti</s> succeeds for someone only when <s>Pārvatīśa</s> is truly gracious.

children.text: na syādyāvad bhairavasya prasādastāvatsūte bandhanaṃ durlabhaṃ hi
children.translated_text: So long as <s>Bhairava</s>'s favor is absent, the binding of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is indeed difficult.

children.text: tāsāṃ madhye durlabhābhradrutiśca svalpaṃ bhāgyaṃ bhūridaurbhāgyabhājām ||
children.translated_text: Among these, the liquefaction of mica is difficult to obtain; the share of luck is small for those who possess great misfortune.
The qualities of the gems have been stated in order, together with their purification and calcination,
and also the extraction of <s>sattva</s> (essence) from them, and then the proper production of liquefaction.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ hi parīkṣaṇaṃ ca drutayaḥ sammelanaṃ vai rase
children.translated_text: The testing of all of them, the liquefactions, and the combining with <s>rasa</s> (mercury),

children.text: adhyāye'tra nidarśitāni sakalānyevaṃ hi karmāṇi vai ||
children.translated_text: all these operations have thus been shown in this chapter.

children.text: bhavati gadagaṇānāṃ nāśanaṃ yena sadyo vividharasavidhānaṃ kathyate 'traiva samyak
children.translated_text: Here, indeed, the varied formulation of <s>rasas</s> is properly taught, by which groups of diseases are at once destroyed.

children.text: rasanigamasudhābdhau mathyamāne mayaiva gaṇitarasaśatānāṃ saṃgrahaḥ procyate vai ||
children.translated_text: As the nectar-ocean of the <s>rasa</s> tradition is churned by me, a collection of hundreds of counted <s>rasa</s> preparations is now declared.

children.text: sukhaṇḍitaṃ hāriṇajaṃ viṣāṇaṃ rasena pācyaṃ jalajaṃbukasya
children.translated_text: A deer-born horn, well cut up, should be cooked with the juice of <s>jalajambuka</s>.

children.text: ruddhvātha bhāṇḍe vipacecca cullyāṃ yāmadvayaṃ śītagataṃ samuddharet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after sealing it in a vessel, one should cook it on the hearth for two <s>yāmas</s>; when it has cooled, one should take it out.

children.text: tato'ṣṭabhāgaṃ trikaṭuṃ niyojya niṣkapramāṇaṃ ca bhajetprabhāte
children.translated_text: After that one should add one-eighth part <s>trikaṭu</s> and take a <s>niṣka</s> measure in the morning.

children.text: taṃ nāgavallīdalajena sārdhaṃ nihanti vātodbhavakaṃ jvaraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Together with juice from leaves of <s>nāgavallī</s>, it destroys fever arising from <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> (mercury), <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), poison, <s>kāravī</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and seeds of <s>dantī</s> should be increased successively in parts.
When they have been ground with the juices of ten lemons, pills should be made, each weighing half a <s>raktikā</s>.

children.text: bhakṣitā jvaragaṇān nihantyayaṃ recano jvaraharo'yam aṅkuśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When eaten, this destroys groups of fevers; this purgative fever-remover is the preparation called <s>Aṅkuśa</s>.

children.text: eka eva kathitastu so'malaḥ svedito'pi saha cūrṇajalena
children.translated_text: That same spotless preparation has been described; even when steamed together with powdered water,
if eaten beforehand in a <s>raktikā</s> measure, it removes every cold fever.
One should take well-purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury), <s>rasaka</s>, <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), <s>tālaka</s>, with <s>tuttha</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
and grind them all together in equal quantity for a day with juices produced from <s>kāravella</s>.
One should smear it inside a sun-vessel to a measure of half a finger's breadth,
seal the mouth of the copper vessel, and cook it in the middle of a sand apparatus.

children.text: dhānyakānyupari muñcitāni cet saṃsphuṭanti yadi śuddhamucyate
children.translated_text: If grains placed above it burst open, it is said to be purified.
A very pleasing <s>Jvarārika</s> is produced; when administered, it removes groups of fevers.
If a <s>māṣa</s> measure is eaten regularly with an equal amount of pungents and with pieces of leaf,
it destroys fevers arising from irregularity, just as sunrise destroys darkness.
All of <s>tālaka</s>, copper, <s>rasa</s> (mercury), <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), and <s>tuttha</s>, weighed to a <s>śāṇa</s> measure,
together with beautiful <s>manaḥśilā</s> of a <s>niṣka</s> measure, should be thoroughly ground with water of <s>triphala</s>.

children.text: golamasya ca vidhāya saṃpuṭe pācayecca puṭapākayogataḥ
children.translated_text: After making this into a ball, one should cook it in a sealed capsule by the method of <s>puṭapāka</s>.
Then one should impregnate it seven times with the latex of <s>arka</s> and <s>vajrī</s>, and with decoctions of <s>dantikā</s>.
When this <s>rasa</s>, in a <s>māṣa</s> measure, is eaten together with pepper of a <s>śāṇa</s> measure,
mixed with one and a half <s>niṣkas</s> of jaggery and accompanied by the juices of twelve leaves,

children.text: śītapūrvamatha dāhapūrvakaṃ dvyāhikaṃ ca sakalān jvarānapi
children.translated_text: it destroys all fevers, whether preceded by chills, preceded by burning, or occurring every two days.
This <s>Taruṇajvarārika</s> pacifies all <s>doṣas</s> and brings ease.

children.text: bhāgaikaḥ syātpāradaḥ śodhitaśca elīyaḥ syātpippalī śreyasī ca
children.translated_text: There should be one part of purified <s>pārada</s> (mercury), and also <s>elī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>śreyasī</s>.

children.text: ākallo vai gaṃdhakaḥ sārṣapeṇa tailenātho śodhito buddhimadbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: There should also be <s>ākalla</s> and <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), purified by the learned with mustard oil.
Having made four parts of the fruits of <s>indravallī</s> into powder, one should dry it in the heat of the sun.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ caitad bhāvayettadrasena māṣaistulyāṃ kārayettadvaṭīṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: One should impregnate this powder with its own juice and make pills equal to <s>māṣas</s>.

children.text: dattvā caikāṃ jātasadyojvarāya chinnāṅgāyāḥ kvāthapānaṃ vidheyam
children.translated_text: After giving one pill to a patient with newly arisen acute fever, a drink of <s>chinnāṅgā</s> decoction should be prescribed.

children.text: doṣodbhūtaṃ sannipātodbhavāṃ ca jūrtiṃ samyaṅ nāśayatyāśu tīvrām ||
children.translated_text: It quickly and properly destroys intense fever arising from the <s>doṣas</s> and also that arising from their combined derangement.

children.text: śuddhaḥ sūto gaṃdhako vatsanābhaḥ pratyekaṃ vai śāṇamātrā vidheyā
children.translated_text: Purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), and <s>vatsanābha</s> should each be assigned a <s>śāṇa</s> measure.

children.text: dhūrtādbījaṃ kārayedvai triśaṇaṃ sarvebhyo vai dvaiguṇā hemadugdhā ||
children.translated_text: One should make seed of <s>dhūrtā</s> three <s>śāṇas</s>, and <s>hemadugdhā</s> twice as much as all the others.

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ cūrṇaṃ kārayettatprayatnāddeyaṃ guṃjāyugmamānaṃ ca samyak
children.translated_text: One should carefully make that into a fine powder, and a proper dose of two <s>guñjās</s> should be given.
The fever patient should eat it moist, with a suitable after-drink; it at once destroys fever arising from all <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: sūtaṃ gaṃdhaṃ hiṅgulaṃ daṃtibījaṃ bhāgairvṛddhaṃ kārayecca krameṇa
children.translated_text: One should prepare <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), <s>hiṅgula</s>, and seed of <s>dantī</s> in successively increasing parts.
After making a powder and grinding it with water of <s>dantī</s>, if it is eaten in a <s>guñjā</s> measure, it is an enemy of fever.

children.text: ekaṃ bhāgaṃ vatsanābhaṃ ca kuryāddvau bhāgau ceṭ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ daṃtibījam
children.translated_text: One should make one part of <s>vatsanābha</s>, two parts of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and seed of <s>dantī</s>,

children.text: trīṇyevaite hiṃgulasyāpi turyaḥ sadyo jūrtiṃ nāśayatyeva sūryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and three parts of <s>hiṅgula</s> as the fourth ingredient; like the sun, it immediately destroys fever.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ bhāgamekaṃ tu tālād dvau bhāgau cedvedasaṃkhyāḥ śilāyāḥ
children.translated_text: One should prepare one part of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury), two parts of <s>tālaka</s>, four parts of <s>śilā</s>,

children.text: tāmrasyaivaṃ bhāgayugmaṃ prakuryādbhallātaṃ vā vedabhāgaṃ tathaiva ||
children.translated_text: two parts of copper in the same way, or four parts of <s>bhallāta</s> likewise.

children.text: arkakṣīrairbhāvayecca trivāraṃ kṛtvā cūrṇaṃ kārayedgolakaṃ tat
children.translated_text: One should impregnate it three times with the latex of <s>arka</s>; after making a powder, one should form that into a ball.

children.text: sthālīmadhye sthāpitaṃ tacca golaṃ dattvā mudrāṃ bhasmanā saiṃdhavena ||
children.translated_text: That ball should be placed inside a pot and sealed with ash and rock salt.
In this way one should close off the smoke and give it steaming over a gentle fire with <s>śāṇas</s>.

children.text: paścāttoyenaiva bhāvyaṃ ca cūrṇaṃ golaṃ kṛtvā maṃdavahnau vipācya ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards the powder should be impregnated with water, made into a ball, and cooked over a gentle fire.

children.text: paścādenaṃ bhakṣayedvai rasendraṃ vallaṃ caikaṃ śarkarācūrṇamiśram ||
children.translated_text: Then one should consume this <s>rasendra</s> in a dose of one <s>valla</s>, mixed with powdered sugar.
Likewise, with <s>kṛṣṇamākṣika</s>, this destroys fever arising from all <s>doṣas</s>.
Now I shall describe <s>rasa</s> preparations that pacify diarrhea,
which, when eaten regularly, produce reliable effect immediately.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ vai samāṃśaṃ citronmattair mardayedvāsaraikam
children.translated_text: Purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), in equal parts, should be triturated for one day with the juices of <s>citra</s> and <s>unmatta</s>.

children.text: cūrṇairetaiḥ śaṃkhamāpūritaṃ vai bhāṇḍe sthāpyaṃ mudritavyaṃ prayatnāt ||
children.translated_text: A conch should be filled with these powders, placed in a vessel, and sealed carefully.

children.text: tasyādhastād aṣṭayāmaṃ prakuryādvahniṃ śīte karṣamātraṃ viṣaṃ hi
children.translated_text: Under it one should maintain a fire for eight <s>yāmas</s>; when it is cold, one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>viṣa</s> should be added.

children.text: dattvā gharme trīṇi cātho puṭāni dadyāttadvat kanyakāyā rasena ||
children.translated_text: Then, under heat, one should give it three <s>puṭas</s> in the same way with the juice of <s>kanyakā</s>.

children.text: vallaṃ yojyaṃ jīrakeṇātha bhṛṃgyā kṣaudrairyuktaṃ bhakṣitaṃ saṃgrahaṇyām
children.translated_text: A <s>valla</s>-dose, joined with <s>jīraka</s> and <s>bhṛṅgī</s> and mixed with honey, is to be eaten for <s>saṃgrahaṇī</s>.

children.text: śvāse śūle cānile śleṣmaje vā kāse'rśaḥsu viḍgrahe cātisāre ||
children.translated_text: It is used for dyspnea, colic, disorders of <s>anila</s> (wind), or disorders arising from <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), for cough, piles, fecal obstruction, and diarrhea.

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ vai hiṃgulaṃ vatsanābhaṃ mārīcaṃ vai hemabījena yuktam
children.translated_text: <s>Saubhāgya</s>, <s>hiṅgula</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, and <s>mārīca</s>, together with <s>hemabīja</s>,

children.text: kṛtvā cūrṇaṃ sarvametatsamāṃśaṃ jambīrais tanmarditaṃ yāmayugmam
children.translated_text: all this should be powdered in equal parts and triturated with <s>jambīra</s> juice for two <s>yāmas</s>.

children.text: guṃjāmātrā nirmitā bhakṣitā hi guṭyo hanyuḥ sannipātātisārān ||
children.translated_text: Pills made to the size of a <s>guñjā</s> and eaten destroy diarrheas caused by combined <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: jātīpattrī devapuṣpaṃ ca śuṇṭhī kaṅkollaṃ cec caṃdanaṃ kuṃkumaṃ ca
children.translated_text: <s>Jātīpattrī</s>, <s>devapuṣpa</s>, <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>kaṅkolla</s>, sandalwood, and saffron,

children.text: kṛṣṇāyuktaṃ śuddhamākallakaṃ syāt sarvāṇyevaṃ cūrṇayedvai samāni ||
children.translated_text: with <s>kṛṣṇā</s> and purified <s>mākallaka</s>: all these should likewise be powdered in equal amounts.

children.text: sūtasyaivaṃ bhasma miśraṃ prakuryād bhāgaṃ caikaṃ miśrayennāgaphenam
children.translated_text: One should mix this with one part of the ash of <s>sūta</s> and combine it with <s>nāgaphena</s>.

children.text: khalve sarvaṃ marditaṃ caikayāmaṃ kāryā golī vallamātrā jalena ||
children.translated_text: All of it is ground in a mortar for one <s>yāma</s>; pills of a <s>valla</s> measure are to be made with water.
One should eat it at night and drink rice-water; it destroys every diarrhea caused by all <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: mārīcaṃ ceṭ ṭaṃkaṇaṃ hiṃgulaṃ ca gaṃdhāśmā vai pippalī vatsanābham
children.translated_text: <s>Mārīca</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>hiṅgula</s>, <s>gandhāśman</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>vatsanābha</s>,

children.text: dhūrtasyaivaṃ bījakānīha śuddhānyevaṃ kṛtvā tacca cūrṇaṃ vidheyam ||
children.translated_text: and the purified seeds of <s>dhūrta</s> here: after preparing them thus, that powder should be made.

children.text: prātaḥ sāyaṃ bhakṣitaṃ vallamātraṃ jūrtiṃ raktaṃ nāśayeccātisāram
children.translated_text: Taken morning and evening in a <s>valla</s>-dose, it removes <s>jūrti</s> and bloody diarrhea.

children.text: dadhyannaṃ vā bhojayettakrayuktaṃ hanyād evaṃ cāgnimāndyaṃ sutīvram ||
children.translated_text: One should feed the patient curd-rice or food mixed with buttermilk; in this way it destroys very severe weakness of digestion.
Now the names of the divine herbs are stated by me here.
They number sixty-four, are auspicious, and properly produce the binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
<s>Somavallī</s>, likewise <s>sobhavṛkṣa</s>, and the creeper <s>somakalā</s>;
<s>Bhūpadminī</s>, <s>gonasā</s>, <s>uccaṭā</s>, and the creeper <s>īśvarī</s>;
<s>Bhūtakeśī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇalatā</s>, <s>laśunī</s>, and <s>rudantikā</s>;

children.text: vārāhī saptapattrā ca nāginī sarpiṇī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>saptapattrā</s>, <s>nāginī</s>, and likewise <s>sarpiṇī</s>;

children.text: chattriṇī caiva gośṛṃgī jyotirnāmnī ca raktikā
children.translated_text: <s>Chattriṇī</s>, <s>gośṛṅgī</s>, one named <s>jyotis</s>, and <s>raktikā</s>;
<s>Pattravallī</s>, <s>kākinī</s>, <s>cāṇḍālī</s>, and <s>tāmravallikā</s>;
<s>Pītavallī</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, the great herb <s>amarī</s> creeper,
<s>Navanītā</s>, <s>rudravallī</s>, <s>lambinī</s>, and <s>bhūmitumbikā</s>;

children.text: gāndharvī vyāghrapādī ca gomārī ca triśūlinī
children.translated_text: <s>Gāndharvī</s>, <s>vyāghrapādī</s>, <s>gomārī</s>, and <s>triśūlinī</s>;
<s>Tridaṇḍī</s>, <s>karasī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgavallī</s>, and likewise <s>camarikā</s>;
the creeper <s>karavallī</s>, and <s>vajrāṅgī</s> and <s>ciravallī</s> too;
<s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>bilvinī</s>, and <s>bhūtaśocanī</s> are also named;

children.text: mārkaṇḍī ca karīrī ca hyakṣarā kuṭajā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Mārkaṇḍī</s>, <s>karīrī</s>, <s>akṣarā</s>, and likewise <s>kuṭajā</s>;
<s>Mūlakandā</s>, <s>ambuvallī</s>, and <s>munivallī</s> are named;
<s>Ghṛtagandhā</s>, <s>nimbuvallī</s>, <s>tilakandā</s>, and <s>atasītalā</s>;
<s>Bodhavallī</s>, <s>sattvagandhā</s>, <s>kūrmavallī</s>, and <s>mādhavī</s>;
<s>Viśālā</s>, <s>mahānāgī</s>, <s>maṇḍūkī</s>, and <s>kṣīragandhikā</s>;
Thus sixty-four powerful divine herbs have been declared.
By the juice of any one of them, <s>sūta</s> (mercury) attains the state of being bound.
<s>Sūta</s> prepared with these removes old age and poverty.
But their identifying marks were stated by <s>Somadeva</s>.
For fear of expanding the book here, they are mentioned only by name.
After this, the mercury-related herbs are expounded according to the path of the śāstra.
<s>Jalotpalā</s>, <s>ciñcikā</s>, and <s>jalāpāmārga</s> with <s>māṃsikā</s>;
<s>Jalakumbhī</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, <s>īśvarī</s>, and <s>aparājitā</s>;

children.text: mālārjunī veṇukā ca śikhipādā ca tiktikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mālārjunī</s>, <s>veṇukā</s>, <s>śikhipādā</s>, and <s>tiktikā</s>;
<s>Kāśmarī</s>, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>samaṅgā</s>, and likewise <s>jālinī</s> are declared;
<s>Tuṣambukā</s>, <s>durgandhā</s>, <s>pāṣāṇī</s>, and <s>śukanāsikā</s>;

children.text: vanamālī ca vārāhī gojihvā musalī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vanamālī</s>, <s>vārāhī</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, and likewise <s>musalī</s>;
<s>Paṭolī</s>, <s>śaṭhikā</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s>, and <s>jalamūlakā</s>;
<s>Rasājamārī</s> is named, along with <s>śiṃśikā</s> and <s>sitagandhikā</s>;

children.text: potakī ca viṣaghnī ca bṛhatī garuḍī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Potakī</s>, <s>viṣaghnī</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, and likewise <s>garuḍī</s>;

children.text: tulasī ca vidārī ca mañjiṣṭhā citrapālikā
children.translated_text: <s>Tulasī</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, and <s>citrapālikā</s>;
<s>Jalapippalikā</s>, <s>bhārṅgī</s>, and the excellent <s>maṇḍūkī</s>;

children.text: candrodakā sārivā ca hariṇī kukkuṭāpi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Candrodakā</s>, <s>sārivā</s>, <s>hariṇī</s>, and also <s>kukkuṭā</s>;
<s>Sarpākṣī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, and the creeper <s>vanakuṣmāṇḍavallikā</s>;
<s>Markasphoṭī</s>, <s>dhanvayāsa</s>, <s>pāgava</s>, and <s>sthalasāriṇī</s>;
<s>Ardhacandrā</s>, <s>hemapuṣpī</s>, <s>mohinī</s>, and <s>vajrakandikā</s>;

children.text: alambuṣā ca halinī rasacitrā ca nandinī
children.translated_text: <s>Alambuṣā</s>, <s>halinī</s>, <s>rasacitrā</s>, and <s>nandinī</s>;

children.text: vṛścikālī guḍūcī ca vāsā śṛṅgī ca kathyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛścikālī</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, and <s>śṛṅgī</s> are named.
Thus sixty-eight powerful <s>rasauṣadhis</s> (mercury-herbs) have been declared.

children.text: sūtasya māraṇe proktā jāraṇe ca niyāmane ||
children.translated_text: They are taught for the calcination of <s>sūta</s>, for its digestion, and for its regulation.
The sixty-eight great herbs are expounded from the science of <s>rasa</s>:
<s>Ṛddhi</s>, <s>śoṣiṇī</s>, <s>adhoguptā</s>, <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, and likewise <s>sārivā</s>;
<s>Jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>tejavatī</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>bākucī</s>, and <s>bimbikā</s>;
<s>Viṣāṇikā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>varṣābhū</s>, and <s>śarapuṣpikā</s>;
<s>Balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>mahābalā</s>;
<s>Dravantī</s>, <s>nīlinī</s>, <s>śatapuṣpā</s>, and <s>prasāraṇī</s>;

children.text: varā śatāvarī cailā hapuṣā sātalā trivṛt
children.translated_text: <s>Varā</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>elā</s>, <s>hapuṣā</s>, <s>sātalā</s>, and <s>trivṛt</s>;
<s>Svarṇakṣīrī</s>, <s>tugā</s>, <s>pṛthvī</s>, <s>viśālā</s>, <s>nalikā</s>, and <s>amalī</s>;
<s>Indravāruṇikā</s>, <s>kākāhvā</s>, <s>sinduvāra</s>, and <s>ajamodikā</s>.
<s>Trāyamāṇā</s>, <s>Āsurī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, and <s>Girikarnikā</s>;
<s>Dhātakī</s>, <s>Kadalī</s>, <s>Dūrvā</s>, <s>Amlikā</s>, and <s>Kāsamardikā</s>;

children.text: jantupādī ca nirguṇḍī drākṣā nīlotpalaṃ śamī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jantupādī</s>, <s>Nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>Drākṣā</s>, <s>Nīlotpala</s>, and <s>Śamī</s>;

children.text: nālikerī ca kharjūrī phalguḥ śiṃśī ca mallikā
children.translated_text: <s>Nālikerī</s>, <s>Kharjūrī</s>, <s>Phalgu</s>, <s>Śiṃśī</s>, and <s>Mallikā</s>;

children.text: vārṣikī śālmalī jātī grīṣmavarṣā tu yūthikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vārṣikī</s>, <s>Śālmalī</s>, <s>Jātī</s>, <s>Grīṣmavarṣā</s>, and <s>Yūthikā</s>;
<s>Kekicūḍā</s>, <s>Ajagandhā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, and <s>Taruṇī</s>;
Thus sixty-eight great herbs, possessed of great power, have been stated.
Now I shall describe the perfected herbs that are especially effective for <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
<s>Devīlatā</s>, <s>Kālavarṇī</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Āsurī</s>, and <s>Siṃhikā</s>;
<s>Pālāśatilakā</s>, <s>Kṣetrī</s>, <s>Saṃvīrā</s>, and <s>Tāmravallikā</s>;

children.text: nāhī kanyā tathā somarājikā ca ṭuṭumbhaṭī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāhī</s>, <s>Kanyā</s>, as well as <s>Somarājikā</s> and <s>Ṭuṭumbhaṭī</s>;
<s>Kuberākṣī</s>, <s>Gṛdhranakhī</s>, <s>Parpaṭī</s>, and <s>Chidralambikā</s>;
<s>Kṣutkārī</s>, <s>Dugdhikā</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>Gaṅgeṭī</s>, and <s>Śarapuṅkhikā</s>;
<s>Aṣṭāvallī</s>, <s>Rājaśamī</s>, <s>Panasī</s>, and <s>Jayantikā</s>;
<s>Viṣakharparikā</s>, <s>Āvantī</s>, <s>Kākāṇḍolā</s>, and <s>Ambumūlikā</s>;
<s>Siddheśvarī</s>, <s>Haṃsapādī</s>, <s>Khoṭakā</s>, and <s>Śṛṅgarīṭikā</s>;
<s>Adhaḥpuṣpī</s>, the one called <s>Madhurā</s>, <s>Śṛṅkhalā</s>, and <s>Gṛñjanī</s>;
<s>Jārāvalī</s>, <s>Mahārāṣṭrī</s>, and likewise <s>Sahadeveśvarī</s>;
<s>Kāṣṭhagodhāmatī</s>, <s>Devagāndhārī</s>, <s>Rajanī</s>, and <s>Iṅgudī</s>;
<s>Palāśinī</s>, <s>Nākulī</s>, <s>Kāmbojikā</s>, and likewise <s>Aśvinī</s>;
<s>Cakravallī</s>, <s>Sarpadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>Śallakī</s>, and likewise <s>Rohitā</s>;
<s>Tauvarī</s>, <s>Vaṅgajā</s>, <s>Rājapadmā</s>, and <s>Jambīravallikā</s>;
<s>Gajapippalikā</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgavallī</s>, and also <s>Arkavallikā</s>;
<s>Jantukārī</s>, <s>Śigruvallī</s>, <s>Karavīrā</s>, and <s>Śivāṭikā</s>;
<s>Nārācī</s>, <s>Kāñcanī</s>, and <s>Ajagandhā</s>, which grant success with <s>Sūtendra</s> (chief mercury);
Thus sixty-eight perfected herbs, especially effective for <s>rasa</s> (mercury), have been stated.
They accomplish every operation and bestow perfection of the body and of metals.

children.text: atha yantrāṇi vakṣyante pārado yena yantryate
children.translated_text: Now the apparatuses by which <s>pārada</s> (mercury) is controlled will be described.
Therefore the forms of the apparatus are to be shown according to the treatise.
The <s>Dolā</s> apparatus, the <s>Palabhalī</s> apparatus, and the apparatus for upward sublimation,
also the apparatus for downward sublimation and the one for lateral sublimation;
the <s>Ghaṭī</s> apparatus, the <s>Garbha</s> apparatus, the brick apparatus, and the water apparatus;
the mortar apparatus, the one called <s>Ḍamaruka</s>, the one called <s>Cipiṭa</s>, and the one named <s>Tulā</s>;
the salt apparatus, the one termed <s>Koṣṭhikā</s>, and the one termed <s>Antarālika</s>;
the <s>Dhūpa</s> apparatus, the <s>Nābhi</s> apparatus, and likewise the <s>Grasta</s> apparatus;
the <s>Vidyādhara</s>, the <s>Kuṇḍaka</s>, and the one designated <s>Ḍhekī</s>;
the <s>Somānala</s>, the <s>Nigaḍa</s>, the <s>Kiṃnara</s>, and the one named <s>Bhairava</s>;
also the one named <s>Vāluka</s>, the <s>Pātāla</s>, and the one called <s>Bhūdhara</s>;
the <s>Sāraṇa</s> apparatus, the secret apparatus, and the <s>Gandhapiṣṭaka</s> apparatus;
the flask apparatus, the one called <s>Pālikā</s>, and likewise the <s>Dīpikā</s> apparatus;
the pan apparatus, the ash apparatus, and the <s>Dega</s> apparatus are stated.
The <s>Ghāṇikā</s> apparatus is specified, and likewise the one named <s>Haṃsapāka</s>.
Here thirty-nine apparatuses have been named.
Now the crucibles are described in order according to the varieties of clay.
A crucible is said to be <s>Kumudikā</s>, <s>Kovikā</s>, and <s>Karahāṭikā</s>;
the same is called <s>Pātinī</s> and is known as <s>Vahnimitrā</s>.
Clay from an anthill, combined with husk-ash and with <s>biḍa</s>,

children.text: tayā yā racitā mūṣā yogamūṣeti kathyate
children.translated_text: when a crucible is made from it, is called a <s>Yoga-mūṣā</s> (compound crucible).
Together with <s>gāra</s>, <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s>, hemp fiber, and burnt husks,
clay is kneaded in buffalo's milk for a half-month.
A crucible made from that clay is called a <s>Gāra-mūṣā</s>.
Cloth, charcoal, and husk are in equal amounts, and clay is four times that measure;
an equal amount of <s>bhūnāga</s> clay is kneaded thoroughly with all these.

children.text: kathitā varamūṣā sā yāmaṃ vahniṃ saheta vai ||
children.translated_text: That is called an excellent crucible, and it can withstand fire for one <s>yāma</s>.
The clay mentioned earlier, when impregnated with the liquid of the red group,
and made into a fine crucible from clay mixed with the red group,
is then smeared with <s>turī</s> flowers and <s>kasīsa</s>.
It should be used for heightening color and is called a <s>Varṇa-mūṣā</s> (coloring crucible).
When smeared with the white group, it is known as a <s>Rūpya-mūṣā</s> (silver crucible).

children.text: viḍena racitā yā tu viḍenaiva pralepitā
children.translated_text: The one made with <s>biḍa</s> and smeared with <s>biḍa</s> itself,
for accomplishing the aims of the body and metals, is called a <s>Biḍa-mūṣā</s>.
Mixed with <s>gāra</s>, <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s>, husk, and hemp fiber,
with clay in equal amount, and kneaded for three days with buffalo's milk,

children.text: saṃsthitā pakṣamātraṃ hi paścānmūṣā kṛtā tayā
children.translated_text: it is kept for a half-month; afterward a crucible is made from it.
Then it is smeared with the blood of a bedbug and with juices of <s>Balā</s>.

children.text: caturyāmaṃ dhmāpitā hi dravate naiva vahninā
children.translated_text: When heated with blowing for four <s>yāmas</s>, it does not melt in the fire.
It is called a <s>Vajra-mūṣā</s> (diamond crucible), for the purpose of melting diamond.
In a crucible shaped like a brinjal, one should make a tube ten <s>aṅgulas</s> long,
long like a <s>Dhattūra</s> flower, and should make it very firm.
It should be eight <s>aṅgulas</s> and perforated; this is the <s>Vṛntāka-mūṣā</s> (brinjal-shaped crucible).
With this one extracts the <s>sattva</s> from soft substances such as <s>Kharpara</s>.
A crucible shaped like a cow's udder, sealed over the mouth,

children.text: satvānāṃ drāvaṇe śuddhau mūṣā sā gostanī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: is the <s>Gostanī</s> crucible, used for melting and purifying <s>sattvas</s>.
The <s>Malla-mūṣā</s> is specified as made from the sealed joining of two <s>mallas</s> (crucible-cups),
and is prescribed for steaming <s>Rasaparpaṭikā</s> and similar substances.

children.text: pakvamūṣā kulālabhāṇḍarūpā yā dṛḍhā ca paripācitā
children.translated_text: A baked crucible is one in the form of a potter's vessel, firm and fully fired;
it is called a <s>Pakva-mūṣā</s> (baked crucible) and purifies <s>sattva</s>-bearing substances.
Very thick, very long, and somewhat widened at the mouth,
it is called a <s>Mahā-mūṣā</s> (great crucible) and purifies <s>sattva</s>-bearing substances.
A crucible six <s>aṅgulas</s> high, elongated, four-sided, and shallow
is called the box-shaped crucible in the calcination of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
When a crucible is buried in the ground and covered with sand,

children.text: garbhamūṣā tu sā jñeyā pāradasya nibandhinī ||
children.translated_text: it should be known as the womb-crucible, a confining vessel for <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
The crucible that is flattened at the base, round, and eight <s>aṅgulas</s> high
is the crucible called <s>musalā</s>, useful when <s>rasa</s> is bound in a wheel-form.
The furnace called the coal-furnace is of the measure of a royal cubit,
and is described as square and twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> wide.
Then it is encased with clay, and in one wall there is a pit-opening
a <s>vitasti</s> in measure, and a firm doorway one and a half <s>vitastis</s> wide.
In the lower part a threshold should be made for blowing,
and the wall above the upper ledge should be a <s>prādeśa</s> in measure.
A doorway one <s>prādeśa</s> in size should certainly be made above it;

children.text: dvāraṃ ceṣṭikayā ruddhvā saṃdhirodhaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: after closing the doorway with a brick, one should seal the joints.
One should fill it with charcoal and blow the bellows;
charcoal, the material to be blown, should be put in through the upper doorway.
This is the coal-furnace, which extracts the metallic essence of hard substances.
One should dig a firm pit in the ground, twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> in measure;
in its middle there should be a firm round depression four <s>aṅgulas</s> across.
One should set an earthen pan there firmly above the central depression;
having filled the pit with charcoal, one should blow it with a single bellows.
That is the subterranean furnace, for extracting the essence of soft substances.
It is a <s>vitasti</s> in depth and likewise a <s>prādeśa</s> in measure;
on top there is a lid furnished with many holes.
Having filled the pit with charcoal, one should blow it through a bent tube;
the <s>gāra</s>-furnace is taught as a means for extracting essence.
It has a height measured by a <s>vitasti</s> and is four <s>aṅgulas</s> at the bottom;
it is called the transverse-blowing furnace and extracts the essence of soft substances.
One should dig in the ground a square pit two <s>hastas</s> across;
after that one should fill it with a thousand cow-dung cakes.
One should place the medicine in the middle and cover it with forest cow-dung cakes;
then, with five hundred of them, one should properly kindle the fire.
This is stated to be the great <s>puṭa</s>, devised by the author of the treatise.
A square pit of the measure of a royal cubit
is filled in the middle with a thousand forest cow-dung cakes.

children.text: mūṣikāṃ cauṣadhenātha pūritāṃ tāṃ tu mudrayet
children.translated_text: Then one should fill a small crucible with the medicine and seal it;
after placing it in the middle of the pit, one should put in the <s>giriṇḍa</s> cakes.
One should kindle the fire properly below; in this way it becomes a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
In a pit of an <s>aratni</s> in measure, it is called a <s>vārāhapuṭa</s>.
If the square pit measures two <s>vitastis</s>,
one should know it as the <s>kukkuṭa-puṭa</s>, a means for preparing medicines.
With eight cow-dung cakes it is correctly called the <s>kapota-puṭa</s>.
With husks or with cow-dung cakes, for refining calcined <s>rasa</s>,
one measuring two <s>māṇikas</s> of cow-dung is called the <s>govara-puṭa</s>.

children.text: mṛdā bhāṇḍaṃ prapūryaiva madhye dravyaṃ tu vinyaset
children.translated_text: After filling a clay vessel with earth, one should place the material in the middle;
one should kindle fire underneath: this is called the clay-vessel <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: garte tu vālukāpūrṇe madhye dravyaṃ tu vinyaset
children.translated_text: In a pit filled with sand, one should place the material in the middle;
one should carefully make fire above and below.
That is correctly called the sand <s>puṭa</s> by those learned in the treatises.

children.text: mūṣikāṃ bhūmimadhye tu sthāpitāṃ dvyaṃgulād adhaḥ
children.translated_text: A small crucible placed in the middle of the ground, two <s>aṅgulas</s> below,
should be given a <s>puṭa</s> from above; that <s>puṭa</s> is named <s>bhūdhara</s>.
A <s>puṭa</s> with cow-dung cakes or husks, measured by a <s>karṣa</s>,
is there called <s>lāvaka</s> for the preparation of soft substances.
<s>Utpala</s>, <s>piṣṭaka</s>, <s>chāṇa</s>, <s>upala</s>, and <s>gariṇḍaka</s>,
together with <s>chagaṇa</s> and <s>upalasārī</s>, are the nine names for cow-dung cakes.
Now then I shall explain the supreme marvel concerning metals,

children.text: svānubhūtaṃ mayā kiṃcit śrutaṃ vā śāstrataḥ khalu
children.translated_text: something partly experienced by me myself and also heard from the treatise;

children.text: tadahaṃ sampravakṣyāmi yatkṛtvā nā sukhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: I shall explain that by doing which a person becomes happy.

children.text: rasakaṃ daradaṃ tāpyaṃ gaganaṃ kunaṭī samam
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s>, <s>darada</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>gagana</s>, and <s>kunaṭī</s> in equal parts
should be triturated for seven days with the latex of red <s>snuhī</s>.
It should be cooked by means of a water-apparatus for twenty-four <s>yāmas</s>;

children.text: tena vedhyaṃ drutaṃ tāmraṃ tāraṃ vā nāgameva vā ||
children.translated_text: with it, molten copper, silver, or lead should be pierced.
That paste becomes a thousandfold-piercing agent; there is no doubt about this.
Then one part <s>sūta</s> (mercury), triturated with <s>vajravallī</s>,
in a mortar with the juice of <s>trinemi</s>, combined with five parts,
and with <s>vetrayaṣṭi</s> and <s>rāgiṇī</s>, becomes a yellow paste.
A sixteenth part should be added to properly purified molten copper;
it becomes excellent pure gold of fourteen <s>varṇas</s> (color-grade).
<s>Suvarṇamākṣika</s> should be steamed in sour gruel for three days;
one should triturate it for seven days with the juice of <s>carmaraṅgī</s>;
it should then be washed with water until it becomes like gold.
<s>Darada</s> from <s>Romadeśa</s> should be steamed with cow urine;
in a swing-apparatus for four <s>yāmas</s>; afterwards it becomes very pure.
<s>Manaḥśilā</s>, lotus-like, red, and very beautiful,
when steamed in a <s>dolā</s> with the juice of <s>munipuṣpa</s>,
is purified after half a <s>yāma</s>; it should be employed in all operations.
<s>Navasāra</s> and likewise <s>sūta</s>, when purified, are indeed able to withstand fire.
One should grind all of these, in equal parts, with juices of <s>nimbuka</s> (lemon),
and likewise with the juice of <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) and the fresh juice of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe).
This should be rubbed thoroughly in the heat of the sun and cooked in a <s>jalayantra</s> (water apparatus),
over a fierce fire for three days; then one should take it down.
It transmutes purified <s>tāra</s> (silver) with a hundredth part, and <s>hema</s> (gold) is produced.

children.text: jalabhedo yadā na syānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: When there is no failure in the water-test, no further doubt is to be entertained here.

children.text: śilayā māritaṃ nāgaṃ kumāryāḥ svarasena ca
children.translated_text: Lead that has been killed with <s>śilā</s> and with the fresh juice of <s>kumārī</s>,
through the application of twelve <s>puṭas</s> (sealed heatings), becomes <s>nāgabhasma</s> (lead ash).
In this way one should perform one hundred <s>puṭas</s> in a small earthen dish,
and should impregnate it for seven days with the fresh juice of <s>kumārī</s> alone.
As before, heating by <s>puṭa</s> should be carried out, likewise to the number of one hundred.
If ash of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>śilā</s>, and <s>tāla</s> are equal to the lead ash,
one should give the <s>puṭa</s> called <s>vārāha</s> with thirty forest cow-dung cakes.
By this method one should properly cause one hundred such heatings to be given.
When, in this way, three hundred and twelve <s>puṭas</s> have been performed,
afterwards it should remain in a strong glass bottle for thirty-two <s>yāmas</s>.
One should apply a sand-bath fire, and when it has cooled of itself, remove it.
The ash from the bottom should be taken and used to pierce copper and silver.
By means of it pure gold is produced; no doubt is to be entertained here.
This is a formula with directly observed proof, and it has been taught without uncertainty.
In cow urine, sour gruel, and also horse-gram liquid, for three days,
one should steam <s>tāpyaka</s>; afterwards one should grind it in an iron vessel.
Grinding it with a heated mortar, one should moisten it with lemon liquids.
Afterwards one should especially add rock salt as a fourth part.
One should make one part <s>tāpyaka</s> and three parts from <s>sūta</s> (mercury),
grind them with lemon-water, and filter them through a clean cloth.

children.text: vastre lagnā tu yā piṣṭī grāhayettāṃ bhiṣagvaraḥ
children.translated_text: The paste that adheres to the cloth should be collected by the excellent physician.
When this has been done two or three times, the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) absorbs the essence of <s>tāpya</s>.
A ball should be made from the paste, and the wise man should blow it in a crucible.
The excellent essence of <s>tāpya</s>, resembling an <s>indragopa</s> insect, should be taken.
Even in a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of gold of deficient color, a <s>valla</s>-measure should be used,

children.text: tutthakaṃ vallamātraṃ ca dattvā hema pragālayet ||
children.translated_text: and, after adding a <s>valla</s>-measure of <s>tutthaka</s>, one should melt the gold.
Foils of that gold should then be made, and they should be smeared in this way.
One should grind <s>tutthaka</s> also with the juice of <s>bījapūra</s> (citron).
Mixing it equally with <s>gairika</s> (red ochre), one should smear the gold foils.
Then one should heat them gently by <s>puṭa</s>, carefully, two or three times.

children.text: kuṅkumābhaṃ suvarṇaṃ hi jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The gold indeed becomes saffron-colored; there is no doubt here.

children.text: vārtikendrāḥ kurudhvaṃ hi satyaṃ guruvaco yathā ||
children.translated_text: O foremost practitioners, do this, for the teacher's word is true.

children.text: dvau varṇau vardhate samyak nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: It properly increases by two grades of color; no further doubt is to be entertained.

children.text: śuddhaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyacūrṇena tulyaṃ drāvyaṃ paścāḍ ḍhālayellākuce hi
children.translated_text: Pure copper, equal in amount to powdered <s>tāpya</s>, should be melted, and afterwards one should pour it into <s>lākuca</s>.
Having made a powder from sulfur and the remaining <s>tāpya</s>-copper, one should add a <s>valla</s> to deficient gold.

children.text: varṇotkarṣo jāyate tena samyak satyaṃ proktaṃ nandinā kautukāya ||
children.translated_text: By that a proper improvement of color is produced; this truth was spoken by <s>Nandin</s> for delight.

children.text: tāpyaṃ nāgaṃ gandhakaṃ sūtarājo hiṃgūlaṃ vai hema śuddhaṃ śilā ca
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s>, <s>nāga</s> (lead), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), the king <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>hiṅgūla</s>, pure gold, and <s>śilā</s>,

children.text: cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā nikṣipet kācakūpyām āpūryānte svai rasaiḥ śākajairvā ||
children.translated_text: should be powdered and placed in a glass bottle, filling it at the end with their own juices or with plant juices.

children.text: agniṃ dadyāllāvakākhye puṭe ca śuddhaḥ kalko jāyate ṣaṣṭisaṃkhyaiḥ
children.translated_text: One should apply fire in the <s>puṭa</s> called <s>lāvaka</s>; by sixty such heatings a purified paste is produced.

children.text: śuddhaṃ tāraṃ vedhitaṃ vallakena gadyāṇaṃ vai jāyate śuddhahema ||
children.translated_text: Pure silver, pierced with a <s>valla</s>, indeed becomes a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of pure gold.

children.text: ahiripum ahitulyaṃ sāritaṃ sūtarāje balivasagiricūrṇaiḥ kāntapātre sudagdham
children.translated_text: <s>Ahiripu</s>, equal to <s>ahi</s>, is made to enter the king <s>sūta</s> and is well burned in a magnetic vessel with powders of <s>bali</s>, <s>vasa</s>, and <s>giri</s>.
Bound with well-prepared portions of <s>phaṇin</s> and with gold in its core, the serpent-conquering <s>rasendra</s> pierces with a hundred-thousandfold transmuting power.

children.text: dvau bhāgau śuddhatāmrasya dvau bhāgau śuddhahemajau
children.translated_text: One should make two parts of purified copper and two parts produced from purified gold,
and exactly four parts of purified <s>tāra</s> (silver).
Eight parts of <s>rasaka</s> should be carefully prepared.
Placed in a closed crucible, blown, and melted, it becomes gold.
As the elders who know the tradition teach, when it is cooked in a smaller <s>puṭa</s>,
silver, bound with threefold powder, comes to the state of gold.
One <s>pala</s> of <s>pārada</s> (mercury) and half a <s>prastha</s> of purified <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur),
with the juice of <s>kiṃśuka</s> leaves or with juices produced from its flowers,
should indeed be ground in the heat of the sun for a period of six months.
Silver is pierced by a sixteenth part; there is no doubt here.
It becomes gold of sevenfold color, fit for sale in the market.

children.text: pāradaṃ gaṃdhakaṃ śulvaṃ mākṣikaṃ tutthakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Pārada</s> (mercury), <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), copper, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>tutthaka</s>,
<s>rasaka</s>, <s>darada</s>, golden <s>gairika</s>, and <s>navasādara</s>,
as well as <s>sūrakṣāra</s> and <s>śilā</s>, should be ground in equal parts.
Except that <s>rasaka</s> is half that amount, one should seal it in a vajra-crucible.

children.text: yathā dhūmo na nirgacchettathā mudrāṃ pradāpayet
children.translated_text: One should apply the seal so that smoke does not escape.

children.text: tolamekaṃ suvarṇaṃ hi jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One <s>tola</s> of gold is indeed produced; there is no doubt here.
The physician should have it blown continuously for only four <s>ghaṭikās</s>.
For a ring of one <s>gadyāṇa</s> of gold whose color is slight,
<s>mākṣika</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, <s>gairika</s>, and <s>navasādara</s>,
together with <s>sūrakṣāra</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
should each be made two <s>vallas</s>, along with blossoms of <s>kāsamarda</s>.
Grinding them also with a woman's milk, one should smear the ring with that mixture.
It is accompanied by <s>sūrakṣāra</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
One part of <s>Saiṃdhava</s> rock salt and two parts of brick powder
should be put inside a <s>Sthālikā</s> apparatus, setting the ring in the middle.
One should apply fire carefully for three <s>yāmas</s>.

children.text: svāṃgaśītaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā mudrikāṃ tāṃ samuddharet
children.translated_text: Then, after it has cooled by itself, one should take out that ring.
The four color-grades increase through rubbing; there is no doubt about this.
Copper that has been drawn from <s>ghoṣa</s> and combined with silver,
and powder of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> mixed with <s>darada</s>, is ground with the juice of <s>Kanyā</s>.
Afterward small pills are to be made, each the size of an <s>āḍhakī</s> seed.

children.text: vāpitā drāvite dravye sarvaṃ tāmraṃ tu saṃkṣipet ||
children.translated_text: When they are cast into the molten metal, they reduce all the copper.
After removing the silver-like material, one should melt it with an equal amount of gold.
It becomes ten-color gold; this has been stated as true.

children.text: tāmre saptaguṇaṃ nāgaṃ vāhitaṃ punareva hi
children.translated_text: Lead, seven times the amount, is again made to combine with copper;

children.text: tena tāmreṇa rasakaṃ saptavāraṃ ca vāhayet ||
children.translated_text: then with that copper one should make <s>rasaka</s> combine seven times.

children.text: svarṇavarṇaṃ hi tattāmraṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That copper becomes gold-colored; there is no doubt about this.
One should melt excellent gold in a crucible made of <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s>;
joined with <s>tāpya-sattva</s>, repeatedly, a hundred times,
the gold becomes like a hibiscus flower; there is no doubt about this.
Into one <s>gadyāṇa</s> of ten-color gold, put that red gold to the amount of one <s>valla</s>;
two color-grades increase properly, making it fit for sale in the market.
Beautiful <s>puṣpa-kāsīsa</s> should be ground in the juice of <s>Arka</s> leaves;
then one should make a disk of <s>rasaka</s>, one <s>pala</s> in measure.
Coated with the previous paste, it should be dried in the heat of the sun.
With thirty forest cow-dung cakes, twenty such <s>puṭas</s> are to be done properly.
Silver is penetrated with a sixteenth part; there is no doubt.
It becomes equal in color to seven-color gold; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: sūtako dvipalaḥ kāryaḥ tu sumbilaśca catuṣpalaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury should be two <s>palas</s>, and <s>sumbila</s> four <s>palas</s>;
clear, fine <s>sphaṭikī</s> should be four <s>ṭaṅkas</s> in measure.

children.text: vṛścikālīrase ghṛṣṭā dinam ekaṃ tu vārtikaiḥ
children.translated_text: Ground for one day in the juice of <s>Vṛścikālī</s>, together with <s>vārttikā</s>,
afterward all of it should be dried and placed in a <s>Ḍamaruka</s> apparatus.
First one should place red ocher, and chalk likewise above it;
making a small pit in the middle of that, one should put <s>navasādara</s> in the pit,
prepared to the measure of a <s>ṭaṅka</s>, and mercury above it;
above the mercury, indeed, the essence mentioned before, in the measure of a <s>ṭaṅka</s>.
After sealing it and drying it, one should then set it on the stove.
One should apply fire carefully for the measure of sixteen <s>yāmas</s>.
Taking it out after it has cooled by itself, one should collect what has adhered above.
Then, placing it in a mortar, one should grind it thoroughly with <s>Vṛścikālī</s>.
Put all of it in a glass flask and set the flask in a sand apparatus.
One should apply fire for twelve <s>yāmas</s>; when it is cool, one should collect it.
Then one should give a <s>valla</s>-measure of it to one and a half <s>ṭaṅkas</s> of purified copper.
This is a formula verified by experience, stated by <s>Nāthasundara</s>.
Iron powder, one <s>pala</s> in measure, <s>sumala-kṣāra</s>, and mica,
and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, one <s>śāṇa</s> in measure, with castor oil:
one should rub two pellets, make them into a ball, and then blow-heat it.
It should be blown well with the bellows; the iron becomes like mercury.
A wise person should prepare <s>rasaka</s> at three times the amount of that iron.
Then the iron and <s>rasaka</s> are melted in a <s>Vajra</s> crucible.
Removing the remaining iron, one should give a <s>valla</s> of it to copper.
In a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of copper it becomes silver; that silver, in pure silver,
at half the measure becomes pure silver, free of faults.
A lump, a <s>karṣa</s> in measure, of <s>sumala-kṣāraka</s>
is wrapped in human hair and plunged into melted lead.
It is quenched in lemon water twenty-one times.
Into a <s>gadyāṇa</s> of melted copper, five <s>raktikās</s>
of the paste should be carefully added; it becomes silver-colored.

children.text: gadyāṇe caturo vallān rūpyaṃ dattvā pragālayet
children.translated_text: Adding four <s>vallas</s> of silver to a <s>gadyāṇa</s>, one should melt it thoroughly.
Beautiful silver results; this has been stated as true.
One should prepare eight <s>palas</s> of conch-shell called <s>Sumbala</s>;
mixed with the juice of <s>Gojihvā</s>, it should be ground for one day.
With lemon juice, with <s>Dhūrta</s>, and with the juice of <s>Kākamācī</s>,
and with the juice of <s>Gṛñjana</s> as well, it should be ground for one day.
It should be impregnated with the latex of <s>Arka</s> and with castor oil.

children.text: yavamātrāṃ guṭīṃ kṛtvā viśoṣya cātape khare ||
children.translated_text: Making barley-sized pills, one should dry them in the fierce sun.
Putting them in a glass flask, one should seal the mouth of the flask.
Setting it in a sand apparatus, one should cook it for sixteen <s>yāmas</s>.

children.text: svāṃgaśītaṃ samuttārya grāhyaṃ satvaṃ tad ūrdhvagam
children.translated_text: Taking it out after it has cooled by itself, one should collect that upward-moving essence.
The essence is one <s>gadyāṇa</s>; the silver capsule should be of that same measure.
Clean mercury is one <s>gadyāṇa</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is five <s>vallas</s>;
alkaline essence equal to the mercury: all this is ground together.

children.text: svarasena tu ketakyā golaṃ kṛtvā viśoṣitam
children.translated_text: With fresh juice of <s>Ketakī</s> it is made into a ball and dried.

children.text: tārasaṃpuṭamadhye tu dhāritaṃ taṃ ca golakam ||
children.translated_text: That ball is then kept inside the silver capsule.
Afterward, a fine crucible made of copper, eight <s>vallas</s> in measure,
should next be placed inside a sealed pair of earthen saucers.

children.text: dhānyābhraṃ tulyaṃ paṃkena kṛtvā śrāvaṃ tu pūrayet
children.translated_text: Having made <s>dhānyābhra</s> equal in amount with clay, one should fill the saucer.
With one heating called <s>Vārāha</s>, an excellent paste results.

children.text: tāmraṃ dvādaśavallaṃ hi rūpyaṃ valladvayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Copper should be twelve <s>vallas</s>, and silver two <s>vallas</s> likewise.
One should melt all of it together with a <s>valla</s>-measure of purified tin.
The intelligent physician should add a dose measuring four <s>guñjās</s>.

children.text: jāyate pravaraṃ tāraṃ satyam etad udīritam ||
children.translated_text: Excellent <s>tāra</s> (silver) is produced; this has been declared true.
Tin killed with bone and <s>bhakṣa-mala</s>, along with <s>tālaka</s>, mica, poison, mercury, and borax,
well impregnated with the milks of <s>vajrī</s> and <s>bhānu</s>, becomes, O king, an auspicious mass of <s>tāra</s> (silver).

children.text: vaṃgaṃ tālakamabhrakaṃ śaśirasaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ viṣaṃ ṭaṃkaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Tin, <s>tālaka</s>, mica, <s>śaśirasa</s> (moon-fluid), iron, poison, and borax,
when blown three times in a sealed crucible, yield a moon-bright product.
<s>Āra</s> is twelve parts, <s>ravi</s> is eight parts, and the seed alloy is one quarter part;
it is free from all faults such as <s>bhūgaṇḍa</s>; this was taught by <s>Śrīpūjyapāda</s>.

children.text: pāradasya trayo bhāgā bhāgaikaṃ rajatasya hi
children.translated_text: There are three parts of mercury and one part of silver.
One should grind them with lemon juice and carefully make a <s>piṣṭī</s> (amalgam).
One should fix that amalgam with sour gruel for three days.
After that, one should carry the mercury through the tin by the <s>sāraṇa</s> process.
Once the mercury has been so carried, one should process it with <s>tāla-sattva</s> (orpiment extract).

children.text: tena vedhyaṃ drutaṃ tāmraṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśena yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: With that, molten copper should be transmuted carefully at one sixteenth.
Excellent <s>tāra</s> (silver) is produced, resembling the moon and stars.

children.text: sūtakasya trayo bhāgā baṃgaṃ bhāgadvayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: There are three parts of mercury and also two parts of tin.
One should grind them for one day mixed with sour gruel.
Then one should grind it with <s>sumbala</s>, three times the amount of all the ingredients.
It should be impregnated for three days with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> in equal amount.
The pills, each the size of a barley grain and dried by the sun's heat,
should then be placed in a glass flask, and fire should be applied carefully.
It should be cooked in a sand apparatus for as long as sixteen <s>yāmas</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, remove it and collect the upward-risen <s>sattva</s> (extract).
With one sixteenth, one should penetrate copper by <s>kuntavedha</s>.
Excellent <s>tāra</s> (silver) is produced, fit for sale in the market.
Eight <s>palas</s> of <s>tāla</s> and mercury measured at two <s>karṣas</s>
should be ground carefully for one day with lemon juice.
Afterward the intelligent practitioner should indeed grind it with castor oil.
Placed inside a sand apparatus, it should be cooked for sixteen <s>yāmas</s>.
Afterward, extracting the <s>sattva</s>, one should grind it for one day.
With linseed and sesame oil, it should be placed in a glass flask.
It should be cooked in fire as before, and removed when cooled by itself.
By this very method one should perform the procedure again.
The <s>sattva</s> settled at the bottom of the flask should always be taken if it is excellent.
One should perform the transmutation of copper with one sixteenth; there is no doubt.

children.text: pāradaṃ ṭaṃkamānaṃ tu lavaṇaṃ dviguṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Mercury of one <s>ṭaṅka</s> measure, and salt twice as much,
should be rubbed in a mortar until the mercury has disappeared.

children.text: tāmraṃ gadyāṇakaṃ śuddhaṃ baṃgaṃ vallamitaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Take pure copper of one <s>gadyāṇaka</s> and tin measuring one <s>valla</s>.
When the copper is molten, add the salt combined with mercury.
A <s>māṣa</s>-measure is to be added, and silver as a fourth part.
The mercury ground with that silver should be cast into the water apparatus.
From that, thirteenfold silver is produced; there is no doubt.

children.text: tālena nihataṃ baṃgaṃ tadbaṃgena tu rūpyakam
children.translated_text: Tin killed with <s>tāla</s>, and silver with that tin,
should be cooked properly for eight <s>yāmas</s>; in this way a paste is produced.

children.text: vallaṃ gadyāṇake dadyād baṃgaṃ stambhayate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: One should add one <s>valla</s> to a <s>gadyāṇaka</s>; it certainly fixes the tin.
Break <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) into pieces, separately measuring three <s>ṭaṅkas</s>.
It should be steamed with the milk of <s>vajrī</s> in a <s>Dolā</s> apparatus, in wick-like rolls.
An equal amount of silver powder should be applied, likewise with an equal amount of citron water.
It should be cooked mildly with cow-dung cakes for twelve <s>yāmas</s>.
By that, the <s>piṣṭī</s> is fixed; afterward silver dust is prepared separately.
One should add lead equal to the piece of <s>darada</s>.
It should be melted inside a crucible; when cooled, it becomes an ingot.

children.text: bhasma mūṣopari nyasya dhmāpayecca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Placing ash over the crucible, one should heat it with blowing very gradually.
Pure, conch-white silver of a <s>niṣka</s> measure comes out.

children.text: dvipalaṃ śuddhasūtaṃ ca dvipalaṃ rasakasya ca
children.translated_text: Two <s>palas</s> of purified mercury and two <s>palas</s> of <s>rasaka</s>,
two <s>palas</s> of <s>tālaka</s>, and <s>surmila</s> of a twofold measure,
one should put all of it into a flask and close the mouth with copper.
It should be cooked properly in a sand apparatus for twelve <s>yāmas</s>.

children.text: kūpīmukhe tu yallagnaṃ sattvaṃ grāhyaṃ prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> adhering to the mouth of the flask should be carefully collected.
With a sixteenth-part transmutation in copper, one should make excellent silver.

children.text: sūtakaṃ palamekaṃ tu śaṃkhābhaṃ surmilaṃ palam
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of mercury and one <s>pala</s> of conch-colored <s>surmila</s>,
rubbed in castor oil, should be kept in a good <s>kharpara</s> vessel.
It is covered with a copper vessel, sealed, and made very firm.
Then, setting it on the hearth, one should apply fire gradually.

children.text: sārdhaṃ yāmaṃ tataḥ pācyaṃ svāṃgaśītaṃ samuddharet
children.translated_text: Next it should be cooked for one and a half <s>yāmas</s> and removed when cooled by itself.

children.text: tāmrapātre tu yallagnaṃ sarvaṃ sattvaṃ samāharet ||
children.translated_text: All the <s>sattva</s> adhering to the copper vessel should be collected.
Anointed with ghee and combined with borax, it is melted at the mouth of a crucible.

children.text: deyaṃ tadvallamātraṃ hi drute tāmre tu sattvakam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>sattva</s>, exactly one <s>valla</s> in measure, should be added to molten copper.

children.text: śaṃkhābhaṃ jāyate tāraṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: Conch-white <s>tāra</s> (silver) is produced; no doubt need be entertained.

children.text: tālaṃ tāmraṃ rītighoṣaṃ samāṃśaṃ kuryādevaṃ gālitaṃ ḍhālitaṃ hi
children.translated_text: One should make equal parts of <s>tāla</s>, copper, and <s>rītighoṣa</s>; thus melted, it is poured out.

children.text: amle varge saptavāraṃ praḍhālya paścādyojyaṃ tulyabhāge ca rūpye
children.translated_text: After quenching it seven times in the sour group, it should then be joined with an equal part of silver.

children.text: śuddhaṃ rūpyaṃ ṣoḍaśākhyaṃ hi samyak jātaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ nānṛtaṃ satyametat ||
children.translated_text: Pure silver called 'sixteen' is duly produced; this has been seen, it is not false, it is true.
White, purified <s>sauvīraka</s>, cooked with <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s>,
when a <s>valla</s> is cast into clear, excellent mercury, becomes capable of producing silver.
The substance called <s>surmila</s> is sometimes seen resembling pure crystal;
when it has been cooked in an earthen potsherd, mixed with lemon juice,
within a period of two <s>ghaṭikās</s> a purified paste is produced.
In a measure of one sixty-fourth part it should be made to penetrate fine copper;
excellent silver is produced, free from every defect.
A <s>mūṣā</s> (crucible) made of seven metals is filled with alkaline ash,
with alkali from plantain and likewise with that produced from <s>Apāmārga</s>.
After placing <s>pārada</s> (mercury) in the middle, one should again fill it in the same way.

children.text: anena vidhinā pūryā dvitīyā mūṣikā śubhā ||
children.translated_text: By this procedure a second fine small crucible should be filled.
It should be carefully sealed and placed in a <s>puṭa</s> (closed firing) of cow-dung cakes.

children.text: sūtakaṃ bandham āyāti vaṅgābhaṃ tu prajāyate
children.translated_text: The mercury becomes bound, and it comes to have the appearance of tin;
it melts quickly and withstands blows; indeed I myself have seen it so.
Having taken the eyes of fish, one should cook them with milk for a <s>yāma</s>.
Afterward the dark particles should be drawn out, so it is said, and broken up.
Those, together with <s>śāli</s> rice, should be made completely white.
Afterward, taking them in the hand with powdered brick, one should rub them thoroughly.

children.text: mauktikāni hi jāyante kṛtānyevaṃ mayā khalu ||
children.translated_text: Pearls are indeed produced; I myself have made them in this way.
One should make a clean little crucible of crystal-like <s>dahanopala</s> (fire-stone).
Fine pearls, however, should be placed in lemon juice.
In a day and night all of them become like fresh butter.

children.text: tasya paṃkasya guṭikāṃ masṛṇāṃ tu prakārayet ||
children.translated_text: From that paste one should make a smooth pill.
Afterward, inside that little crucible, it is kept in bright heat for two <s>yāmas</s>.
Four bronze vessels are also placed in the four directions.
One should drop all the little pellets upon the central vessel.
The pearl becomes bound, very excellent and endowed with all qualities.

children.text: śuddhaśaṅkhasya cūrṇaṃ hi sūkṣmaṃ kṛtvā prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Having carefully made a fine powder of purified conch shell,
then the wise man should powder half as much <s>darada</s> (cinnabar).
He should triturate it with the milk of a ewe that has just given birth, with that milk itself.
Having formed a wick, the wise man should steam it among cotton seeds.
When it has cooled by itself and been taken out, it becomes beautiful coral.
The dried, husked fruit of <s>Ātmaguptā</s> should be in an eight-<s>pala</s> measure,
and likewise eight <s>palas</s> of black gram, thoroughly ground with water.
Having moistened both properly, one should grind them on a stone slab.
<s>Kuṅkuma</s>, <s>kesara</s>, <s>jātīpatra</s>, and <s>Śatāvarī</s>,
<s>Gokṣura</s> and <s>Ikṣura</s> seeds, clove, black pepper, and <s>Kaṇā</s>,
and <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s> should each separately be prepared in a <s>karṣa</s> measure.
After making them into a fine powder, one should then put them into the paste ground earlier.
Afterward one should make pills of a <s>karṣa</s> each and cook them well.
One should immerse them in three <s>prasthas</s> of ghee so that they are well covered.
In honey equal to the measure of the ghee, one should seal the mouth for three days.
One should eat one pill at daybreak, mixed with honey and ghee.
For five weeks in this way, one should follow a sweet diet.

children.text: dugdhaudanaṃ tathā rātrau kṣāramamlaṃ ca varjayet
children.translated_text: Likewise one should take milk-rice at night and avoid alkaline and sour foods.
A man whose semen is depleted, and likewise an impotent man, may go to a hundred women.
A sonless man obtains a son; even a eunuch becomes virile.
This is a formulation whose efficacy has been seen; this has been declared true.

children.text: śatāvarīṃ kṣīravidārikāṃ ca prasthārdhamānāṃ pṛthageva kuryāt
children.translated_text: One should separately take <s>Śatāvarī</s> and <s>Kṣīravidārī</s>, each in a half-<s>prastha</s> measure.

children.text: rasaṃ tathā śālmalimadhyamūlāt prasthaṃ sitārdhāḍhakamatra deyam ||
children.translated_text: Also a <s>prastha</s> of juice from the middle root of <s>Śālmali</s>; here half an <s>āḍhaka</s> of sugar should be added.

children.text: supācitaṃ vai mṛduvahninā tathā darvīpralepo'pi hi jāyate yathā
children.translated_text: It should be well cooked over a gentle fire until it forms a coating on the ladle.

children.text: tvakpatrakailāḥ saha kesareṇa palapramāṇā hi tato vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then one should add cinnamon bark, leaf, cardamom, and saffron, each in a <s>pala</s> measure.

children.text: lehe suśīte madhu bilvamātraṃ prātaḥ prabhakṣediha karṣamātram ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>leha</s> (electuary) is well cooled, one should eat a <s>karṣa</s> measure in the morning with honey of a <s>bilva</s>-fruit measure.
One <s>pala</s> of <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s> also should be prescribed, and <s>Vārāhīkanda</s> in a <s>pala</s> measure.

children.text: cūrṇīkṛtaṃ gālitameva vastrād bhṛṣṭaṃ tathājyena sitāsametam ||
children.translated_text: It is powdered, strained through a cloth, and fried with ghee, together with sugar.
One should add a <s>pala</s> of clove, black pepper, <s>aguru</s>, and saffron, with ten parts milk.

children.text: lehaṃ sujātaṃ khalu bhakṣayettat karṣapramāṇaṃ nitarāṃ prabhāte
children.translated_text: One should indeed eat that well-prepared <s>leha</s>, a <s>karṣa</s> in measure, very early in the morning.

children.text: kāmasya bodhaṃ kurute hi śīghraṃ nārīṃ ramedvai caṭakāyate'sau ||
children.translated_text: It quickly awakens desire; he indeed enjoys a woman and becomes as vigorous as a sparrow.
<s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>Gokṣura</s>, darbha root, <s>Śṛṅgāṭaka</s>, <s>Nāgabala</s>, and <s>Ātmaguptā</s>,

children.text: saṃcūrṇya sarvaṃ pṛthageva pālikaṃ kṣīreṇa pācyaṃ daśabhāgakena ||
children.translated_text: having powdered them all separately, one <s>pala</s> each, they should be cooked with ten parts milk.

children.text: sitā pradeyā daśapālikātra pākaṃ vidadhyādapi cāgniyogāt
children.translated_text: Ten <s>palas</s> of sugar should be added here, and the cooking should be done by applying fire.
Eaten with honey, within half a <s>yāma</s> it always kindles desire.

children.text: vīryasya vṛddhiṃ jaṭharāgnivṛddhiṃ kāmāgnivṛddhiṃ sahasā karoti ||
children.translated_text: It quickly increases virility, digestive fire, and the fire of passion.
A fresh <s>āḍhaka</s> measure of black gram and of <s>Ātmaguptā</s> seeds,
with <s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>Jīvā</s>, <s>Medā</s>, <s>Vṛddhi</s>, and <s>Śatāvarī</s>,
and also <s>Madhuka</s> and <s>Aśvagandhā</s>, measured by the <s>prasṛta</s>, should be boiled.
In that decoction one should put a <s>prastha</s> of cow's ghee and ten times as much cow's milk,
a <s>prastha</s> of fresh <s>Vidārī</s> juice and a <s>prastha</s> of sugarcane juice.
Having cooked it over a gentle fire, one should store the perfected ghee.
Of sugar, <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, and honey, each separately,
one should add portions of four <s>palas</s> there, and one <s>pala</s> of <s>Pippalī</s>.
Having first licked a <s>pala</s> of this, he should then take food,
if he desires inexhaustible semen and excellent strength of the penis.
<s>Śrīvāsa</s>, <s>mastakī</s>, <s>nāgakeśara</s>, and clove,
<s>kaṅkola</s>, seeds of <s>tulasī</s>, <s>khurāsānī</s>, and <s>ahiphena</s>,
mace, <s>abdhiśoṣa</s>, <s>karabha</s>, aloe-wood, and saffron,
with equal parts of <s>kaṅkola</s>, <s>kaṭugā</s>, <s>kṣīrī</s>, and nutmeg:
after reducing all these to a fine powder, one should put them inside a coconut.

children.text: dugdhamadhye vipācyainaṃ dinānyevaṃ hi pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: It should be cooked in milk in this way for five days.
It is to be taken from the coconut fruit and triturated together with honey.
Pills the size of a <s>kola</s> fruit are to be eaten at the onset of night.
It produces intense semen-retention for as long as four <s>yāmas</s>.
Clove, purified camphor, mace, and also nutmeg,
saffron, <s>svarṇabīja</s>, and the leaf and flower of <s>dhūrta</s>,
the root and bark of <s>abdhiśoṣa</s>: all these should be triturated together.
It should also be purified in cow's milk, and one part should be prepared.
One part should be powder made from <s>bhṛṅgī</s> leaves, and one part red ochre.
A wise physician should give it twenty-one impregnations with poppy water,
and make it into a pill that causes retention of semen.
Nutmeg, <s>arka</s>, <s>karahāṭa</s>, clove, dry ginger, <s>kaṅkola</s>, saffron, <s>kaṇā</s>, and yellow sandalwood:

children.text: etaiḥ samānamahiphenamanena cābhraṃ śvetaṃ nidhāya madhunā vaṭakān vidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: with these, an equal quantity of <s>ahiphena</s> and white <s>abhra</s> should be placed, and pills should be made with honey.

children.text: māṣadvayonmitamamuṃ niśi bhakṣayitvā mṛṣṭaṃ payastadanu māhiṣamāśu pītvā
children.translated_text: After eating this at night in a dose measuring two <s>māṣas</s>, and then quickly drinking sweetened buffalo milk,

children.text: kurvantu kāmukajanāḥ pratiruddhapātāścetāṃsi tāni cakitāni kalāvatīnām ||
children.translated_text: let amorous men, their emission checked, act upon the startled minds of accomplished women.
The potent substance arising from a frog, produced from the shoulder region,
together with camphor and the powder of <s>karahāṭa</s>,
should be well triturated and made into a pill the size of a mung bean.
After rubbing it with saliva from the mouth, one should apply it as an ointment to the penis.
He should retain the drop for half a <s>yāma</s>; this is true, like the word of a teacher.

children.text: postakaṃ palamekaṃ vai śuṃṭhīkarṣaḥ sitā palaikā ca
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of poppy, one <s>karṣa</s> of dry ginger, and one <s>pala</s> of sugar,

children.text: karṣamitā tvakpayasā pītaṃ reto dhruvaṃ dhatte ||
children.translated_text: with cinnamon bark measured by a <s>karṣa</s>, when drunk with milk, certainly holds back semen.
His mind was attached to devotion to <s>Śrī Gaṅgādhara</s>, and he was an ocean of delight in learning;
the son of that wise <s>Padmanābha</s> of the venerable <s>Goḍa</s> lineage,
the good physician and poet <s>Yaśodhara</s>, who brought joy to learned people,

children.text: grantho'yaṃ grathitaḥ karotu satataṃ saukhyaṃ satāṃ mānase ||
children.translated_text: composed this treatise; may it always bring happiness in the minds of the good.
Among lands, <s>Surarāṣṭra</s> is the very best; there too is a fort named <s>Jīrṇa</s>,
adorned with Brahmins devoted to the Veda and the śāstras.
In that place was <s>Śrī Padmanābha</s> himself, delighting in the lotus feet of <s>Śambhu</s>;

children.text: tatputreṇa yaśodhareṇa kavinā graṃthaḥ svayaṃ nirmitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by his son, the poet <s>Yaśodhara</s>, this treatise was himself composed.
For the instruction of the good, for the comfort of the sick, and for the fulfillment of pupils' aims,
for the livelihood of physicians and indeed for the removal of anxiety among the learned,
in venerable old <s>Durgapura</s>, the very skilled son of <s>Śrī Padmanābha</s>,
the venerable <s>Bhaṭṭa Yaśodhara</s>, best of poets, himself composed the treatise.
